body.text: mālinīvijayottaratantram
body.translated_text: <s>Mālinīvijayottaratantram</s> (The Supreme Tantra of the Victory of <s>Mālinī</s>)

body.text: sṛṣṭyadhikāraḥ prathamaḥ
body.translated_text: The First Chapter: On Creation (<s>Sṛṣṭyadhikāra</s>)

body.text:
1.1ab: jayanti jagadānandavipakṣakṣapaṇakṣamāḥ
1.1cd: parameśamukhodbhūtajñānacandramarīcayaḥ
1.2ab: jagadarṇavamagnānāṃ tārakaṃ tārakāntakam
1.2cd: sanatkumārasanakasanātanasanandanāḥ
1.3ab: nāradāgastyasaṃvartavasiṣṭhādyā maharṣayaḥ
1.3cd: jijñāsavaḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ śivaśaktyunmukhīkṛtāḥ
1.4ab: samabhyarcya vidhānena te tam ūcuḥ praharṣitāḥ
1.4cd: bhagavadyogasaṃsiddhikāṅkṣiṇo vayam āgatāḥ
1.5ab: sā ca yogaṃ vinā yasmān na bhavet tam ato vada
1.5cd: ṛṣibhir yogam icchadbhiḥ sa tair evam udāhṛtaḥ
1.6ab: pratyuvāca prahṛṣṭātmā namaskṛtya maheśvaram
1.6cd: śṛṇudhvaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi sarvasiddhiphalapradam
1.7ab: mālinīvijayaṃ tantraṃ parameśamukhodgatam
1.7cd: bhuktimuktipradātāram umeśam amarārcitam
1.8ab: svasthānastham umā devī praṇipatyedam abravīt
1.8cd: siddhayogeśvarītantraṃ navakoṭipravistaram
1.9ab: yat tvayā kathitaṃ pūrvaṃ bhedatrayavisarpitam
1.9cd: mālinīvijaye tantre koṭitritayalakṣite
1.10ab: yogamārgas tvayā proktaḥ suvistīrṇo maheśvara
1.10cd: bhūyas tasyopasaṃhāraḥ prokto dvādaśabhis tathā
1.11ab: sahasraiḥ so 'pi vistīrṇo gṛhyate nālpabuddhibhiḥ
1.11cd: atas tam upasaṃhṛtya samāsād alpadhīhitam
1.12ab: sarvasiddhikaraṃ brūhi prasādāt parameśvara
1.12cd: evam uktas tadā devyā prahasyovāca viśvarāṭ
1.13ab: śṛṇu devi pravakṣyāmi siddhayogeśvarīmatam
1.13cd: yan na kasya cid ākhyātaṃ mālinīvijayottaram
1.14ab: mayāpy etat purā prāptam aghorāt paramātmanaḥ
1.14cd: upādeyaṃ ca heyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ paramārthataḥ
1.15ab: śivaḥ śaktiḥ savidyeśā mantrā mantreśvarāṇavaḥ
1.15cd: upādeyam iti proktam etat ṣaṭkaṃ phalārthinām
1.16ab: malaḥ karma ca māyā ca māyīyam akhilaṃ jagat
1.16cd: sarvaṃ heyam iti proktaṃ vijñeyaṃ vastu niścitam
1.17ab: etaj jñātvā parityajya sarvasiddhiphalaṃ labhet
1.17cd: tatreśaḥ sarvakṛc chāntaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvakṛt prabhuḥ
1.18ab: sakalo niṣkalo 'nantaḥ śaktir apy asya tadvidhā
1.18cd: sa sisṛkṣur jagat sṛṣṭer ādāv eva nijecchayā
1.19ab: vijñānakevalān aṣṭau bodhayām āsa pudgalān
1.19cd: aghoraḥ paramo ghoro ghorarūpas tadānanaḥ
1.20ab: bhīmaś ca bhīṣaṇaś caiva vamanaḥ pivanas tathā
1.20cd: etān aṣṭau sthitidhvaṃsarakṣānugrahakāriṇaḥ
1.21ab: mantramantreśvare śuddhe saṃniyojya tataḥ punaḥ
1.21cd: mantrāṇām asṛjat tadvat saptakoṭīḥ samaṇḍalāḥ
1.22ab: sarve 'py ete mahātmāno mantrāḥ sarvaphalapradāḥ
1.22cd: ātmā caturvidho jñeyas tatra vijñānakevalaḥ
1.23ab: malaikayuktas tatkarmayuktaḥ pralayakevalaḥ
1.23cd: malam ajñānam icchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam
1.24ab: dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇam
1.24cd: īśvarecchāvaśād asya bhogecchā saṃprajāyate
1.25ab: bhogasādhanasaṃsiddhyai bhogecchor asya mantrarāṭ
1.25cd: jagad utpādayām āsa māyām āviśya śaktibhiḥ
1.26ab: sā caikā vyāpinī sūkṣmā niṣkalā jagato nidhiḥ
1.26cd: anādyantāśiveśānī vyayahīnā ca kathyate
1.27ab: asūta sā kalātattvaṃ yad yogād abhavat pumān
1.27cd: jātakartṛtvasāmarthyo vidyārāgau tato 'sṛjat
1.28ab: vidyā vivecayaty asya karma tatkāryakāraṇe
1.28cd: rāgo 'nurañjayaty enaṃ svabhogeṣv aśuciṣv api
1.29ab: niyatir yojayaty enaṃ svake karmaṇi pudgalam
1.29cd: kālo 'pi kalayaty enaṃ tuṭyādibhir avasthitaḥ
1.30ab: tata eva kalātattvād avyaktam asṛjat tataḥ
1.30cd: guṇān aṣṭaguṇāṃ tebhyo dhiyaṃ dhīto 'py ahaṅkṛtim
1.31ab: tat tridhā taijasāt tasmān mano 'kṣeśam ajāyata
1.31cd: vaikārikāt tato 'kṣāṇi tanmātrāṇi tṛtīyakāt
1.32ab: śrotraṃ tvakcakṣuṣī jihvā ghrāṇaṃ buddhīndriyāṇi tu
1.32cd: karmendriyāṇi vākpāṇipāyūpasthāṅghrayaḥ kramāt
1.33ab: kalādikṣitiparyantam etat saṃsāramaṇḍalam
1.33cd: samudrādi jagat kṛtsnaṃ parivartayatīcchayā
1.34ab: bhedaḥ paraḥ kalādīnāṃ bhuvanatvena yaḥ sthitaḥ
1.34cd: asṛjat tam asāv eva bhogināṃ bhogasiddhaye
1.35ab: ity anena kalādyena dharāntena samanvitāḥ
1.35cd: pumāṃsaḥ sakalā jñeyās tadavasthājighāṃsubhiḥ
1.36ab: avasthātritaye 'py asmiṃs tirobhāvanaśīlayā
1.36cd: śivaśaktyā samākrāntāḥ prakurvanti viceṣṭitam
1.37ab: evaṃ jagati sarvatra rudrāṇāṃ yogyatāvaśāt
1.37cd: aṅguṣṭhamātrapūrvāṇāṃ śatam aṣṭādaśottaram
1.38ab: anugṛhya śivaḥ sākṣān mantreśatve niyuktavān
1.38cd: te svagocaram āsādya bhuktimuktiphalārthinām
1.39ab: brahmādīnāṃ prayacchanti svabalena samaṃ phalam
1.39cd: ṛṣibhyas te 'pi te cānu manvantebhyo mahādhipāḥ
1.40ab: heyopādeyavijñānaṃ kathayanti śivoditam
1.40cd: brahmādistambaparyante jātamātre jagaty alam
1.41ab: mantrāṇāṃ koṭayas tisraḥ sārdhāḥ śivaniyojitāḥ
1.41cd: anugṛhyāṇusaṃghātaṃ yātāḥ padam anāmayam
1.42ab: evam asyātmanaḥ kāle kasmiṃś cid yogyatāvaśāt
1.42cd: śaivī saṃbadhyate śaktiḥ śāntā muktiphalapradā
1.43ab: tatsaṃbandhāt tataḥ kaś cit tatkṣaṇād apavṛjyate
1.43cd: ajñānena sahaikatvaṃ kasya cid vinivartate
1.44ab: rudraśaktisamāviṣṭaḥ sa yiyāsuḥ śivecchayā
1.44cd: bhuktimuktiprasiddhyarthaṃ nīyate sadguruṃ prati
1.45ab: tam ārādhya tatas tuṣṭād dīkṣām āsādya śāṅkarīm
1.45cd: tatkṣaṇād vopabhogād vā dehapāte śivaṃ vrajet
1.46ab: yogadīkṣāṃ samāsādya jñātvā yogaṃ samabhyaset
1.46cd: yogasiddhim avāpnoti tadante śāśvataṃ padam
1.47ab: anena kramayogena saṃprāptaḥ paramaṃ padam
1.47cd: na bhūyaḥ paśutām eti śuddhe svātmani tiṣṭhati
1.48ab: ātmā caturvidho hy eṣa punar eṣa caturvidhaḥ
1.48cd: ācāryatvādibhedena śuddhātmā paripaṭhyate
1.49ab: nityāditritayaṃ kuryād guruḥ sādhaka eva ca
1.49cd: nityam eva dvayaṃ cānyo yāvajjīvaṃ śivājñayā
1.50ab: upādeyaṃ ca heyaṃ ca tad etat parikīrtitam
1.50cd: jñātvaitaj jñeyasarvasvaṃ sarvasiddhyaraho bhavet
body.translated_text:
(1.1) Victorious are the rays of the moon of knowledge arisen from the mouth of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord), capable of destroying the adversaries of the world's bliss.
(1.2) [This knowledge is] the deliverer of those submerged in the ocean of the world, and the destroyer of <s>Tāraka</s>. <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Sanaka</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Sanandana</s>,
(1.3) <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Agastya</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, and other great sages, desiring to know the supreme reality (<s>tattva</s>), turned toward <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>,
(1.4) having worshipped [them] according to the prescribed method, they spoke with great delight: 'We have come desiring the attainment of <s>yoga</s> (union) through the Blessed Lord.'
(1.5) 'Since that [attainment] cannot be without <s>yoga</s>, therefore tell us [about] it.' To those sages desiring <s>yoga</s>, he (<s>Sanatkumāra</s>) thus declared:
(1.6) With a joyful heart, having bowed to <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord), he replied: 'Listen, I shall expound [that which] bestows the fruit of all <s>siddhi</s>s (accomplishments),
(1.7) the <s>Mālinīvijaya Tantra</s>, which issued forth from the mouth of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord).
(1.8) Having prostrated before <s>Umeśa</s> (the Lord of <s>Umā</s>), who bestows enjoyment and liberation, who is worshipped by the gods, while he was seated in his own abode, the goddess <s>Umā</s> spoke thus:
(1.9) "The <s>Siddhayogeśvarī Tantra</s>, expanded into nine <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions), which was previously narrated by you, pervading through the three divisions —
(1.10) in the <s>Mālinīvijaya Tantra</s>, characterized by three <s>koṭi</s>s, the path of <s>yoga</s> was expounded by you in great detail, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.
(1.11) Its summary was further expounded in twelve thousand [verses]; that too is extensive and is not grasped by those of limited intellect.
(1.12) Therefore, having condensed it, for the benefit of those of lesser understanding, please speak [that which] accomplishes all <s>siddhi</s>s, by your grace, O <s>Parameśvara</s> (Supreme Lord)."
(1.13) Thus addressed by the Goddess, the Lord of the Universe laughed and said: 'Listen, O Goddess, I shall expound the doctrine of <s>Siddhayogeśvarī</s>,
(1.14) the supreme <s>Mālinīvijaya</s>, which has not been revealed to anyone. Even by me, this was previously received from <s>Aghora</s>, the Supreme Self.
(1.15) What is to be accepted (<s>upādeya</s>) and what is to be rejected (<s>heya</s>) must be understood in the highest sense. <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Vidyeśa</s>s (Lords of Knowledge) together, <s>Mantra</s>s, <s>Mantreśvara</s>s (Lords of Mantras), and <s>Aṇu</s>s (individual souls) —
(1.16) this group of six is declared as what is to be accepted (<s>upādeya</s>) by those seeking the fruit [of liberation]. <s>Mala</s> (impurity), <s>karma</s> (action), <s>Māyā</s> (illusion), and the entire world produced by <s>Māyā</s> —
(1.17) all this is declared as what is to be rejected (<s>heya</s>). What is to be known (<s>vijñeya</s>) is the established reality. Having known and renounced this, one obtains the fruit of all <s>siddhi</s>s.
(1.18) Therein, the Lord is the doer of all, peaceful, omniscient, the maker of all, the master — both with parts (<s>sakala</s>) and without parts (<s>niṣkala</s>), infinite. His <s>Śakti</s> (Power) is also of the same nature.
(1.19) He, desiring to create, at the very beginning of creation, by his own will, awakened eight souls who are pure consciousness (<s>vijñānakevala</s>).
(1.20) <s>Aghora</s>, the supreme <s>Ghora</s>, <s>Ghorarūpa</s>, <s>Tadānana</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and <s>Pivana</s> —
(1.21) having appointed these eight, who perform maintenance, dissolution, protection, and grace, to the pure [ranks of] <s>Mantra</s> and <s>Mantreśvara</s>, then again
(1.22) he similarly created seven <s>koṭi</s>s (tens of millions) of <s>Mantra</s>s along with their circles (<s>maṇḍala</s>s). All these great <s>Mantra</s>s bestow all fruits.
(1.23) The self (<s>ātman</s>) should be known as fourfold. Among them, the <s>vijñānakevala</s> (pure consciousness alone) is joined with <s>mala</s> (impurity) alone; the <s>pralayakevala</s> (dissolved soul) is joined with that [mala] and <s>karma</s>.
(1.24) <s>Mala</s> (impurity) they consider to be ignorance, the cause of the sprout of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence). <s>Karma</s> (action) has the nature of <s>dharma</s> (merit) and <s>adharma</s> (demerit), characterized by pleasure, pain, and so forth.
(1.25) By the will of the Lord, the desire for experience arises in this [soul]. For the accomplishment of the means of experience for this soul desiring experience, the Lord of <s>Mantra</s>s
(1.26) created the world by entering <s>Māyā</s> with [his] powers. That [<s>Māyā</s>] is described as one, all-pervading, subtle, without parts, the repository of the world,
(1.27) without beginning or end, the sovereign of the impure, and without diminution. She produced the <s>kalā-tattva</s> (principle of limited agency); from union with which the <s>puruṣa</s> (individual soul) came into being.
(1.28) Having attained the capacity of doership, [the soul] then created <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>rāga</s> (attachment). <s>Vidyā</s> enables discernment regarding <s>karma</s> in its cause and effect;
(1.29) <s>rāga</s> causes attachment to one's own experiences, even those that are impure. <s>Niyati</s> (destiny) connects this individual soul to its own <s>karma</s>;
(1.30) <s>kāla</s> (time) also measures him, established in units beginning with <s>tuṭi</s> (the smallest time-unit). Then from that very <s>kalā-tattva</s>, it created <s>avyakta</s> (the unmanifest), then
(1.31) the <s>guṇa</s>s (qualities) having eight attributes, from them <s>dhī</s> (intellect), from intellect also <s>ahaṅkṛti</s> (ego-sense). That [ego] is threefold: from the <s>taijasa</s> (luminous) aspect arose <s>manas</s> (mind), the lord of the senses;
(1.32) from the <s>vaikārika</s> (modified) aspect, the sense organs; from the third [aspect], the <s>tanmātra</s>s (subtle elements). The organs of cognition (<s>buddhīndriya</s>s) are: hearing, touch, sight, taste, and smell;
(1.33) the organs of action (<s>karmendriya</s>s) are, in order: speech, hands, anus, generative organ, and feet. This circle of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), from <s>kalā</s> to earth,
(1.34) revolves the entire world including the oceans by [the Lord's] will. The further division of <s>kalā</s> and the other [principles], which exists as worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>s),
(1.35) he himself created for the accomplishment of the experiences of the experiencers. Thus, <s>puruṣa</s>s (individual souls) endowed with [principles] from <s>kalā</s> to earth
(1.36) should be known as <s>sakala</s> (bound souls with all impurities), by those who wish to destroy that condition. Even in this triple state, pervaded by <s>Śiva</s>'s <s>Śakti</s> (power) whose nature is concealment,
(1.37) they perform activity. Thus everywhere in the world, by the force of the fitness of the <s>Rudra</s>s, [who are]
(1.38) one hundred and eighteen, beginning with those the size of a thumb — <s>Śiva</s> himself, having graced [them], appointed them to the rank of <s>Mantreśa</s> (Lord of Mantras).
(1.39) They, having reached their respective domains, bestow fruit commensurate with their own power upon <s>Brahmā</s> and others who seek the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
(1.40) To the sages, they also — and those [sages] in turn to the great lords at the end of each <s>manvantara</s> (cosmic age) — relate the knowledge of what is to be rejected and accepted, as declared by <s>Śiva</s>.
(1.41) In the entire world from <s>Brahmā</s> to a blade of grass, as soon as it is born, three and a half <s>koṭi</s>s of <s>Mantra</s>s, appointed by <s>Śiva</s>,
(1.42) having graced the aggregate of individual souls, have gone to the state free from affliction. Thus, at some time, by the force of fitness, for this self,
(1.43) the <s>Śaiva Śakti</s> (power of <s>Śiva</s>), peaceful, bestowing the fruit of liberation, becomes connected. Through that connection, someone is liberated at that very instant;
(1.44) for someone else, the unity with ignorance is dissolved. Pervaded by <s>Rudra</s>'s power, desiring to depart, by <s>Śiva</s>'s will,
(1.45) for the accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation, [the soul] is led toward a true teacher (<s>sadguru</s>). Having propitiated him, then having obtained the <s>Śāṅkarī dīkṣā</s> (initiation of <s>Śaṅkara</s>) from the pleased [teacher],
(1.46) at that very instant, or through [continued] experience, or at the fall of the body, one goes to <s>Śiva</s>. Having obtained the <s>yoga-dīkṣā</s> (initiation into yoga), having understood <s>yoga</s>, one should practice it;
(1.47) one attains <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (perfection in yoga) and at the end of that, the eternal state. Through this sequential <s>yoga</s>, having attained the supreme state,
(1.48) one does not again become a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>); one abides in the pure Self. This self is indeed fourfold; and this [purified self] is again fourfold,
(1.49) being distinguished by the divisions of teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) and so forth — the purified self is so enumerated. The teacher and the <s>sādhaka</s> (practitioner) should perform the triad [of rites] beginning with the daily (<s>nitya</s>);
(1.50) and the other two [categories of practitioners] should perform only the daily [rites], for life, by the command of <s>Śiva</s>. What is to be accepted and what is to be rejected — all this has been declared. Having known this, which is the totality of all that is to be known, one becomes the vessel of all <s>siddhi</s>s (accomplishments).'

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre prathamo 'dhikāraḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter in the illustrious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: vyāptyadhikāro dvitīyaḥ
body.translated_text: The Second Chapter: On Pervasion (<s>Vyāptyadhikāra</s>)

body.text:
2.1ab: athaiṣām eva tattvānāṃ dharādīnām anukramāt
2.1cd: prapañcaḥ kathyate leśād yogināṃ yogasiddhaye
2.2ab: śaktimacchaktibhedena dharātattvaṃ vibhidyate
2.2cd: svarūpasahitaṃ tac ca vijñeyaṃ daśapañcadhā
2.3ab: śivādisakalātmāntāḥ śaktimantaḥ prakīrtitāḥ
2.3cd: tacchaktayaś ca vijñeyās tadvad eva vicakṣaṇaiḥ
2.4ab: evaṃ jalādimūlāntaṃ tattvavrātam idaṃ mahat
2.4cd: pṛthag bhedair imair bhinnaṃ vijñeyaṃ tatphalepsubhiḥ
2.5ab: anenaiva vidhānena puṃstattvāt tu kalāntikam
2.5cd: trayodaśavidhaṃ jñeyaṃ rudravat pralayākalaḥ
2.6ab: tadvan māyāpi vijñeyā navadhā jñānakevalaḥ
2.6cd: mantrāḥ saptavidhās tadvat pañcadhā mantranāyakāḥ
2.7ab: tridhā mantreśvareśānāḥ śivaḥ sākṣān na bhidyate
2.7cd: bhedaḥ prakathito leśād ananto vistarād ayam
2.8ab: evaṃ bhuvanamālāpi bhinnā bhedair imaiḥ sphuṭam
2.8cd: vijñeyā yogasiddhyarthaṃ yogibhir yogapūjitā
2.9ab: eteṣām eva tattvānāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca śāṅkari
2.9cd: ya ekam api jānāti so 'pi yogaphalaṃ labhet
2.10ab: yaḥ punaḥ sarvatattvāni vetty etāni yathārthataḥ
2.10cd: sa gurur matsamaḥ prokto mantravīryaprakāśakaḥ
2.11ab: dṛṣṭāḥ saṃbhāṣitās tena spṛṣṭāś ca prītacetasā
2.11cd: narāḥ pāpaiḥ pramucyante saptajanmakṛtair api
2.12ab: ye punar dīkṣitās tena prāṇinaḥ śivacoditāḥ
2.12cd: te yatheṣṭaṃ phalaṃ prāpya gacchanti paramaṃ padam
2.13ab: rudraśaktisamāveśas tatra nityaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ
2.13cd: sati tasmiṃś ca cihnāni tasyaitāni vilakṣayet
2.14ab: tatraitat prathamaṃ cihnaṃ rudre bhaktiḥ suniścalā
2.14cd: dvitīyaṃ mantrasiddhiḥ syāt sadyaḥpratyayakārikā
2.15ab: sarvasattvavaśitvaṃ ca tṛtīyaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ smṛtam
2.15cd: prārabdhakāryaniṣpattiś cihnam āhuś caturthakam
2.16ab: kavitvaṃ pañcamaṃ proktaṃ sālaṃkāraṃ manoharam
2.16cd: sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvam akasmāc cāsya jāyate
2.17ab: rudraśaktisamāveśaḥ pañcadhā paripaṭhyate
2.17cd: bhūtatattvātmamantreśaśaktibhedād varānane
2.18ab: pañcadhā bhūtasaṃjñas tu tathā triṃśatidhā paraḥ
2.18cd: ātmākhyas trividhaḥ prokto daśadhā mantrasaṃjñakaḥ
2.19ab: dvividhaḥ śaktisaṃjño 'pi jñātavyaḥ paramārthataḥ
2.19cd: pañcāśadbhedabhinno 'yaṃ samāveśaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
2.20ab: āṇavo 'yaṃ samākhyātaḥ śākto 'py evaṃvidhaḥ smṛtaḥ
2.20cd: evaṃ śāmbhavam apy ebhir bhedair bhinnaṃ vilakṣayet
2.21ab: uccārakaraṇadhyānavarṇasthānaprakalpanaiḥ
2.21cd: yo bhavet sa samāveśaḥ samyag āṇava ucyate
2.22ab: uccārarahitaṃ vastu cetasaiva vicintayan
2.22cd: yam āveśam avāpnoti śāktaḥ so 'trābhidhīyate
2.23ab: akiṃciccintakasyaiva guruṇā pratibodhataḥ
2.23cd: jāyate yaḥ samāveśaḥ śāmbhavo 'sāv udīritaḥ
2.24ab: sārdham etac chataṃ proktaṃ bhedānām anupūrvaśaḥ
2.24cd: saṃkṣepād vistarād asya parisaṃkhyā na vidyate
2.25ab: saṃvittiphalabhedo 'tra na prakalpyo manīṣibhiḥ
2.25cd: bhedo 'paro 'pi saṃkṣepāt kathyamāno 'vadhāryatām
2.26ab: jāgratsvapnādibhedena sarvāveśakramo budhaiḥ
2.26cd: pañcabhinnaḥ parijñeyaḥ svavyāpārāt pṛthak pṛthak
2.27ab: tatra svarūpaṃ śaktiś ca sakalaś ceti tattrayam
2.27cd: iti jāgradavastheyaṃ bhede pañcadaśātmake
2.28ab: akalau dvau parijñeyau samyak svapnasuṣuptayoḥ
2.28cd: mantrāditatpatīśānavargas turya iti smṛtaḥ
2.29ab: śaktiśaṃbhū parijñeyau turyātīte varānane
2.29cd: trayodaśātmake bhede svarūpam akalāv ubhau
2.30ab: mantramantreśvareśānāḥ śaktiśaṃbhū ca kīrtitau
2.30cd: pralayākalabhede 'pi svaṃ vijñānakalāv ubhau
2.31ab: mantramantreśvareśānāḥ śaktīśāv api pūrvavat
2.31cd: navadhā kīrtite bhede svaṃ mantrā mantranāyakāḥ
2.32ab: tadīśāḥ śaktiśaṃbhū ca pañcāvasthāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
2.32cd: pūrvavat saptabhede 'pi svaṃ mantreśeśaśaktayaḥ
2.33ab: śivaś ceti parijñeyāḥ pañcaiva varavarṇini
2.33cd: svaṃ śaktiḥ sanijeśānā śaktiśaṃbhū ca pañcake
2.34ab: trike svaśaktiśaktīcchāśivapadaṃ vilakṣayet
2.34cd: svavyāpārādhipatvena taddhīnaprerakatvataḥ
2.35ab: icchānivṛtteḥ svasthatvād abhinnam api pañcadhā
2.35cd: iti pañcātmake bhede vijñeyaṃ vastu kīrtitam
2.36ab: bhūyo 'py āsām avasthānāṃ saṃjñābhedaḥ prakāśyate
2.36cd: piṇḍasthaḥ sarvatobhadro jāgrannāmadvayaṃ matam
2.37ab: dvisaṃjñaṃ svapnam icchanti padasthaṃ vyāptir ity api
2.37cd: rūpasthaṃ tu mahāvyāptiḥ suṣuptasyāpi taddvayam
2.38ab: pracayaṃ rūpātītaṃ ca samyak turyam udāhṛtam
2.38cd: mahāpracayam icchanti turyātītaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ
2.39ab: pṛthak tattvaprabhedena bhedo 'yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ
2.39cd: sarvāṇi eva tattvāni pañcaitāni yathā śṛṇu
2.40ab: bhūtatattvābhidhānānāṃ yo 'ṃśo 'dhiṣṭheya iṣyate
2.40cd: piṇḍastham iti taṃ prāhuḥ padastham aparaṃ viduḥ
2.41ab: mantrās tatpatayaḥ seśā rūpastham iti kīrtyate
2.41cd: rūpātītaṃ parā śaktiḥ savyāpārāpy anāmayā
2.42ab: niṣprapañco nirābhāsaḥ śuddhaḥ svātmany avasthitaḥ
2.42cd: sarvātītaḥ śivo jñeyo yaṃ viditvā vimucyate
2.43ab: caturvidhaṃ tu piṇḍastham abuddhaṃ buddham eva ca
2.43cd: prabuddhaṃ suprabuddhaṃ ca padasthaṃ ca caturvidham
2.44ab: gatāgataṃ suvikṣiptaṃ saṅgataṃ susamāhitam
2.44cd: caturdhā rūpasaṃsthaṃ tu jñātavyaṃ yogacintakaiḥ
2.45ab: uditaṃ vipulaṃ śāntaṃ suprasannam athāparam
2.45cd: manonmanam anantaṃ ca sarvārthaṃ satatoditam
2.46ab: pracaye tatra saṃjñeyam ekaṃ tanmahati sthitam
2.46cd: ity evaṃ pañcadhādhvānaṃ tridhedānīṃ nigadyate
2.47ab: vijñānākalaparyantam ātmatattvam udāhṛtam
2.47cd: īśvarāntaṃ ca vidyāhvaṃ śeṣaṃ śivapadaṃ viduḥ
2.48ab: evaṃ bhedair imair bhinnas tatrādhvā parikīrtitaḥ
2.48cd: yugapat sarvamārgāṇāṃ prabhedaḥ procyate 'dhunā
2.49ab: pārthivaṃ prākṛtaṃ caiva māyīyaṃ śāktam eva ca
2.49cd: iti saṅkṣepataḥ proktam etad aṇḍacatuṣṭayam
2.50ab: pṛthag dvayam asaṅkhyātam ekam ekaṃ pṛthak pṛthak
2.50cd: ādyaṃ dhārikayā vyāptaṃ tatraikaṃ tattvam iṣyate
2.51ab: ekam ekaṃ pṛthak kṣārṇaṃ padārṇamanuṣu smaret
2.51cd: kālāgnibhuvanād yāvad vīrabhadrapurottamam
2.52ab: puraṣoḍaśakaṃ jñeyaṃ ṣaḍvidho 'dhvā prakīrtitaḥ
2.52cd: āpyāyinyā dvitīyaṃ ca tatra tattvāni lakṣayet
2.53ab: trayoviṃśatyabādīni tadvad dhādyakṣarāṇi ca
2.53cd: padāni pañca mantrāś ca ṣaṭpañcāśatpurāṇi ca
2.54ab: tattvāni sapta bodhinyā tac caturdhā purāṇi ca
2.54cd: tṛtīye sapta varṇāḥ syuḥ padamantradvayaṃ dvayam
2.55ab: utpūyinyā caturthaṃ tu tatra tattvatrayaṃ viduḥ
2.55cd: varṇatrayaṃ mantram ekaṃ padam ekaṃ ca lakṣayet
2.56ab: aṣṭādaśa vijānīyād bhuvanāni samāsataḥ
2.56cd: śivatattvaṃ paraṃ śāntaṃ kalā tatrāvakāśadā
2.57ab: svaraṣoḍaśakaṃ mantraṃ padaṃ caikaṃ vilakṣayet
2.57cd: ity evaṃ ṣaḍvidho 'py adhvā samāsāt parikīrtitaḥ
2.58ab: śuddhāśuddhaṃ jagatsarvaṃ brahmāṇḍaprabhavaṃ yataḥ
2.58cd: tasmāc chuddham imaiḥ śuddhair brahmāṇḍaiḥ sarvam iṣyate
2.59ab: brahmā viṣṇuś ca rudraś ca īśvaraś ceti suvrate
2.59cd: pṛthag eteṣu boddhavyaṃ śāntaṃ paticatuṣṭayam
2.60ab: yo hi yasmād guṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmād ūrdhva ucyate
2.60cd: etat te kathitaṃ sarvaṃ kim anyat paripṛcchasi
body.translated_text:
Now, the elaboration of these very <s>tattvas</s> (principles), beginning with <s>dharā</s> (earth), in sequence,
is briefly described for the <s>yoga</s>-attainment of <s>yogins</s>.
The <s>dharā-tattva</s> (earth principle) is divided by the distinction of possessors of power and powers,
and that, together with its own nature, should be known as fifteenfold.
From <s>Śiva</s> down to <s>Sakala</s>, the possessors of power are proclaimed;
and their powers should be known in the same manner by the discerning.
Thus this great multitude of <s>tattvas</s> (principles), from water to the root,
each divided by these distinctions, should be known by those who seek their fruit.
By this very method, from the <s>Puṃs-tattva</s> (soul principle) up to <s>Kalā</s>,
the thirteenfold should be known; like <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Pralayākala</s> (dissolution-void being).
Likewise <s>Māyā</s> too should be known as ninefold; the <s>Jñānakevala</s> (knowledge-only being);
the <s>Mantras</s> are sevenfold, likewise the <s>Mantranāyakas</s> (mantra-lords) are fivefold.
The <s>Mantreśvareśānas</s> (lords of mantra-lords) are threefold; <s>Śiva</s> himself is not divided.
This division has been briefly stated; in its fullness it is endless.
Thus the garland of worlds (<s>bhuvanamālā</s>) too, clearly divided by these distinctions,
should be known for the purpose of <s>yoga</s>-attainment, honored in <s>yoga</s> by <s>yogins</s>.
Of these very <s>tattvas</s> and worlds, O <s>Śāṅkarī</s>,
he who knows even one of them, even he shall obtain the fruit of <s>yoga</s>.
But he who knows all these <s>tattvas</s> as they truly are,
he is declared a <s>guru</s> equal to Me, a revealer of <s>mantra</s>-power.
Those people who have been seen by him, conversed with by him, or touched by him with a pleased heart,
are freed from sins, even those committed over seven births.
And those living beings who are initiated by him, impelled by <s>Śiva</s>,
having obtained their desired fruit, they go to the supreme state.
<s>Rudra-śakti-samāveśa</s> (absorption into Rudra's power) is perpetually established in such a one,
and when that is present, one should discern these signs of it.
Therein the first sign is unwavering devotion to <s>Rudra</s>;
the second would be <s>mantra-siddhi</s> (perfection of mantra), producing immediate results.
Mastery over all beings is declared the third characteristic;
completion of every undertaking, they call the fourth sign.
Poetic power is declared the fifth, adorned with figures of speech and captivating;
and knowledge of the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures) arises in him spontaneously.
<s>Rudra-śakti-samāveśa</s> (absorption into Rudra's power) is taught as fivefold,
by the distinction of <s>bhūta</s> (element), <s>tattva</s> (principle), <s>ātman</s> (self), <s>mantra</s>, and <s>śakti</s> (power), O fair-faced one.
The one called <s>bhūta</s> is fivefold, and the next is thirtyfold;
the one called <s>ātman</s> is declared threefold, the one called <s>mantra</s> is tenfold.
The one called <s>śakti</s> too should be known as twofold in the ultimate sense;
this <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) is proclaimed as divided into fifty distinctions.
This is called <s>āṇava</s> (pertaining to the individual); the <s>śākta</s> (pertaining to power) is likewise considered of the same kind;
thus one should discern the <s>śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to Śiva) too as divided by these distinctions.
That <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) which arises through <s>uccāra</s> (breath-rising), <s>karaṇa</s> (sense-activity), <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>varṇa</s> (phoneme), and <s>sthāna</s> (station) practices,
is properly called <s>āṇava</s> (individual-level absorption).
Contemplating with the mind alone a reality devoid of <s>uccāra</s> (breath-rising),
the absorption one attains is here called <s>śākta</s> (power-level absorption).
For one who thinks of nothing whatsoever, from the awakening by a <s>guru</s>,
the <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) that arises is called <s>śāmbhava</s> (Śiva-level absorption).
These one hundred and fifty divisions have been stated in order;
in brief and in detail, their enumeration is without limit.
The distinction of the fruit of consciousness should not be imagined here by the wise;
yet another division, briefly stated, should be understood.
By the distinctions of waking, dreaming, and so forth, the wise should know
the sequence of all absorptions as fivefold, each distinct by its own function.
Therein, own-nature, power, and the <s>Sakala</s> — these are three;
thus this is the waking state, in the fifteenfold division.
The two <s>Akalas</s> (void beings) should be properly known in dream and deep sleep;
the group of <s>Mantra</s>, their lord, and <s>Īśāna</s> is known as <s>turya</s> (the fourth state).
<s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śambhu</s> should be known in <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), O fair-faced one.
In the thirteenfold division: own-nature, both <s>Akalas</s>,
<s>Mantra</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s> (lord of mantras), <s>Īśāna</s>, and <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śambhu</s> are declared.
In the <s>Pralayākala</s> division too: own-nature, both <s>Vijñānakalas</s> (knowledge-void beings),
<s>Mantra</s>, <s>Mantreśvara</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Īśa</s> as before.
In the ninefold division declared: own-nature, <s>Mantras</s>, <s>Mantranāyakas</s> (mantra-lords),
their lords, <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śambhu</s> — five states are proclaimed.
As before in the sevenfold division too: own-nature, <s>Mantreśa</s> (lord of mantras), <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Śaktis</s>,
and <s>Śiva</s> — these should be known as five alone, O lady of excellent complexion.
Own-nature, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Īśāna</s> with his lord, and <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śambhu</s> in the fivefold;
in the threefold, one should discern own-nature, <s>Śakti</s>, <s>Śakti-Icchā</s> (power-will), and the station of <s>Śiva</s>.
By sovereignty over one's own function, by being the impeller of those dependent on it,
by the cessation of will, and by abiding in one's own nature — though undivided, it is fivefold;
thus in the fivefold division, the reality to be known has been declared.
Furthermore, the distinction of names for these states is now revealed:
<s>Piṇḍastha</s> (abiding in the body) and <s>Sarvatobhadra</s> (auspicious in all directions) are the two names considered for waking.
Two names are assigned to dreaming: <s>Padastha</s> (abiding in the station) and <s>Vyāpti</s> (pervasion);
<s>Rūpastha</s> (abiding in form) and <s>Mahāvyāpti</s> (great pervasion) are the two for deep sleep.
<s>Pracaya</s> (accumulation) and <s>Rūpātīta</s> (beyond form) are properly declared for <s>turya</s> (the fourth);
the discerning call <s>Mahāpracaya</s> (great accumulation) the <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth).
This division has been set forth according to the distinctions of each <s>tattva</s> (principle) separately;
now hear how all the <s>tattvas</s> are these same five.
The portion of the <s>tattvas</s> called <s>bhūta</s> (elements) which is regarded as the governed —
that they call <s>Piṇḍastha</s> (abiding in the body); the other they know as <s>Padastha</s> (abiding in the station).
The <s>Mantras</s>, their lords, together with <s>Īśa</s> — that is called <s>Rūpastha</s> (abiding in form);
<s>Rūpātīta</s> (beyond form) is the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, together with her function, yet free from affliction.
Devoid of elaboration, without appearance, pure, established in his own Self,
transcending all — <s>Śiva</s> should be known; knowing whom one is liberated.
<s>Piṇḍastha</s> (abiding in the body) is fourfold: unawakened, awakened,
fully awakened, and supremely awakened; and <s>Padastha</s> (abiding in the station) is also fourfold:
come-and-gone, well-projected, unified, and fully concentrated.
<s>Rūpastha</s> (abiding in form) too should be known by contemplators of <s>yoga</s> as fourfold:
arisen, expanded, peaceful, and supremely serene; and the other —
<s>Manonmana</s> (the beyond-mind), infinite, all-purposed, and perpetually arisen.
In <s>Pracaya</s> (accumulation), one thing is to be known there, established in the great;
thus the fivefold path is now stated in three ways.
Up to <s>Vijñānākala</s> (knowledge-void being) is declared the <s>Ātma-tattva</s> (self-principle);
up to <s>Īśvara</s> is that called <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge); the remainder they know as the station of <s>Śiva</s>.
Thus, the path (<s>adhvan</s>) there, divided by these distinctions, has been proclaimed;
now the division of all paths simultaneously is declared.
<s>Pārthiva</s> (of earth), <s>Prākṛta</s> (of nature), <s>Māyīya</s> (of māyā), and <s>Śākta</s> (of power) —
thus, in brief, this fourfold cosmic egg (<s>aṇḍa-catuṣṭaya</s>) has been declared.
Each two separately are innumerable, each one individually distinct;
the first is pervaded by <s>Dhārikā</s> (the sustaining power); therein one <s>tattva</s> is recognized.
One should contemplate each one separately — the phonemes of syllables, the phonemes of words, and <s>mantras</s> —
from the world of <s>Kālāgni</s> (fire of time) up to the supreme city of <s>Vīrabhadra</s>.
Sixteen worlds should be known; the sixfold path (<s>ṣaḍ-adhvan</s>) is proclaimed.
By <s>Āpyāyinī</s> (the nourishing power), the second [cosmic egg]; therein one should discern the <s>tattvas</s>:
twenty-three beginning with water, and likewise the phonemes beginning with 'ha',
five words, and <s>mantras</s>, and fifty-six worlds.
By <s>Bodhinī</s> (the awakening power), seven <s>tattvas</s>, and those worlds fourfold;
in the third, seven phonemes, two words and two <s>mantras</s>.
By <s>Utpūyinī</s> (the purifying power), the fourth; therein they know three <s>tattvas</s>,
three phonemes, one <s>mantra</s>, and one word should be discerned,
and eighteen worlds should be known in brief.
The supreme <s>Śiva-tattva</s> (Śiva-principle), peaceful, and the <s>kalā</s> (power) therein that grants space;
sixteen vowels, one <s>mantra</s>, and one word should be discerned.
Thus the sixfold path (<s>ṣaḍ-adhvan</s>) too has been proclaimed in summary.
Since the entire world, pure and impure, arises from the cosmic egg (<s>Brahmāṇḍa</s>),
therefore all is considered pure by means of these pure cosmic eggs.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Īśvara</s> — O virtuous one,
in each of these separately, one should know the peaceful fourfold lordship.
For he who is superior in qualities to another is said to be higher than that one.
All this has been told to you; what else do you ask?

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre vyāptyadhikāro dvitīyaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the second chapter, on <s>vyāpti</s> (pervasion), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottaratantra</s>.

body.text:
mantroddhārādhikāras tṛtīyaḥ
3.1ab: evam uktā mahādevī jagadānandakāriṇā
3.1cd: praṇipatya punar vākyam idam āha jagatpatim
3.2ab: evam etan mahādeva nānyathā samudāhṛtam
3.2cd: yathākhyātaṃ tathā jñātam āditaḥ samanukramāt
3.3ab: śivādivasturūpāṇāṃ vācakān parameśvara
3.3cd: sāṃprataṃ śrotum icchāmi prasādād vaktum arhasi
3.4ab: ity uktaḥ sa maheśānyā jagadārtiharo haraḥ
3.4cd: vācakān avadan mantrān pāramparyakramāgatān
3.5ab: yā sā śaktir jagaddhātuḥ kathitā samavāyinī
3.5cd: icchātvaṃ tasya sā devi sisṛkṣoḥ pratipadyate
3.6ab: saikāpi saty anekatvaṃ yathā gacchati tac chṛṇu
3.6cd: evam etad iti jñeyaṃ nānyatheti suniścitam
3.7ab: jñāpayantī jagaty atra jñānaśaktir nigadyate
3.7cd: evaṃbhūtam idaṃ vastu bhavatv iti yadā punaḥ
3.8ab: jātā tadaiva tat tadvat kurvaty atra kriyocyate
3.8cd: evam eṣā dvirūpāpi punar bhedair anantatām
3.9ab: arthopādhivaśād yāti cintāmaṇir iveśvarī
3.9cd: tatra tāvat samāpannā mātṛbhāvaṃ vibhidyate
3.10ab: dvidhā ca navadhā caiva pañcāśaddhā ca mālinī
3.10cd: bījayonyātmakād bhedād dvidhā bījaṃ svarā matāḥ
3.11ab: kādibhiś ca smṛtā yonir navadhā vargabhedataḥ
3.11cd: pṛthag varṇavibhedena śatārdhakiraṇojjvalā
3.12ab: bījam atra śivaḥ śaktir yonir ity abhidhīyate
3.12cd: vācakatvena sarvāpi śaṃbhoḥ śaktiś ca śasyate
3.13ab: vargāṣṭakam iha jñeyam aghorādyam anukramāt
3.13cd: tad eva śaktibhedena māheśvaryādi cāṣṭakam
3.14ab: māheśī brāhmaṇī caiva kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā
3.14cd: aindrī yāmyā ca cāmuṇḍā yogīśī ceti tā matāḥ
3.15ab: śatārdhabhedabhinnānāṃ tatsaṃkhyānāṃ varānane
3.15cd: rudrāṇāṃ vācakatvena kalpitāḥ parameṣṭhinā
3.16ab: tadvad eva ca śaktīnāṃ tatsaṃkhyānām anukramāt
3.16cd: sarvaṃ ca kathayiṣyāmi tāsāṃ bhedaṃ yathā śṛṇu
3.17ab: amṛto 'mṛtapūrṇaś ca amṛtābho 'mṛtadravaḥ
3.17cd: amṛtaugho 'mṛtormiś ca amṛtasyandano 'paraḥ
3.18ab: amṛtāṅgo 'mṛtavapur amṛtodgāra eva ca
3.18cd: amṛtāsyo 'mṛtatanus tathā cāmṛtasecanaḥ
3.19ab: tanmūrtir amṛteśaś ca sarvāmṛtadharo 'paraḥ
3.19cd: ṣoḍaśaite samākhyātā rudrabījasamudbhavāḥ
3.20ab: jayaś ca vijayaś caiva jayantaś cāparājitaḥ
3.20cd: sujayo jayarudraś ca jayakīrtir jayāvahaḥ
3.21ab: jayamūrtir jayotsāho jayado jayavardhanaḥ
3.21cd: balaś cātibalaś caiva balabhadro balapradaḥ
3.22ab: balāvahaś ca balavān baladātā baleśvaraḥ
3.22cd: nandanaḥ sarvatobhadro bhadramūrtiḥ śivapradaḥ
3.23ab: sumanāḥ spṛhaṇo durgo bhadrakālo manonugaḥ
3.23cd: kauśikaḥ kālaviśveśau suśivaḥ kopavardhanaḥ
3.24ab: ete yonisamudbhūtāś catustriṃśat prakīrtitāḥ
3.24cd: strīpāṭhavaśam āpannā eta evātra śaktayaḥ
3.25ab: bījayonisamudbhūtā rudraśaktisamāśrayāḥ
3.25cd: vācakānām anantatvāt parisaṃkhyā na vidyate
3.26ab: sarvaśāstrārthagarbhiṇyā ity evaṃvidhayānayā
3.26cd: aghoraṃ bodhayām āsa svecchayā parameśvaraḥ
3.27ab: sa tayā saṃprabuddhaḥ san yoniṃ vikṣobhya śaktibhiḥ
3.27cd: tatsamānaśrutīn varṇāṃs tatsaṃkhyān asṛjat prabhuḥ
3.28ab: te tair āliṅgitāḥ santaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradāḥ
3.28cd: bhavanti sādhakendrāṇāṃ nānyathā vīravandite
3.29ab: tair idaṃ saṃtataṃ viśvaṃ sadevāsuramānuṣam
3.29cd: tebhyaḥ śāstrāṇi vedāś ca saṃbhavanti punaḥ punaḥ
3.30ab: anantasyāpi bhedasya śivaśakter mahātmanaḥ
3.30cd: kāryabhedān mahādevi traividhyaṃ samudāhṛtam
3.31ab: viṣayeṣv eva saṃlīnān adho 'dhaḥ pātayanty aṇūn
3.31cd: rudrāṇūnyāḥ samāliṅgya ghorataryo 'parāḥ smṛtāḥ
3.32ab: miśrakarmaphalāsaktiṃ pūrvavaj janayanti yāḥ
3.32cd: muktimārganirodhinyās tāḥ syur ghorāḥ parāparāḥ
3.33ab: pūrvavaj jantujātasya śivadhāmaphalapradāḥ
3.33cd: parāḥ prakathitās tajjñair aghorāḥ śivaśaktayaḥ
3.34ab: etāḥ sarvāṇusaṃghātam api niṣṭhā yathā sthitāḥ
3.34cd: tathā te kathitāḥ śaṃbhoḥ śaktir ekaiva śāṅkarī
3.35ab: asyā vācakabhedena bhedo 'nyaḥ saṃpracakṣyate
3.35cd: yatheṣṭaphalasaṃsiddhyai mantratantrānuvartinām
3.36ab: viśeṣavidhihīneṣu nyāsakarmasu mantravit
3.36cd: nyasec chāktaśarīrārthaṃ bhinnayoniṃ tu mālinīm
3.37ab: na śikhā ṛ.Rḷṭ ca śiromālā tha mastakam
3.37cd: netrāṇi cadha vai nāsā ī samudre ṇuṇū śrutī
3.38ab: bakavarga iā vaktradantajihvāsu vāci ca
3.38cd: vabhayāḥ kaṇṭhadakṣādiskandhayor bhujayor ḍaḍhau
3.39ab: ṭho hastayor jhañau śākhā jraṭau śūlakapālake
3.39cd: pa hṛc chalau stanau kṣīram ā sa jīvo visargayuk
3.40ab: tatparaḥ kathitaḥ prāṇaḥ ṣakṣāv udaranābhigau
3.40cd: maśaṃtāḥ kaṭiguhyoru yugmagā jānunī tathā
3.41ab: eaikārau tathā jaṅghe tatparau caraṇau daphau
3.41cd: ato vidyāś ca mantrāś ca samuddhāryā yathā śṛṇu
3.42ab: sabindukāṃ dakṣajaṅghāṃ tato vācaṃ prakalpayet
3.42cd: tayaiva jaṅghayā yuktaṃ caturthaṃ daśanaṃ tataḥ
3.43ab: dakṣajānuyutaṃ daṇḍaṃ prāṇaṃ daṇḍastham īryutam
3.43cd: pṛthag ghṛddaṇḍakaṭigā dvijadaṇḍau ca pūrvavat
3.44ab: usthitaṃ binduyukprāṇaṃ pūrvavad daśanaṃ tataḥ
3.44cd: daṇḍaṃ kevalam uddhṛtya vāmamudrānvitaṃ punaḥ

3.45cd: daśanaṃ purvavan nyasya daṇḍaṃ kevalam eva ca
3.46ab: nitambaṃ dakṣamudretaṃ dvitīyaṃ jihvayā dvijam
3.46cd: sanāsaṃ dakṣaśikharaṃ nitambaṃ kevalaṃ tataḥ
3.47ab: punas tathaiva śikharaṃ jaṭharaṃ kevalaṃ tataḥ
3.47cd: dakṣajānuyutaṃ karṇaṃ kaṇṭhaṃ kevalam eva ca
3.48ab: nitambaṃ kevalaṃ nyasya hṛdayaṃ jihvayā yutam
3.48cd: vaktraṃ kevalam uddhṛtya prāṇam ādyena jānunā
3.49ab: śūladaṇḍacatuṣkaṃ ca tatrādyaṃ dvayam usthitam
3.49cd: vāmapādaṃ ca tasyānte kapālaṃ patitaṃ nyaset
3.50ab: tataḥ paramaghorāntaṃ pādyakādye ca pūrvavat
3.50cd: parāparā samākhyātā aparā ca prakathyate
3.51ab: aghorāntaṃ nyased ādau prāṇaṃ binduyutaṃ punaḥ
3.51cd: vāmamudrānvitaṃ nyasya pādyaṃ kādyena pūrvavat
3.52ab: apareyaṃ samākhyātā rudraśaktiṃ parāṃ śṛṇu
3.52cd: mantrāḥ saṃmukhatāṃ yānti yayoccāritamātrayā
3.53ab: kampate gātrayaṣṭiś ca drutaṃ cotpatanaṃ bhavet
3.53cd: mudrābandhaṃ ca geyaṃ ca śivāruditam eva ca
3.54ab: atītānagatārthasya kuryād vā kathanādikam
3.54cd: vāmajaṅghānvito jīvaḥ pāramparyakramāgataḥ
3.55ab: pareyam anayā siddhiḥ sarvakāmaphalapradā
3.55cd: nāśiṣyāya pradeyeyaṃ nābhaktāya kadā cana
3.56ab: rudraś ca rudraśaktiś ca guruś ceti trayaṃ samam
3.56cd: bhaktyā prapaśyate yas tu tasmai deyā varānane
3.57ab: śiṣyenāpi tadā grāhyā yadā saṃtoṣito guruḥ
3.57cd: śarīradravyavijñānaśuddhikarmaguṇādibhiḥ
3.58ab: bodhitā tu yadā tena guruṇā hṛṣṭacetasā
3.58cd: tadā siddhipradā jñeyā nānyathā vīravandite
3.59ab: parāparāṅgasaṃbhūtā yoginyo 'ṣṭau mahābalāḥ
3.59cd: pañca ṣaṭ pañca catvāri dvitridvyarṇāḥ krameṇa tu
3.60ab: jñeyāḥ saptaikādaśārṇā ekārdhārṇadvayānvitā
3.60cd: jīvo dīrghasvaraiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ pṛthag jātivibheditaḥ
3.61ab: vidyātrayasya gātrāṇi hrasvair vaktrāṇi pañcabhiḥ
3.61cd: oṃkāraiḥ pañcabhir mantro vidyāṅgahṛdayaṃ bhavet
3.62ab: oṃ amṛte tejomālini svāhā padāni bhūṣitam
3.62cd: ekādaśākṣaraṃ proktam etad brahmaśiraḥ priye
3.63ab: vedavedini hūṃphaṭ ca ca praṇavādisamanvitā
3.63cd: rudrāṇy aṣṭākṣarā jñeyā śikhā vidyāgaṇasya tu
3.64ab: vajriṇe vajradharāya svāhāntaṃ praṇavādikam
3.64cd: ekādaśākṣaraṃ varma puruṣṭutam iti smṛṭam
3.65ab: ślīpadaṃ paśuśabdaṃ ca hūṃphaḍantaṃ bhavādikam
3.65cd: etat pāśupataṃ proktam ardhasaptākṣaraṃ param
3.66ab: laraṭakṣavayair dīrghaiḥ sūmāyuktaiḥ sabindukaiḥ
3.66cd: indrādīn kalpayed dhrasvais tadastrāṇi vicakṣaṇaḥ
3.67ab: tadvan nāsāpayobhyāṃ tu kalpyau viṣṇuprajāpatī
3.67cd: svarāv ādyatṛtīyau tu vācakau padmacakrayoḥ
3.68ab: iti mantragaṇaḥ proktaḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaḥ
3.68cd: yogināṃ yogasiddhyarthaṃ kim anyat paripṛcchasi
body.translated_text:
The Third Chapter: On the Extraction of <s>Mantras</s> (<s>Mantroddhārādhikāra</s>)
(3.1) Thus addressed by the one who brings bliss to the world, the great goddess (<s>Mahādevī</s>), having bowed down, again spoke this word to the lord of the world:
(3.2) "So it is, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, it has been declared as nothing other [than this]. As it was explained, so it has been understood, from the beginning in due sequence.
(3.3) O Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), I now wish to hear the signifiers (<s>vācaka</s>) of the realities (<s>vastu</s>) beginning with <s>Śiva</s>. Please be gracious and speak."
(3.4) Thus addressed by the great queen of the Lord (<s>Maheśānī</s>), <s>Hara</s>, the remover of the world's suffering, spoke the signifying <s>mantras</s>, which have come down through the lineage of tradition.
(3.5) That <s>Śakti</s> (power) of the creator of the world, which has been described as inseparable [from him] — O <s>Devī</s>, she assumes the nature of will (<s>icchā</s>) when he desires to create.
(3.6) Hear how she, though one, assumes multiplicity. "It is thus" — this should be known; "not otherwise" — this is firmly established.
(3.7) When she makes [things] known in this world, she is called the power of knowledge (<s>jñānaśakti</s>). And when again [she wills] "let this reality be of such a nature,"
(3.8) Having arisen at that very moment, she who acts accordingly is called the power of action (<s>kriyāśakti</s>). Thus, though she has two forms, she again assumes infinitude
(3.9) Through the conditions of [various] objects, like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), O sovereign goddess. There, first, having assumed the state of the knower (<s>mātṛbhāva</s>), she divides
(3.10) Into twofold, ninefold, and fiftyfold — [she is] <s>Mālinī</s>. From the division into seed (<s>bīja</s>) and womb (<s>yoni</s>): the twofold [division] — the vowels are considered the seed,
(3.11) And the [consonants] beginning with 'ka' are called the womb. Ninefold, through the division into groups (<s>varga</s>). Individually, through the distinction of [fifty] phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>), she shines with fifty rays.
(3.12) Here, <s>Śiva</s> is the seed and <s>Śakti</s> is called the womb. All [phonemes] are praised as signifiers of <s>Śambhu</s>'s power.
(3.13) The eight groups should be known here as beginning with <s>Aghora</s>, in order. These same [groups], through the division of <s>Śaktis</s>, are the eightfold [group] beginning with <s>Māheśvarī</s>:
(3.14) <s>Māheśī</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇī</s>, <s>Kaumārī</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, <s>Aindrī</s>, <s>Yāmyā</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, and <s>Yogīśī</s> — these are considered [the eight].
(3.15) O beautiful-faced one, they have been ordained by the Supreme Lord as signifiers of the same number of <s>Rudras</s>, who are differentiated by the fifty divisions.
(3.16) Likewise, in sequence, for the same number of <s>Śaktis</s> — I shall tell all, hear the distinction among them:
(3.17) <s>Amṛta</s>, <s>Amṛtapūrṇa</s>, <s>Amṛtābha</s>, <s>Amṛtadrava</s>, <s>Amṛtaugha</s>, <s>Amṛtormi</s>, and another — <s>Amṛtasyandana</s>,
(3.18) <s>Amṛtāṅga</s>, <s>Amṛtavapu</s>, and also <s>Amṛtodgāra</s>, <s>Amṛtāsya</s>, <s>Amṛtatanu</s>, and also <s>Amṛtasecana</s>,
(3.19) <s>Tanmūrti</s>, <s>Amṛteśa</s>, and another — <s>Sarvāmṛtadhara</s>. These sixteen are declared as born from the <s>Rudra</s>-seed [i.e., the vowels].
(3.20) <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, <s>Aparājita</s>, <s>Sujaya</s>, <s>Jayarudra</s>, <s>Jayakīrti</s>, <s>Jayāvaha</s>,
(3.21) <s>Jayamūrti</s>, <s>Jayotsāha</s>, <s>Jayada</s>, <s>Jayavardhana</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Atibala</s>, <s>Balabhadra</s>, <s>Balaprada</s>,
(3.22) <s>Balāvaha</s>, <s>Balavān</s>, <s>Baladātā</s>, <s>Baleśvara</s>, <s>Nandana</s>, <s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>Bhadramūrti</s>, <s>Śivaprada</s>,
(3.23) <s>Sumanā</s>, <s>Spṛhaṇa</s>, <s>Durga</s>, <s>Bhadrakāla</s>, <s>Manonuga</s>, <s>Kauśika</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, <s>Viśveśa</s>, <s>Suśiva</s>, <s>Kopavardhana</s>.
(3.24) These thirty-four, born from the womb [i.e., consonants], are proclaimed. When converted to the feminine form, these very same are the <s>Śaktis</s>.
(3.25) Born from the combination of seed and womb, supported by <s>Rudra</s> and <s>Śakti</s> — since the signifiers are infinite, their enumeration is not [fully] possible.
(3.26) By means of this [<s>Mālinī</s>], who is pregnant with the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s>, the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) awakened <s>Aghora</s> by his own will.
(3.27) He [<s>Aghora</s>], being fully awakened by her, having agitated the womb with [his] <s>Śaktis</s>, the Lord created phonemes equal in number [to them], with sounds corresponding to them.
(3.28) Those [phonemes], being embraced by those [<s>Śaktis</s>], become bestowers of all desired fruits for the foremost of practitioners (<s>sādhaka</s>) — not otherwise, O one praised by heroes.
(3.29) By them, this entire universe — with gods, demons, and humans — is pervaded. From them, the <s>śāstras</s> and <s>Vedas</s> arise again and again.
(3.30) O <s>Mahādevī</s>, though the division of <s>Śiva</s>'s power, the great-souled one, is infinite, a threefold [classification] is declared based on the differences of effects:
(3.31) Those [<s>Śaktis</s>] which, embracing the <s>aṇus</s> (souls) that are absorbed in sense-objects, cause them to fall lower and lower — the lesser <s>Rudra</s> [-Śaktis], are called the most terrible (<s>ghoratara</s>), the 'other' [class].
(3.32) Those which, as before, generate attachment to the fruits of mixed <s>karma</s> and obstruct the path to liberation — they are the terrible (<s>ghorā</s>), the 'intermediate' (<s>parāparā</s>) [class].
(3.33) Those which, as before, bestow upon living beings the fruit of <s>Śiva</s>'s abode — the knowers of truth call them the supreme (<s>parā</s>), the non-terrible (<s>aghorā</s>) <s>Śiva</s>-powers.
(3.34) Just as these are established as the final state of the aggregate of all <s>aṇus</s> (souls), so they have been described. [In truth,] <s>Śambhu</s>'s power is one alone — <s>Śāṅkarī</s>.
(3.35) Another division of hers will be explained through the distinction of signifiers, for the attainment of desired fruits by the followers of <s>mantra</s> and <s>tantra</s>.
(3.36) In <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) rites that lack specific procedural rules, the knower of <s>mantras</s> should place <s>Mālinī</s> with separated womb [consonants], for the purpose of [constructing] the body of <s>Śakti</s>.
(3.37) 'Na' [is placed on] the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>); 'Ṛ', 'Ṝ', 'Ḷ', 'Ṭ' and 'Ca' [form] the head-garland (<s>śiromālā</s>); 'Tha' [on] the crown;
(3.38) The eyes are 'Ca', 'Da', 'Ha'; indeed 'Vai' [is] the nose; 'Ī' [is] the ocean [of the face]; 'Ṇu', 'Ṇū' [are] the ears. The 'ba-ka' group, 'I', 'Ā' [are placed on] the face, teeth, tongue, and in the voice.
(3.39) 'Va', 'Bha', 'Ya' [are on] the throat, right [shoulder], left shoulder, and both arms; 'Ḍa', 'Ḍha' [are on the arms]. 'Ṭho' [is on] both hands; 'Jha', 'Ña' [are] the branches [fingers]; 'Jra', 'Ṭa' are the trident and skull[-staff].
(3.40) 'Pa' [is on] the heart; 'Cha', 'La' [on] the two breasts; 'Kṣ' [is] the milk; 'Ā', 'Sa' [is] the life-force (<s>jīva</s>) joined with <s>visarga</s>. Beyond that is declared the <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath); 'Ṣa', 'Kṣ' [cover] the belly and navel.
(3.41) 'Ma', 'Śa', 'Ṃ', 'Tā' [are placed on] the hips, private parts, and thighs — paired [on both sides]; likewise 'Ja' and 'Ā' [are] the knees. 'E' and 'Ai' [are] the two shanks; beyond them, 'Ca' and 'Ra' [are] the two feet; 'Da', 'Pha' [complete the placement].
(3.42) Now hear how the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledge-formulas) and <s>mantras</s> are to be extracted. One should construct the speech (<s>vāc</s>) from the right shank joined with <s>bindu</s> (nasal dot); then the fourth tooth [i.e., phoneme from that position],
(3.43) Joined with the right knee [phoneme], [forms] the rod (<s>daṇḍa</s>); the <s>prāṇa</s> stationed on the rod, joined with 'Ī'; separately, the 'Hṛd' [heart-phoneme], rod, and hip [phonemes]; the two 'tooth' and 'rod' [phonemes] as before;
(3.44) The 'U'-stationed [phoneme] joined with <s>bindu</s> and <s>prāṇa</s>; then as before the 'tooth' [phoneme]; having extracted the rod alone, again joined with the left <s>mudrā</s> [seal-phoneme];
(3.45) The right knee [phoneme] joined with 'Hṛc' (heart) and <s>prāṇa</s> joined with the individual self (<s>jīvātman</s>); having placed the 'tooth' [phoneme] as before, and the rod alone;
(3.46) The hip [phoneme] joined with the right <s>mudrā</s>; the second 'tooth' [phoneme] with the 'tongue'; joined with the 'nose' [phoneme], the right 'peak' [phoneme]; then the hip alone;
(3.47) Again likewise the 'peak'; then the belly alone; the 'ear' [phoneme] joined with the right knee; and the 'throat' alone;
(3.48) Having placed the hip alone, the heart joined with the 'tongue'; having extracted the face alone, the <s>prāṇa</s> with the first knee [phoneme];
(3.49) And the four-fold trident-rod — of which the first two are 'U'-stationed; and the left foot at its end — one should place the 'skull' [phoneme] as fallen [at the end].
(3.50) Then, ending with <s>Paramaghorā</s>, and in the washing rites (<s>pādya</s>) and others as before — [this] is called <s>Parāparā</s> (the intermediate [<s>vidyā</s>]). And the <s>Aparā</s> (lower [<s>vidyā</s>]) is now explained:
(3.51) One should first place [the sequence] ending with <s>Aghorā</s>; then <s>prāṇa</s> joined with <s>bindu</s>; having placed [it] joined with the left <s>mudrā</s>; the washing [rite] with [the sequence] beginning with 'ka' as before.
(3.52) This is called <s>Aparā</s>. Now hear the supreme <s>Rudra-Śakti</s> (<s>Parā</s>): [she is the <s>mantra</s>] by whose mere utterance the <s>mantras</s> come face-to-face [i.e., become effective];
(3.53) The bodily frame trembles, and rapid levitation occurs; <s>mudrā</s>-locks (spontaneous gestures), singing, and the weeping of <s>Śiva</s> [arise];
(3.54) Or one may narrate matters past and future. The life-force (<s>jīva</s>) joined with the left shank [phoneme], come through the succession of tradition —
(3.55) This is the <s>Parā</s> (supreme). By her, <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) that bestows all desired fruits [is gained]. She should not be given to a non-disciple, nor ever to one lacking devotion.
(3.56) <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Rudra-Śakti</s>, and the <s>Guru</s> — these three are equal. To one who perceives [them] with devotion, O beautiful-faced one, she should be given.
(3.57) And by the disciple she should be accepted [only] when the <s>Guru</s> is satisfied — through purity of body, wealth, knowledge, ritual action, qualities, and the like.
(3.58) When [the <s>vidyā</s>] is awakened by the <s>Guru</s> with a joyful heart, then she should be known as bestowing <s>siddhi</s>; not otherwise, O one praised by heroes.
(3.59) Born from the limbs of the <s>Parāparā</s> [<s>vidyā</s>], there are eight <s>Yoginīs</s> of great power — [having respectively] five, six, five, four, two, three, [and] two phonemes, in order;
(3.60) They should be known [as having] seven, eleven phonemes, [and] one-and-a-half and two [phonemes respectively]. The life-force (<s>jīva</s>), with the six long vowels, is separately differentiated by class.
(3.61) The limbs of the triad of <s>vidyās</s> [are formed] with the short [vowels]; the five faces with [the five syllables] beginning with '<s>Oṃ</s>'; the <s>mantra</s> that constitutes the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) of the <s>vidyā</s>-limbs [is formed] with the five '<s>Oṃ</s>'-s.
(3.62) "<s>Oṃ amṛte tejomālini svāhā</s>" — adorned with [these] words, it is declared to have eleven syllables. This is the '<s>Brahmaśiras</s>' (Head of <s>Brahman</s>), O beloved.
(3.63) "<s>Vedavedini hūṃ phaṭ</s>" — preceded by <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>) — this <s>Rudrāṇī</s> [<s>mantra</s>] should be known as having eight syllables; it is the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) of the group of <s>vidyās</s>.
(3.64) "<s>Vajriṇe vajradharāya svāhā</s>" — ending with <s>svāhā</s>, preceded by <s>praṇava</s> — this eleven-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] is the armor (<s>varma</s>), known as <s>Puruṣṭuta</s> (praised by men).
(3.65) The '<s>ślī</s>'-word and the '<s>paśu</s>'-word, ending with '<s>hūṃ phaṭ</s>', beginning with '<s>bhava</s>' — this is declared as the <s>Pāśupata</s> [weapon-<s>mantra</s>], supreme, with seven and a half syllables.
(3.66) With 'La', 'Ra', 'Ṭa', 'Kṣa', 'Va', 'Ya' — lengthened, joined with <s>ū</s>-sounds and <s>bindu</s> — one should construct [the <s>mantras</s> of] <s>Indra</s> and the other [guardians]; the discerning one [should use] the short [vowels] for their weapons (<s>astra</s>).
(3.67) Likewise, with the 'nose' and 'breast' [phonemes], one should construct <s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>. The first and third vowels are the signifiers of the lotus (<s>padma</s>) and the discus (<s>cakra</s>).
(3.68) Thus has been declared the group of <s>mantras</s>, bestowing the fruits of all desires, for the attainment of <s>yoga</s>-perfection by <s>yogins</s>. What else do you wish to ask?

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre mantroddhārādhikāras tṛtīyaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, on the extraction of <s>mantras</s> (<s>mantroddhārādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottaratantra</s>.

body.text: yogalakṣaṇadhikāraś caturthaḥ
body.translated_text: The Fourth Chapter: On the Characteristics of <s>Yoga</s> (<s>Yogalakṣaṇādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
4.1ab: athaitad upasaṃśrutya munayo muditekṣaṇāḥ
4.1cd: praṇamya krauñcahantāraṃ punar ūcur idaṃ vacaḥ
4.2ab: yogamārgavidhiṃ devyā pṛṣṭena parameṣṭhinā
4.2cd: tatpratijñāvatāpy uktaṃ kimarthaṃ mantralakṣaṇam
4.3ab: evam uktaḥ sa taiḥ samyak kārtikeyo mahāmatiḥ
4.3cd: idam āha vacas teṣāṃ saṃdehavinivṛttaye
4.4ab: yogam ekatvam icchanti vastuno 'nyena vastunā
4.4cd: yad vastu jñeyam ity uktaṃ heyatvādiprasiddhaye
4.5ab: dvirūpam api taj jñānaṃ vinā jñātuṃ na śakyate
4.5cd: tatprasiddhyai śivenoktaṃ jñānaṃ yad upavarṇitam
4.6ab: sabījayogasaṃsiddhyai mantralakṣaṇam apy alam
4.6cd: na cādhikāritā dīkṣāṃ vinā yoge 'sti śāṅkare
4.7ab: kriyājñānavibhedena sā ca dvedhā nigadyate
4.7cd: dvividhā sā prakartavyā tena caitad udāhṛtam
4.8ab: na ca yogādhikāritvam ekam evānayā bhavet
4.8cd: api mantrādhikāritvaṃ muktiś ca śivadīkṣayā
4.9ab: śrutvā caitat pater vākyaṃ romāñcitaśarīriṇī
4.9cd: idam āha punar vākyam ambā munivarottamāḥ
4.10ab: abhinnamālinīkāye tattvāni bhuvanāni ca
4.10cd: kalāḥ padāni mantrāś ca yathāvad avadhāritāḥ
4.11ab: bhinnayonis tu yā deva tvayoktā mālinī mama
4.11cd: tasyā aṅge yathaitāni saṃsthitāni tathā vada
4.12ab: evam ukto mahādevyā bhairavo bhūribhogadaḥ
4.12cd: sphuraddhimāṃśusaṃtānaprakāśitadigantaraḥ
4.13ab: surāsuraśiromaulimālālālitaśāsanaḥ
4.13cd: uvāca madhurāṃ vācam imām akleśitāśayām
4.14ab: yā mayā kathitā devi bhinnayonis tu mālinī
4.14cd: tadaṅge saṃpravakṣyāmi sarvam etad yathā sthitam
4.15ab: phe dharātattvam uddiṣṭaṃ dādijhānte 'nupūrvaśaḥ
4.15cd: trayoviṃśatyabādīni pradhānāntāni lakṣayet
4.16ab: ṭhādau ca saptake sapta puruṣādīni pūrvavat
4.16cd: iṅagheṣu trayaṃ vidyād vidyātaḥ sakalāvadhi
4.17ab: śivatattve gakārādināntān ṣoḍaśa lakṣayet
4.17cd: kalāḥ padāni mantrāś ca bhuvanāni ca sundari
4.18ab: pūrvavad veditavyāni tat saṅkhyārṇavibhedataḥ
4.18cd: vidyātrayavibhāgena yathedānīṃ tathā śṛṇu
4.19ab: niṣkale padam ekārṇaṃ tryarṇaikārṇam atha dvayam
4.19cd: sakale tu parijñeyaṃ pañcaikārṇadvayaṃ dvaye
4.20ab: caturekākṣare dve ca māyāditritaye mate
4.20cd: caturakṣaram ekaṃ ca kālādidvitaye matam
4.21ab: rañjake dvyarṇam uddiṣṭaṃ pradhāne tryarṇam iṣyate
4.21cd: buddhau devāṣṭakavyāptyā padaṃ dvyakṣaram iṣyate
4.22ab: tataḥ pañcāṣṭakavyāptyā dvyekadvidvyakṣarāṇi tu
4.22cd: vidyāpadāni catvāri sārdhavarṇaṃ tu pañcamam
4.23ab: ekaikasārdhavarṇāni trīṇi tattve tu pārthive
4.23cd: parāṅge sarvam anyac ca varṇamantrakalādikam
4.24ab: sārdhenāṇḍadvayaṃ vyāptam ekaikena pṛthag dvayam
4.24cd: aparāyāḥ samākhyātā vyāptir eṣā vilomataḥ
4.25ab: sārṇenāṇḍatrayaṃ vyāptaṃ triśūlena caturthakam
4.25cd: sarvātītaṃ visargeṇa parāvyāptir udāhṛtā
4.26ab: etat sarvaṃ parijñeyaṃ yoginā hitam icchatā
4.26cd: ātmano vā pareṣāṃ vā nānyathā tad avāpyate
4.27ab: dvāv eva mokṣadau jñeyau jñānī yogī ca śāṅkari
4.27cd: pṛthaktvāt tatra [3] boddhavyaṃ phalakāṅkṣibhiḥ
4.28ab: jñānaṃ ca trividhaṃ proktaṃ tatrādyaṃ śrutam iṣyate
4.28cd: cintāmayam athānyac ca bhāvanāmayam eva ca
4.29ab: śāstrārthasya parijñānaṃ vikṣiptasya śrutaṃ matam
4.29cd: idam atredam atreti idam atropayujyate
4.30ab: sarvam ālocya śāstrārtham ānupūrvyā vyavasthitam
4.30cd: tadvac cintāmayaṃ jñānaṃ dvirūpam upadiśyate
4.31ab: mandasvabhyastabhedena tatra svabhyastam ucyate
4.31cd: suniṣpanne tatas tasmiñ jāyate bhāvanāmayam
4.32ab: yato yogaṃ samāsādya yogī yogaphalaṃ labhet
4.32cd: evaṃ vijñānabhedena jñānī proktaś caturvidhaḥ
4.33ab: saṃprāpto ghaṭamānaś ca siddhaḥ siddhatamo 'nyathā
4.33cd: yogī caturvidho devi yathāvat pratipadyate
4.34ab: samāveśoktivad yogas trividhaḥ samudāhṛtaḥ
4.34cd: tatra prāptopadeśas tu pāramparyakrameṇa yaḥ
4.35ab: prāptayogaḥ sa vijñeyas trividho 'pi manīṣibhiḥ
4.35cd: cetaso ghaṭanaṃ tattvāc calitasya punaḥ punaḥ
4.36ab: yaḥ karoti tam icchanti ghaṭamānaṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
4.36cd: tad eva cetasā nānyad dvitīyam avalambate
4.37ab: siddhayogas tadā jñeyo yogī yogaphalārthibhiḥ
4.37cd: yaḥ punar yatra tatraiva saṃsthito 'pi yathā tathā
4.38ab: bhuñjānas tatphalaṃ tena hīyate na kathañ cana
4.38cd: susiddhaḥ sa tu boddhavyaḥ sadāśivasamaḥ priye
4.39ab: uttarottaravaiśiṣṭyam eteṣāṃ samudāhṛtam
4.39cd: jñānināṃ yogināṃ caiva dvayor yogavid uttamaḥ
4.40ab: yato 'sya jñānam apy asti pūrvo yogaphalojjhitaḥ
4.40cd: yataś ca mokṣadaḥ proktaḥ svabhyastajñānavān budhaiḥ
4.41ab: ity etat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ vijñeyaṃ yogipūjite
4.41cd: tantrārtham upasaṃhṛtya samāsād yogināṃ hitam
body.translated_text:
(4.1) Now, having heard this, the sages with delighted eyes,
having bowed to the slayer of <s>Krauñca</s> [i.e., <s>Kārtikeya</s>], spoke these words again:
(4.2) 'The procedure of the path of yoga was asked by the Goddess of the Supreme Lord;
even though He promised [to explain yoga], why did He describe the characteristics of mantras [instead]?'
(4.3) Thus addressed by them properly, <s>Kārtikeya</s>, of great wisdom,
spoke these words to them, for the removal of their doubt:
(4.4) '<s>Yoga</s> (union) is desired as the oneness of one entity with another;
what is declared as the entity to be known — [that teaching is] for the establishment of [its being] worthy of rejection and the like.
(4.5) Even though that [knowable entity] is of dual form, without knowledge it cannot be known;
for the accomplishment of that [knowledge], what <s>Śiva</s> described as knowledge [was explained].
(4.6) For the accomplishment of yoga with seed (<s>sabīja-yoga</s>), the characteristics of mantras are indeed sufficient;
and there is no eligibility for yoga in the Śaiva [system] without initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>).
(4.7) And that [initiation] is declared to be twofold, by the distinction of action (<s>kriyā</s>) and knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>);
it should be performed in two ways, and therefore this has been explained.
(4.8) And not only eligibility for yoga arises from this [initiation],
but also eligibility for mantras and liberation through the initiation of <s>Śiva</s>.'
(4.9) Having heard this statement of the father [Śiva], with her body thrilling [with joy],
the Mother [Goddess] spoke these words again, O best of sages:
(4.10) 'In the undivided body of the <s>Mālinī</s>, the principles (<s>tattva</s>), the worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>),
the divisions (<s>kalā</s>), the stages (<s>pada</s>), and the mantras have been duly ascertained.
(4.11) But the <s>Mālinī</s> of divided origin (<s>bhinnayoni</s>) that you, O Lord, spoke of to me —
tell me how these [tattvas, etc.] are established in her body.'
(4.12) Thus addressed by the Great Goddess, <s>Bhairava</s>, the giver of abundant enjoyments,
whose spreading radiant rays illuminated all directions,
(4.13) whose commands were honored by the garlands of crowns of gods and demons,
spoke these sweet words, free from all strain:
(4.14) 'The <s>Mālinī</s> of divided origin that I described, O Goddess —
I shall now explain how all this is arranged in her body.
(4.15) The earth principle (<s>dharā-tattva</s>) is indicated by [the letter] PHA; from DĀ to JHA, in order,
twenty-three [tattvas] from water (<s>ab</s>) onwards up to <s>Pradhāna</s> should be observed.
(4.16) In the group of seven beginning with ṬHA, the seven [tattvas] beginning with <s>Puruṣa</s>, as before;
in I, Ṅ, and GHA, one should know the three from <s>Vidyā</s> up to <s>Sakala</s>.
(4.17) In the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, one should observe the sixteen from GA and so on up to NĀ;
the divisions (<s>kalā</s>), stages (<s>pada</s>), mantras, and worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>), O Beautiful One,
(4.18) should be understood as before, by the distinction of those [tattvas and their] letters;
now hear about the division of the three <s>vidyā</s>s as [I explain].
(4.19) In the partless (<s>niṣkala</s>), one stage has one letter, [another has] three letters, one letter, and then two;
in the with-parts (<s>sakala</s>), one should know: five one-letter [stages] and two pairs.
(4.20) Two of four-and-one letters each, and in the triad beginning with <s>Māyā</s>,
one [stage] of four letters, and in the pair beginning with <s>Kāla</s> [also prescribed].
(4.21) In the coloring (<s>rañjaka</s>), a stage of two letters is indicated; in <s>Pradhāna</s>, three letters are desired;
in <s>Buddhi</s>, by the pervasion of the eight deities, a stage of two letters is desired.
(4.22) Then, by the pervasion of the five eights, two, one, two, and two letters —
these are the four stages of <s>Vidyā</s>; and the fifth has a half-letter.
(4.23) Three [stages] of one-and-a-half letters each in the earth principle;
in the other body (<s>parāṅga</s>), all the rest — letters, mantras, <s>kalā</s>s, and so forth.
(4.24) By a half[-letter], two cosmic eggs (<s>aṇḍa</s>) are pervaded; by one each, two separately;
of the latter [Mālinī], this pervasion is declared in reverse order.
(4.25) By one letter, three cosmic eggs are pervaded; by the trident, the fourth;
by the <s>Visarga</s>, all is transcended — thus is described the pervasion of <s>Parā</s>.
(4.26) All this should be understood by the yogin who desires welfare,
whether his own or that of others; it cannot be obtained otherwise.
(4.27) Two alone should be known as granting liberation: the knower (<s>jñānin</s>) and the yogin, O <s>Śāṅkarī</s>;
the distinction between them should be understood by those who desire results.
(4.28) And knowledge is declared to be threefold: the first is considered to be learned (<s>śruta</s>),
another is born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), and [the third is] born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>).
(4.29) The comprehension of the meaning of scripture by one whose mind is scattered is considered 'learned' (<s>śruta</s>);
"this is here, this is there, this is applicable here" —
(4.30) having considered all the meaning of scripture, systematically arranged,
reflective knowledge (<s>cintāmaya</s>) is likewise taught as being of two kinds:
(4.31) by the distinction of moderate and well-practiced; there, the well-practiced is [further] described;
when that is fully accomplished, then meditation-born [knowledge] (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>) arises.
(4.32) Whereupon, having attained yoga, the yogin obtains the fruit of yoga;
thus, by the distinction of [types of] understanding, the knower (<s>jñānin</s>) is declared fourfold.
(4.33) The arrived (<s>saṃprāpta</s>), the striving (<s>ghaṭamāna</s>), the accomplished (<s>siddha</s>), and the most accomplished (<s>siddhatama</s>) —
likewise, O Goddess, the yogin is fourfold, each to be understood properly.
(4.34) As was stated regarding the [three types of] absorption (<s>samāveśa</s>), yoga is likewise declared to be threefold;
there, one who has received instruction through the lineage of transmission,
(4.35) he is to be known as a 'yoga-arrived' (<s>prāptayoga</s>), himself also threefold according to the wise.
[The yogin] who brings the mind, again and again fallen from Reality, back to concentration —
(4.36) him the wise call the 'striving' (<s>ghaṭamāna</s>) yogin.
When his mind rests on that alone and does not grasp any second [object],
(4.37) then the 'accomplished yoga' (<s>siddhayoga</s>) should be known by those who desire the fruit of yoga.
But one who, wherever he may be, however situated,
(4.38) enjoys that fruit and is never diminished by it in any way —
he should be understood as 'most accomplished' (<s>susiddha</s>), equal to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, O Beloved.
(4.39) Among these, a progressively increasing excellence is declared;
and of the two — knowers and yogins — the knower of yoga is superior.
(4.40) Because he also possesses knowledge, whereas the former [mere knower] is devoid of the fruit of yoga;
and because the one possessing well-practiced knowledge is declared by the wise to grant liberation.
(4.41) Thus all this has been declared, which should be understood, O one honored by yogins;
having summarized the meaning of the tantra, [this is taught] in brief for the benefit of yogins.'

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre caturtho 'dhikāraḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: atha pañcamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: Now the fifth chapter.

body.text:
5.1ab: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi bhuvanādhvānam īśvari
5.1cd: ādau kālāgnibhuvanaṃ śodhitavyaṃ prayatnataḥ
5.2ab: avīciḥ kumbhīpākaś ca rauravaś ca tṛtīyakaḥ
5.2cd: kūṣmāṇḍabhuvane śuddhe sarve śuddhā na saṃśayaḥ
5.3ab: pātālāni tataḥ sapta teṣām ādau mahātalam
5.3cd: rasātalaṃ tataś cānyat talātalam ataḥ param
5.4ab: sutalaṃ nitalaṃ ceti vitalaṃ talam eva ca
5.4cd: hāṭakena viśuddhena sarveṣāṃ śuddhir iṣyate
5.5ab: tadūrdhvaṃ pṛthivī jñeyā saptadvīpārṇavānvitā
5.5cd: devānām āśrayo merus tanmadhye saṃvyavasthitaḥ
5.6ab: bhuvolokas tadūrdhve ca svarlokas tasya copari
5.6cd: maho janas tapaḥ satyam ity etal lokasaptakam
5.7ab: caturdaśavidho yatra bhūtagrāmaḥ pravartate
5.7cd: sthāvaraḥ sarpajātiś ca pakṣijātis tathāparā
5.8ab: mṛgasaṃjñaś ca paśvākhyaḥ pañcamo 'nyaś ca mānuṣaḥ
5.8cd: paiśāco rākṣaso yākṣo gāndharvaś caindra eva ca
5.9ab: saumyaś ca prājāpatyaś ca brāhmaś cātra caturdaśa
5.9cd: sarvasyaivāsya saṃśuddhir brāhme saṃśodhite sati
5.10ab: bhuvanaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tasmān madīyaṃ tadanantaram
5.10cd: tatra śuddhe bhavec chuddhaṃ sarvam etan na saṃśayaḥ
5.11ab: kālāgnipūrvakair ebhir bhuvanaiḥ pañcabhiḥ priye
5.11cd: śuddhaiḥ sarvam idaṃ śuddhaṃ brahmāṇḍāntarvyavasthitam
5.12ab: tadbahiḥ śatarudrāṇāṃ bhuvanāni pṛthak pṛthak
5.12cd: daśa saṃśodhayet paścād ekaṃ tannāyakāvṛtam
5.13ab: anantaḥ prathamas teṣāṃ kapālīśas tathāparaḥ
5.13cd: agnirudro yamaś caiva nairṛto bala eva ca
5.14ab: śīghro nidhīśvaraś caiva sarvavidyādhipo 'paraḥ
5.14cd: śaṃbhuś ca vīrabhadraś ca vidhūmajvalanaprabhaḥ
5.15ab: ebhir daśaikasaṃkhyātaiḥ śuddhaiḥ śuddhaṃ śataṃ matam
5.15cd: upariṣṭāt puras teṣām aṣṭakāḥ pañca saṃsthitāḥ
5.16ab: lakulī bhārabhūtiś ca diṇḍhyāṣāḍhī sapuṣkarau
5.16cd: naimiṣaṃ ca prabhāsaṃ ca amareśam athāṣṭakam
5.17ab: etat pratyātmakaṃ proktam ato guhyātiguhyakam
5.17cd: tatra bhairavakedāramahākālāḥ samadhyamāḥ
5.18ab: āmrātikeśajalpeśaśrīśailāḥ saharīndavaḥ
5.18cd: bhīmeśvaramahendrāṭṭahāsāḥ savimaleśvarāḥ
5.19ab: kanakhalaṃ nākhalaṃ ca kurukṣetraṃ gayā tathā
5.19cd: guhyam etat tṛtīyaṃ tu pavitram adhunocyate
5.20ab: sthānusvarṇākṣakāv ādyau bhadragokarṇakau parau
5.20cd: mahākālāvimukteśarudrakoṭyambarāpadāḥ
5.21ab: sthūlaḥ sthūleśvaraḥ śaṅkukarṇakālañjarāv api
5.21cd: maṇḍaleśvaramākoṭadviraṇḍachagalāṇḍakau
5.22ab: sthāṇvāṣṭakam iti proktam ahaṅkārāvadhi sthitam
5.22cd: devayonyaṣṭakaṃ buddhau kathyamānaṃ mayā śṛṇu
5.23ab: paiśācaṃ rākṣasaṃ yākṣaṃ gāndharvaṃ caindram eva ca
5.23cd: tathā saumyaṃ saprājeśaṃ brāhmam aṣṭamam iṣyate
5.24ab: yogāṣṭakaṃ pradhāne tu tatrādāv akṛtaṃ bhavet
5.24cd: kṛtaṃ ca raibhavaṃ brāhmaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tadanantaram
5.25ab: kaumāram aumaṃ śraikaṇṭham iti yogāṣṭakaṃ tathā
5.25cd: puruṣe vāmabhīmograbhaveśānaikavīrakāḥ
5.26ab: pracaṇḍomādhavājāś ca anantaikaśivāv atha
5.26cd: krodheśacaṇḍau vidyāyāṃ saṃvarto jyotir eva ca
5.27ab: kalātattve parijñeyau surapañcāntakau pare
5.27cd: ekavīraśikhaṇḍīśaśrīkaṇṭḥāḥ kālam āśritāḥ
5.28ab: mahātejaḥ prabhṛtayoḥ maṇḍaleśānasaṃjñakāḥ
5.28cd: māyātattve sthitās tatra vāmadevabhavodbhavau
5.29ab: ekapiṅgekṣaṇeśānabhuvaneśapuraḥsarāḥ
5.29cd: aṅguṣṭhamātrasahitāḥ kālānalasamatviṣaḥ
5.30ab: vidyātattve 'pi pañcāhur bhuvanāni manīṣiṇaḥ
5.30cd: tatra hālāhalaḥ pūrvo rudraḥ krodhas tathāparaḥ
5.31ab: ambikā ca aghorā ca vāmadevī ca kīrtyate
5.31cd: īśvare pivanādyāḥ syur aghorāntā maheśvarāḥ
5.32ab: raudrī jyeṣṭhā ca vāmā ca tathā śaktisadāśivau
5.32cd: etāni sakale pañca bhuvanāni vidur budhāḥ
5.33ab: evaṃ tu sarvatattveṣu śatam aṣṭādaśottaram
5.33cd: bhuvanānāṃ parijñeyaṃ saṅkṣepān na tu vistarāt
5.34ab: śuddhenānena śuddhyanti sarvāṇy api na saṃśayaḥ
5.34cd: sarvamārgaviśuddhau tu kartavyāyāṃ mahāmatiḥ
5.35ab: sakalāvadhi saṃśodhya śive yogaṃ prakalpayet
5.35cd: bubhukṣoḥ sakalaṃ dhyātvā yogaṃ kurvīta yogavit
5.36ab: ity eṣa kīrtito mārgo bhuvanākhyasya me mataḥ
body.translated_text:
5.1ab: Now I shall expound the path of worlds (<s>bhuvanādhvan</s>), O <s>Īśvarī</s> (Goddess).
5.1cd: First, the world of <s>Kālāgni</s> (the Fire of Time) should be purified with effort.
5.2ab: <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>, and <s>Raurava</s> as the third—
5.2cd: when [these are purified] in the world of <s>Kūṣmāṇḍa</s>, all are purified, without doubt.
5.3ab: Then the seven <s>pātālas</s> (netherworlds): among them, <s>Mahātala</s> is first,
5.3cd: then <s>Rasātala</s>, and another, <s>Talātala</s>, beyond that.
5.4ab: <s>Sutala</s>, <s>Nitala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, and <s>Tala</s> itself—
5.4cd: the purification of all of these is accomplished by pure gold (<s>hāṭaka</s>).
5.5ab: Above that is the earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>), known to be endowed with seven continents (<s>dvīpa</s>) and oceans.
5.5cd: <s>Meru</s>, the abode of the gods, is situated in its center.
5.6ab: Above that is <s>Bhuvar-loka</s>, and above that <s>Svar-loka</s>,
5.6cd: <s>Mahas</s>, <s>Janas</s>, <s>Tapas</s>, <s>Satya</s>—this is the sevenfold system of worlds.
5.7ab: Wherein the fourteen types of beings operate:
5.7cd: the stationary (plants), the serpent class, and likewise another, the bird class,
5.8ab: those called animals, the fifth called beasts, and another, the human;
5.8cd: the <s>paiśāca</s> (ghostly), <s>rākṣasa</s> (demonic), <s>yākṣa</s>, <s>gāndharva</s>, and <s>aindra</s> (belonging to <s>Indra</s>),
5.9ab: <s>saumya</s> (lunar), <s>prājāpatya</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>), and <s>brāhma</s> (of <s>Brahmā</s>)—here [are] fourteen.
5.9cd: When the <s>brāhma</s> [world] is purified, the purification of all this [follows].
5.10ab: After that is the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s> (<s>vaiṣṇava</s>), and then my own (<s>madīya</s>, i.e., of <s>Śiva</s>).
5.10cd: When that is purified, all this becomes purified, without doubt.
5.11ab: Through these five worlds beginning with <s>Kālāgni</s>, O beloved,
5.11cd: when purified, all that is situated within the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) is purified.
5.12ab: Beyond that, the worlds of the hundred <s>Rudras</s>, each separately—
5.12cd: ten should be purified afterward, and one [more] surrounded by their chief.
5.13ab: <s>Ananta</s> is the first among them, <s>Kapālīśa</s> the next,
5.13cd: <s>Agnirudra</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Nairṛta</s>, and <s>Bala</s>.
5.14ab: <s>Śīghra</s>, <s>Nidhīśvara</s>, and <s>Sarvavidyādhipa</s> the next,
5.14cd: <s>Śambhu</s> and <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, resplendent as smokeless flame.
5.15ab: Through these eleven in number, when purified, the hundred are considered purified.
5.15cd: Above and before them are established five groups of eight (<s>aṣṭaka</s>).
5.16ab: <s>Lakulī</s>, <s>Bhārabhūti</s>, <s>Diṇḍhi</s>, <s>Āṣāḍhi</s> with <s>Puṣkara</s>,
5.16cd: <s>Naimiṣa</s>, <s>Prabhāsa</s>, and <s>Amareśa</s>—this is one group of eight.
5.17ab: This is said to pertain to the individual self (<s>pratyātmaka</s>); hence [it is] secret beyond secret.
5.17cd: Therein are <s>Bhairava</s>, <s>Kedāra</s>, and <s>Mahākāla</s> as the middle ones.
5.18ab: <s>Āmrātīkeśa</s>, <s>Jalpeśa</s>, <s>Śrīśaila</s>, together with <s>Harīndava</s>,
5.18cd: <s>Bhīmeśvara</s>, <s>Mahendrāṭṭahāsa</s>, together with <s>Vimaleśvara</s>.
5.19ab: <s>Kanakhala</s>, <s>Nākhala</s>, <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, and <s>Gayā</s>—
5.19cd: this third [group] is secret; now the purificatory [group] is described.
5.20ab: <s>Sthānu</s> and <s>Svarṇākṣa</s> are the first two, <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Gokarṇa</s> the next two,
5.20cd: <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Avimukteśa</s>, <s>Rudrakoṭi</s>, and <s>Ambarāpada</s>.
5.21ab: <s>Sthūla</s>, <s>Sthūleśvara</s>, <s>Śaṅkukarṇa</s>, and <s>Kālañjara</s>,
5.21cd: <s>Maṇḍaleśvara</s>, <s>Mākoṭa</s>, <s>Dviraṇḍa</s>, and <s>Chagalāṇḍaka</s>.
5.22ab: This is declared the group of eight of <s>Sthāṇu</s>, extending up to <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (ego-principle).
5.22cd: The group of eight of the divine wombs (<s>devayoni</s>), [situated] in <s>buddhi</s> (intellect)—hear [it] as proclaimed by me.
5.23ab: The <s>paiśāca</s>, <s>rākṣasa</s>, <s>yākṣa</s>, <s>gāndharva</s>, and <s>aindra</s>,
5.23cd: likewise <s>saumya</s>, <s>prājeśa</s> (of <s>Prajāpati</s>), and <s>brāhma</s> as the eighth.
5.24ab: The group of eight of <s>yoga</s>, [situated] in <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter): therein, the first is <s>Akṛta</s>,
5.24cd: <s>Kṛta</s>, <s>Raibhava</s>, <s>Brāhma</s>, and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> next,
5.25ab: <s>Kaumāra</s>, <s>Auma</s> (of <s>Umā</s>), and <s>Śraikaṇṭha</s>—thus the group of eight of <s>yoga</s>.
5.25cd: In the <s>puruṣa</s> (soul) [principle]: <s>Vāma</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and <s>Ekavīra</s>,
5.26ab: <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>, <s>Umādhava</s>, <s>Aja</s>, and then <s>Ananta</s> and <s>Ekaśiva</s>.
5.26cd: <s>Krodheśa</s> and <s>Caṇḍa</s> in <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge [principle]); <s>Saṃvarta</s> and <s>Jyotis</s> also
5.27ab: in the <s>kalā</s> (activity) <s>tattva</s> (principle) should be known; <s>Surapañcāntaka</s> in the higher [principle].
5.27cd: <s>Ekavīra</s>, <s>Śikhaṇḍīśa</s>, and <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> are situated in the <s>kāla</s> (time [principle]).
5.28ab: Those beginning with <s>Mahātejas</s>, called <s>Maṇḍaleśāna</s>,
5.28cd: are situated in the <s>māyā</s> (illusion) <s>tattva</s>; therein <s>Vāmadeva</s> and <s>Bhavodbhava</s>,
5.29ab: <s>Ekapiṅga</s>, <s>Ikṣaṇeśāna</s>, and <s>Bhuvaneśa</s> leading the rest,
5.29cd: together with <s>Aṅguṣṭhamātra</s> (the thumb-sized one), blazing like the fire of dissolution (<s>kālānala</s>).
5.30ab: In the <s>vidyā-tattva</s> (pure knowledge principle) also, the wise declare five worlds:
5.30cd: therein <s>Hālāhala</s> is the first, <s>Rudra</s>, then <s>Krodha</s> the next,
5.31ab: <s>Ambikā</s>, <s>Aghorā</s>, and <s>Vāmadevī</s> are proclaimed.
5.31cd: In the <s>Īśvara</s> [principle], beginning with <s>Pivana</s>, ending with <s>Aghora</s>, are the <s>Maheśvaras</s>.
5.32ab: <s>Raudrī</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Vāmā</s>, and likewise <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Sadāśiva</s>—
5.32cd: these five worlds in the <s>sakala</s> (complete [level]) the wise know.
5.33ab: Thus in all the <s>tattvas</s>, one hundred and eighteen
5.33cd: worlds should be known, in brief and not in detail.
5.34ab: By this purification, all are purified, without doubt.
5.34cd: For the purification of all paths, the great-minded one
5.35ab: having purified up to the <s>sakala</s> level, should establish <s>yoga</s> in <s>Śiva</s>.
5.35cd: The knower of <s>yoga</s>, desiring enjoyment (<s>bubhukṣu</s>), having meditated on the <s>sakala</s>, should perform <s>yoga</s>.
5.36ab: Thus has been declared by me this path called the [path of] worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>), in my view.

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre pañcamo 'dhikāraḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: atha dehamārgādhikāraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ
body.translated_text: Now the sixth chapter: On the Path of the Body (<s>Dehamārgādhikāra</s>).

body.text:
6.1ab: athāsya vastujātasya yathā dehe vyavasthitiḥ
6.1cd: kriyate jñānadīkṣāsu tathedānīṃ nigadyate
6.2ab: pādādhaḥ pañcabhūtāni vyāptyā dvyaṅgulayā nyaset
6.2cd: dharātattvaṃ ca gulphāntam abādīni tataḥ kramāt
6.3ab: tadvat tundopariṣṭāt tu parvaṣaṭkāvasānakam
6.3cd: puṃstattvāt kalātattvāntaṃ tattvaṣaṭkaṃ vicintayet
6.4ab: tato māyāditattvāni catvāri susamāhitaḥ
6.4cd: caturaṅgulayā vyāptyā sakalāntāni bhāvayet
6.5ab: śivatattvaṃ tataḥ paścāt tejorūpam anākulam
6.5cd: sarveṣāṃ vyāpakatvena sabāhyābhyantaraṃ smaret
6.6ab: ṣaṭtriṃśattattvabhedena nyāso 'yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ
6.6cd: adhunā pañca tattvāni yathā dehe tathocyate
6.7ab: nābher ūrdhvaṃ tu yāvat syāt parvaṣaṭkam anukramāt
6.7cd: dharātattvena gulphāntaṃ vyāptaṃ śeṣam ihāmbunā
6.8ab: dvāviṃśatiś ca parvāṇi tadūrdhvaṃ tejasāvṛtam
6.8cd: tasmād dvādaśa parvāṇi vāyuvyāptir udāhṛtā
6.9ab: ākāśāntaṃ paraṃ śāntaṃ sarveṣāṃ vyāpakaṃ smaret
6.9cd: śaktyādipañcakhaṇḍādhvavidhiṣv apy evam iṣyate
6.10ab: trikhaṇḍe kaṇṭhaparyantam ātmatattvam udāhṛtam
6.10cd: vidyātattvam atordhvaṃ ca śivatattvaṃ tu pūrvavat
6.11ab: evaṃ tattvavidhiḥ prokto bhuvanādhvā tathocyate
6.11cd: kālāgner vīrabhadrāntaṃ puraṣoḍaśakaṃ tataḥ
6.12ab: gulphāntaṃ vinyased dhyātvā yathāvad anupūrvaśaḥ
6.12cd: tasmād ekāṅgulavyāptyā lakulīśāditaḥ kramāt
6.13ab: vinyaset tu dviraṇḍāntaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ chagalāṇḍakam
6.13cd: tataḥ pādāṅgulavyāptyā devayogāṣṭakaṃ pṛthak
6.14ab: tato 'py ardhāṅgulavyāptyā puraṣaṭkam anukramāt
6.14cd: catuṣkaṃ tu dvaye 'nyasminn ekam ekatra cintayet
6.15ab: uttarādikramād dvyekabhedo vidyādike traye
6.15cd: kāle pratyekam uddiṣṭam ekaikaṃ tu yathākramaṃ
6.16ab: maṇḍalādhipatīnāṃ tu vyāptir ardhāṅgulā matā
6.16cd: tribhāganyūnaparvākhyā tritayasya tathopari
6.17ab: dvitayasya ca saṃpūrṇā pañcakaṃ samudāhṛtam
6.17cd: aṣṭakaṃ pañcakaṃ cānyad evam eva vilakṣayet
6.18ab: bhuvanādhvavidhāv atra pūrvavac cintayec chivam
6.18cd: padāni dvividhāny atra vargavidyāvibhedataḥ
6.19ab: teṣāṃ tanmantravad vyāptir yathedānīṃ tathā śṛṇu
6.19cd: caturaṅgulam ādyaṃ tu dve cānye 'ṣṭāṅgule pṛthak
6.20ab: daśāṅgulāni trīṇy asmād ekaṃ pañcadaśāṅgulam
6.20cd: caturbhir adhikaiś cānyad vyāpakaṃ navamaṃ mahat
6.21ab: ūnaviṃśatike bhede padānāṃ vyāptir ucyate
6.21cd: ekaikaṃ dvyaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ tatra pūrvaṃ padatrayam
6.22ab: aṣṭāṅgulāni catvāri daśāṅgulam ataḥ param
6.22cd: dvyaṅgule dve pade cānye ṣaḍaṅgulam ataḥ param
6.23ab: dvādaśāṅgulam anyac ca dve 'nye pañcāṅgule pṛthak
6.23cd: padadvayaṃ catuṣparva tathānye dve dviparvaṇī
6.24ab: vyāpakaṃ padam anyac ca pūrvavat parikīrtitaṃ
6.24cd: aparo 'yaṃ vidhiḥ proktaḥ parāparam ataḥ śṛṇu
6.25ab: pūrvavat pṛthivītattvaṃ vijñeyaṃ caturaṅgulam
6.25cd: sārdhadvyaṅgulamānāni dhiṣaṇāntāni lakṣayet
6.26ab: pradhānaṃ tryaṅgulaṃ jñeyaṃ śeṣaṃ pūrvavad ādiśet
6.26cd: pare 'pi pūrvavat pṛthvī tryaṅgulāny aparāṇi ca
6.27ab: catuṣparva pradhānaṃ ca śeṣaṃ pūrvavad āśrayet
6.27cd: dvividho 'pi hi varṇānāṃ ṣaḍvidho bheda ucyate
6.28ab: tattvamārgavidhānena jñātavyaḥ paramārthataḥ
6.28cd: padamantrakalādīnāṃ pūrvasūtrānusārataḥ
6.29ab: tritayatvaṃ prakurvīta tattvavarṇoktavartmanā
6.29cd: itthaṃ bhūtaśarīrasya guruṇā śivamūrtinā
6.30ab: prakartavyā vidhānena dīkṣā sarvaphalapradā
body.translated_text:
(6.1) Now, how the arrangement of these categories of reality (<s>tattva</s>s) is made upon the body in the initiations of knowledge (<s>jñāna-dīkṣā</s>) — that is now described.
