(6.2) Below the feet, one should place the five elements (<s>bhūta</s>s) with a pervasion of two finger-breadths [each]. The earth-<s>tattva</s> extends up to the ankles, and then the rest in order upward.
(6.3) Likewise, above the navel, extending through six joints, one should contemplate the group of six <s>tattva</s>s from <s>puṃs-tattva</s> (the individual soul principle) to <s>kalā-tattva</s> (the principle of limited agency).
(6.4) Then, with focused mind, one should visualize the four <s>tattva</s>s beginning with <s>Māyā</s>, ending with <s>Sakala</s>, with a pervasion of four finger-breadths [each].
(6.5) After that, the <s>Śiva-tattva</s>, luminous in form, unperturbed — one should contemplate it as pervading all, both externally and internally.
(6.6) This <s>nyāsa</s> (placement) has been described according to the thirty-six <s>tattva</s> divisions. Now the five <s>tattva</s>s and how they [are placed] on the body is stated.
(6.7) Above the navel, up to six joints in sequence — [this area] is pervaded by the earth-<s>tattva</s> up to the ankles; the remainder here by water.
(6.8) Twenty-two joints above that are enveloped by fire; from that, twelve joints are declared as the pervasion of wind.
(6.9) The rest, ending with <s>ākāśa</s> (space), supreme and peaceful, one should contemplate as pervading all. In the procedures of the fivefold path beginning with <s>Śakti</s>, this same [arrangement] is accepted.
(6.10) In the threefold [division], up to the throat is declared as <s>ātma-tattva</s> (the self-principle); above that is <s>vidyā-tattva</s> (the knowledge-principle); and <s>Śiva-tattva</s> is as before.
(6.11) Thus the method of <s>tattva</s>s has been explained. Now the path of worlds (<s>bhuvana-adhvan</s>) is likewise described. From <s>Kālāgni</s> to <s>Vīrabhadra</s>, sixteen worlds —
(6.12) these one should place [on the body] up to the ankles, meditating properly in due sequence. From that, with a pervasion of one finger-breadth, beginning from <s>Lakulīśa</s>, in order,
(6.13) one should place [worlds] up to two egg[-shaped regions]; the <s>Chagalāṇḍaka</s> (Goat's Egg [world]) is three finger-breadths. Then, with a pervasion of one toe-breadth, the eight <s>Devayoga</s>s separately;
(6.14) then with a pervasion of half a finger-breadth, six worlds in sequence. Four [worlds] in two [groups], in another one each — one should contemplate.
(6.15) In the order beginning from the north, the division of two and one [applies] in the three [levels] beginning with <s>Vidyā</s>. In [the path of] time (<s>kāla</s>), each is indicated singly, one by one in sequence.
(6.16) The pervasion of the lords of the <s>maṇḍala</s>s (circles) is considered to be half a finger-breadth. [The pervasion] designated as a joint minus one-third [applies] to the [next] three above;
(6.17) and for the two [above that], a full [joint]; the group of five is thus declared. Another group of eight and group of five should be similarly distinguished.
(6.18) In this procedure of the path of worlds (<s>bhuvana-adhvan</s>), one should contemplate <s>Śiva</s> as before. The <s>pada</s>s (words/stages) here are of two kinds, according to the division of <s>varga</s> (group) and <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).
(6.19) Their pervasion is like that of their respective <s>mantra</s>s — now listen to how it is. The first is four finger-breadths; two others are each eight finger-breadths separately;
(6.20) three [more] are ten finger-breadths each; one is fifteen finger-breadths; and another, exceeding by four, is the ninth, great and all-pervading.
(6.21) In the division of nineteen, the pervasion of the <s>pada</s>s is stated: the first three <s>pada</s>s should be known as two finger-breadths each;
(6.22) four [are] eight finger-breadths; beyond that, ten finger-breadths; two other <s>pada</s>s are two finger-breadths; beyond that, six finger-breadths;
(6.23) another is twelve finger-breadths; two others are five finger-breadths separately; a pair of <s>pada</s>s spans four joints; likewise two others span two joints each;
(6.24) and another <s>pada</s>, the all-pervading, is declared as before. This is the other method that has been expounded; now listen to the <s>parāpara</s> (supreme-non-supreme [method]).
(6.25) As before, the earth-<s>tattva</s> should be known as four finger-breadths. Those ending with <s>dhiṣaṇā</s> (intellect) should be measured at two and a half finger-breadths each.
(6.26) <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial nature) should be known as three finger-breadths; the rest should be assigned as before. In the other [method] also, earth is as before; the others are three finger-breadths;
(6.27) <s>Pradhāna</s> spans four joints; the rest should be followed as before. The division of <s>varṇa</s>s (letters/phonemes), though twofold, is said to be sixfold.
(6.28) It should be understood in the highest sense according to the arrangement of the <s>tattva</s>-path. Following the previous rules regarding <s>pada</s>s, <s>mantra</s>s, <s>kalā</s>s, and the rest,
(6.29) one should establish the threefold [division] according to the path described for <s>tattva</s>s and <s>varṇa</s>s. Thus, for the body [of the initiate] so constituted, by the <s>guru</s> (teacher) who is the embodiment of <s>Śiva</s>,
(6.30) the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), which bestows all fruits, should be performed according to the prescribed method.

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre dehamārgādhikāraḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixth chapter, on the path of the body (<s>dehamārgādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottaratantra</s>.

body.text: mudrādhikāraḥ saptamaḥ
body.translated_text: The Seventh Chapter: On <s>Mudrās</s> (Ritual Gestures) (<s>Mudrādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
7.1ab: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi mudrākhyāḥ śivaśaktayaḥ
7.1cd: yābhiḥ saṃrakṣito mantrī mantrasiddhim avāpnuyāt
7.2ab: triśūlaṃ ca tathā padmaṃ śaktiś cakraṃ savajrakam
7.2cd: daṇḍadaṃṣṭre mahāpretā mahāmudrā khageśvarī
7.3ab: mahodayā karālā ca khaṭvāṅgaṃ sakapālakam
7.3cd: halaṃ pāśāṅkuśā ghaṇṭā mudgaras triśikho 'paraḥ
7.4ab: āvāhasthāpanīrodhā dravyadā natir eva ca
7.4cd: amṛtā yogamudreti vijñeyā vīravandite
7.5ab: tarjanīmadhyamānāmā dakṣiṇasya prasāritāḥ
7.5cd: kaṇiṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakākrāntās triśūlaṃ parikīrtitam
7.6ab: padmākārau karau kṛtvā padmamudrāṃ pradarśayet
7.6cd: saṃmukhau prasṛtau kṛtvā karāv antaritāṅgulī
7.7ab: prasṛte madhyame lagne kaumāryāḥ śaktir iṣyate
7.7cd: uttānavāmamuṣṭes tu dakṣa[6]
7.8ab: [4] kṣipen muṣṭiṃ cakraṃ nārāyaṇīpriyam
7.8cd: uttānavāmakasyordhvaṃ nyased dakṣam adhomukham
7.9ab: kaniṣṭhāṅguṣṭhakau śliṣṭau śeṣāḥ syur maṇibandhagā
7.9cd: vajramudreti vikhyātā aindrīsaṃtoṣakārikā
7.10ab: ūrdhvaprasārito muṣṭir dakṣiṇo 'ṅguṣṭhagarbhagaḥ
7.10cd: daṇḍamudreti vikhyātā vaivasvatakulapriyā
7.11ab: vāmato vaktragāṃ kuryād vāmamuṣṭeḥ kaniṣṭhikām
7.11cd: daṃṣṭreyaṃ kīrtitā devi cāmuṇḍākulanandinī
7.12ab: vāmajānugataṃ pādaṃ but hastau pṛṣṭhapralambinau
7.12cd: vikṛte locane grīvā bhagnā jihvā prasāritā
7.13ab: sarvayogigaṇasyeṣṭā pretā yogīśvarī matā
7.13cd: hastāv adhomukhau padbhyāṃ hṛdayāntaṃ nayed budhaḥ
7.14ab: tiryag mukhāntam upari saṃmukhāv ūrdhvagau nayet
7.14cd: mahāmudreti vikhyātā dehaśodhanakarmaṇi
7.15ab: sarvakarmakarī caiṣā yogināṃ yogasiddhaye
7.15cd: baddhvā padmāsanaṃ yogī nābhāv akṣeśvaraṃ nyaset
7.16ab: daṇḍākāraṃ tu taṃ tāvan nayed yāvat kakhatrayam
7.16cd: nigṛhya tatra tat tūrṇaṃ prerayet khatrayeṇa tu
7.17ab: etāṃ baddhvā mahāvīraḥ khe gatiṃ pratipadyate
7.17cd: adhomukhasya dakṣasya vāmam uttānam ūrdhvataḥ
7.18ab: anāmāmadhyame tasya vāmāṅguṣṭhena pīḍayet
7.18cd: tarjanyā tatkaniṣṭhāṃ ca tarjanīṃ ca kaniṣṭhayā
7.19ab: madhyamānāmikābhyāṃ ca tadaṅguṣṭhaṃ nipīḍayet
7.19cd: mudrā mahodayākhyeyaṃ mahodayakarī nṛṇām
7.20ab: anāmikākaniṣṭhābhyāṃ sṛkviṇyau pravidārayet
7.20cd: jihvāṃ ca lālayen mantrī hāhākāraṃ ca kārayet
7.21ab: kruddhadṛṣṭiḥ karāleyaṃ mudrā duṣṭabhayaṅkarī
7.21cd: vāmaskandhagato vāma muṣṭir ucchritatarjanī
7.22ab: khaṭvāṅgākhyā smṛtā mudrā kapālam adhunā śṛṇu
7.22cd: nimnaṃ pāṇitalaṃ dakṣam īṣat saṃkucitāṅguli
7.23ab: kapālam iti vijñeyam adhunā halam ucyate
7.23cd: muṣṭibaddhasya dakṣasya tarjanī vāmamuṣṭinā
7.24ab: vakratarjaninā grastā halamudreti kīrtitā
7.24cd: muṣṭyā pṛṣṭhagayor dakṣa vāmayos tarjanīdvayam
7.25ab: vāmāṅguṣṭhāgrasaṃlagnaṃ pāśaḥ prasṛtakuñcitaḥ
7.25cd: hale muṣṭir yathā vāmo dakṣahīnas tathāṅkuśaḥ
7.26ab: adhomukhasthite vāme dakṣiṇāṃ tarjanīṃ budhaḥ
7.26cd: cālayen madhyadeśasthāṃ ghaṇṭāmudrā priyā matā
7.27ab: karāv ūrdhvamukhau kāryāv anyonyāntaritāṅgulī
7.27cd: anāme madhyapṛṣṭhasthe tarjanyau mūlaparvage
7.28ab: madhyame dve yute kārye kaniṣṭhe puruṣāvadhi
7.28cd: tarjanyau madhyapārśvasthe virale parikalpite
7.29ab: mudgaras triśikho hy eṣa kṣaṇād āveśakārakaḥ
7.29cd: karābhyām añjaliṃ kṛtvā anāmāmūlaparvagau
7.30ab: aṅguṣṭhau kalpayed vidvān mantrāvāhanakarmaṇi
7.30cd: muṣṭī dvāv unnatāṅguṣṭhau sthāpanī parikīrtitā
7.31ab: dvāv eva garbhagāṅguṣṭhau vijñeyā saṃnirodhinī
7.31cd: dravyadā tu samākhyātā [4]tra saṃmukhī
7.32ab: hṛdaye saṃmukhau hastau saṃlagnau prasṛtāṅgulī
7.32cd: namaskṛtir iyaṃ mudrā mantravandanakarmaṇi
7.33ab: anyonyāntaritāḥ sarvāḥ karayor aṅgulīḥ sthitāḥ
7.33cd: kaniṣṭhāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ vāme 'nāmikāgre niyojayet
7.34ab: dakṣiṇe ca tathā vāmaṃ tarjanīmadhyame tathā
7.34cd: aṅguṣṭhau madhyamūlasthau mudreyam amṛtaprabhā
7.35ab: dakṣiṇaṃ nābhimūle tu vāmasyopari saṃsthitam
7.35cd: tarjanyaṅguṣṭhakau lagnau ucchritau yogakarmaṇi
7.36ab: evaṃ mudrāgaṇaṃ mantrī badhnīyad dhṛdaye budhaḥ
7.36cd: sarvāsāṃ vācakāś cāsāṃ oṃ hrīṃ nāma tato namaḥ
body.translated_text:
(7.1) Now I shall expound the powers of <s>Śiva</s> called <s>mudrā</s>s (ritual hand-gestures), by which the <s>mantrī</s> (mantra-practitioner), being protected, may attain <s>mantra-siddhi</s> (perfection in mantra).
(7.2) The <s>triśūla</s> (trident), the <s>padma</s> (lotus), the <s>śakti</s> (spear), the <s>cakra</s> (discus) together with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), the <s>daṇḍa</s> (staff), the <s>daṃṣṭrā</s> (fang), the <s>mahāpretā</s> (great corpse), the <s>mahāmudrā</s> (great seal), the <s>khageśvarī</s> (queen of the sky),
(7.3) the <s>mahodayā</s> (great arising), the <s>karālā</s> (terrifying), the <s>khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) together with the <s>kapāla</s> (skull-bowl), the <s>hala</s> (plough), the <s>pāśa</s> (noose), the <s>aṅkuśa</s> (goad), the <s>ghaṇṭā</s> (bell), the <s>mudgara</s> (mace), and another called <s>triśikha</s> (three-crested),
(7.4) the <s>āvāha</s> (invocation), the <s>sthāpanī</s> (establishment), the <s>nirodha</s> (restraint), the <s>dravyadā</s> (substance-giving), <s>nati</s> (salutation) itself, <s>amṛtā</s> (the immortal), and <s>yogamudrā</s> (the yoga-seal) — these should be known, O you who are worshipped by heroes.
(7.5) The index, middle, and ring fingers of the right hand are extended, [while] the little finger and thumb are pressed together — this is declared as the <s>triśūla</s> (trident) [mudrā].
(7.6) Making the hands in the form of a lotus, one should display the <s>padma-mudrā</s> (lotus seal). Making both hands face each other, extended, with interlaced fingers,
(7.7) with the middle fingers extended and joined — this is considered the <s>śakti</s> (spear) of <s>Kaumārī</s>. With the left fist turned upward, the right...
(7.8) ...one should cast the fist — [this is] the <s>cakra</s> (discus), dear to <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>. Above the upturned left [hand], one should place the right hand face-down.
(7.9) The little finger and thumb are joined; the rest [of the fingers] should reach the wrist — this is known as the <s>vajra-mudrā</s> (thunderbolt seal), which delights <s>Aindrī</s>.
(7.10) The right fist extended upward, with the thumb enclosed within — this is known as the <s>daṇḍa-mudrā</s> (staff seal), dear to the family of <s>Vaivasvata</s> (<s>Yama</s>).
(7.11) One should bring the little finger of the left fist toward the mouth from the left side — this is declared as the <s>daṃṣṭrā</s> (fang [mudrā]), O Goddess, the delight of the clan of <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>.
(7.12) The [left] foot placed upon the left knee, both hands hanging behind the back, the eyes distorted, the neck broken [bent], the tongue protruding —
(7.13) desired by the entire assembly of <s>yogin</s>s, this is considered the <s>Pretā</s> (corpse [mudrā]), belonging to <s>Yogīśvarī</s>. The wise one should bring both hands face-down from the feet up to the heart;
(7.14) then diagonally to the face, then turning them upward, facing each other, moving upward — this is known as the <s>Mahāmudrā</s> (Great Seal), [used] in the act of purifying the body.
(7.15) This [mudrā] accomplishes all actions for <s>yogin</s>s, for the attainment of <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic perfection). Having assumed <s>padmāsana</s> (the lotus posture), the <s>yogin</s> should place <s>Akṣeśvara</s> (the Lord of the senses) at the navel;
(7.16) he should lead it upward in a staff-like form as far as the three openings (<s>kha-traya</s>). Having restrained [it] there, he should quickly propel [it] through the three openings.
(7.17) Having bound this [mudrā], the great hero attains movement through space. With the right hand face-down and the left hand face-up above it,
(7.18) one should press the ring and middle fingers [of the right hand] with the left thumb, and its little finger with the index, and the index with the little finger;
(7.19) and with the middle and ring fingers one should press its thumb — this <s>mudrā</s> is called <s>Mahodayā</s> (Great Arising), producing great prosperity for humans.
(7.20) With the ring and little fingers one should widen the corners of the mouth, and the <s>mantrī</s> should loll the tongue and make the exclamation 'hā hā!'
(7.21) With a furious gaze — this is the <s>Karālā</s> (Terrifying) <s>mudrā</s>, causing fear in the wicked. The left fist placed on the left shoulder, with the index finger raised —
(7.22) this is known as the <s>Khaṭvāṅga</s> (skull-staff) <s>mudrā</s>. Now hear about the <s>Kapāla</s> (skull-bowl): the right palm [held] concave, with slightly curled fingers —
(7.23) this should be known as the <s>Kapāla</s> (skull-bowl). Now the <s>Hala</s> (plough) is described: the index finger of the right fist, [grasped] by the left fist,
(7.24) seized by the bent index finger [of the left hand] — this is declared as the <s>Hala-mudrā</s> (plough seal). With both right and left fists held behind the back, the two index fingers
(7.25) joined to the tip of the left thumb, extended and curved — [this is] the <s>Pāśa</s> (noose). In the plough, [if] the left fist is as described but without the right — that is the <s>Aṅkuśa</s> (goad).
(7.26) With the left hand held face-down, the wise one should shake the right index finger, placed in the middle — this is considered the beloved <s>Ghaṇṭā-mudrā</s> (bell seal).
(7.27) Both hands should be made face-up, with fingers interlaced alternately; the ring fingers placed on the back of the middle fingers, the index fingers reaching the base-joint;
(7.28) the two middle fingers should be made joined, the little fingers up to [the level of] a man's [thumbs]; the index fingers placed at the sides of the middle fingers, arranged with gaps —
(7.29) this is the <s>Mudgara Triśikha</s> (three-crested mace), which instantly causes possession. Making an <s>añjali</s> (joined-palms gesture) with both hands, with the thumbs placed at the base-joint of the ring fingers —
(7.30) the learned one should fashion [this] in the act of invoking <s>mantra</s>s. Two fists with thumbs raised upward — this is declared as <s>Sthāpanī</s> (the establishing [mudrā]).
(7.31) The same two [fists] with thumbs enclosed within — this should be known as <s>Saṃnirodhinī</s> (the restraining [mudrā]). The <s>Dravyadā</s> (substance-giving) is declared as... with hands facing each other.
(7.32) Both hands at the heart, facing each other, joined with extended fingers — this <s>mudrā</s> is <s>Namaskṛti</s> (salutation), [used] in the act of venerating <s>mantra</s>s.
(7.33) All the fingers of both hands are placed alternately interlaced; the right little finger should be placed at the tip of the left ring finger;
(7.34) and likewise the left [little finger] on the right; similarly the index and middle fingers; the thumbs placed at the base of the middle fingers — this <s>mudrā</s> has the radiance of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar).
(7.35) The right [hand] at the root of the navel, situated above the left; the index finger and thumb joined and raised upward — [this is used] in the act of <s>yoga</s>.
(7.36) Thus the wise <s>mantrī</s> should bind this group of <s>mudrā</s>s at the heart. And the invocation for all of them is: 'Oṃ hrīṃ, salutation, then namaḥ.'

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre mudrādhikāro saptamaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventh chapter, on <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text:
8.1ab: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi yajanaṃ sarvakāmadam
8.1cd: yasya darśanamātreṇa yoginīsaṃmato bhavet
8.2ab: tatrādau yāgasadanaṃ śubhe kṣetre manoramam
8.2cd: kārayed agnikuṇḍena vartulena samanvitam
8.3ab: pañcaviṃśatiparveṇa samantād ardhanābhinā
8.3cd: turyāṃśamekhalenāpi parvauṣṭhena suśobhinā
8.4ab: tataḥ snātvā jitadvandvo bhāvasnānena mantravit
8.4cd: tac ca ṣaḍvidham uddiṣṭaṃ bhasmasnānādyanukramāt
8.5ab: bhasmasnānaṃ mahāstreṇa bhasma saptābhimantritam
8.5cd: malasnānāya saṃhārakrameṇoddhūlayet tanum
8.6ab: vidyāṅgaiḥ pañcabhiḥ paścāc chiraḥ prabhṛti guṇṭhayet
8.6cd: abhiṣekaṃ tu kurvīta mūlenaiva ṣaḍaṅginā
8.7ab: tato 'vāsāḥ suvāsā ca hastau pādau ca dhāvayet
8.7cd: ācamya mārjanaṃ kuryād vidyayā bhūrivarṇayā
8.8ab: nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tu sāmānyām aghamarṣaṃ dvitīyayā
8.8cd: upasthānaṃ ca mālinyā japec caikākṣarāṃ parām
8.9ab: jalasnāne 'pi cāstreṇa mṛdaṃ saptābhimantritam
8.9cd: pūrvavat tanum ālabhya malasnānaṃ samācaret
8.10ab: vidhisnānādikaṃ cātra pūrvavat kiṃ tu vāriṇā
8.10cd: sādhāraṇavidhisnāto vidyātritayamantritam
8.11ab: toyaṃ vinikṣipen mūrdhni mantrasnānāya mantravit
8.11cd: rajasā godhutenaiva vāyavyaṃ snānam ācaret
8.12ab: mahāstram uccaran gacched dhyānayuk padasaptakam
8.12cd: tad eva punar āgacched anusmṛtya parāparām
8.13ab: varṣātapasamāyogād divyo .apy evaṃvidho mataḥ
8.13cd: kiṃ tu tatra parāṃ mantrī sravantīm amṛtaṃ smaret
8.14ab: astreṇāṅguṣṭhamūlāt tu vahnim utthāpya nirdahet
8.14cd: svatanuṃ plāvayet paścāt parayaivāmṛtena tu
8.15ab: sūryādau mantram ādāya gacched astram anusmaran
8.15cd: yāgaveśmāstrasaṃśuddhaṃ viśec chucir anākulaḥ
8.16ab: tatra dvārapatīn pūjya mahāstreṇābhimantritam
8.16cd: puṣpaṃ vinikṣiped dhyātvā jvaladvighnapraśāntaye
8.17ab: daśasv api tato 'streṇa dikṣu saṃkalpya rakṣaṇaṃ
8.17cd: praviśed yāgasadanaṃ vahnivad vahnisaṃyutam
8.18ab: pūrvāsyaḥ saumyavaktro vā viśeṣanyāsam ārabhet
8.18cd: tatrādāv astramantreṇa kālānalasamatviṣā
8.19ab: aṅguṣṭhāgrāt tanuṃ dagdhāṃ sabāhyābhyantarāṃ smaret
8.19cd: vikīryamāṇaṃ tadbhasma dhyātvā kavacavāyunā
8.20ab: śivabindusamākāram ātmānam anucintayet
8.20cd: tato 'sya yojayec chaktiṃ so 'ham ity aparājitaḥ
8.21ab: vidyāmūrtiṃ tato dadhyān mantreṇānena śāṅkari
8.21cd: daṇḍākrāntaṃ mahāprāṇaṃ daṇḍārūḍhaṃ sanābhikam
8.22ab: nitambaṃ tadadhastāc ca vāmastanam adhaḥ punaḥ
8.22cd: kaṇṭhaṃ ca vāmaśikharaṃ vāmamudrāvibhūṣitam
8.23ab: bindvardhacandrakhaṃ nādaśaktibinduvibhūṣitam
8.23cd: eṣa piṇḍakaro devi navātmaka iti śrutaḥ
8.24ab: sarvasiddhikaraś cāyaṃ sarahasyam udāhṛtaḥ
8.24cd: eṣa tryarṇojjhito .adhastād dīrghaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ svarair yutaḥ
8.25ab: ṣaḍaṅgāni hṛdādīni jātibhedena kalpayet
8.25cd: kṣayaravalabījaiś ca dīptair binduvibhūṣitaiḥ
8.26ab: vaktrāṇi kalpayet pūrvam ūrdhvavaktrāditaḥ kramāt
8.26cd: pratyaṅgavidhisiddhyarthaṃ lalāṭādiṣv atho nyaset
8.27ab: a lalāṭe dvitīyaṃ ca vaktre saṃparikalpayet
8.27cd: i ī netradvaye dattvā u ū karṇadvaye nyaset
8.28ab: ṛ .R nāsāpuṭe tadvad ḷ .L gaṇḍadvaye tathā
8.28cd: e ai adhordhvadanteṣu o-aukārau tathoṣṭhayoḥ
8.29ab: aṃ śikhāyāṃ visargeṇa jihvāṃ saṃparikalpayet
8.29cd: dakṣiṇaskandhadordaṇḍa karāṅgulinakheṣu ca
8.30ab: kavargaṃ vinyased vāme tadvac cādyam anukramāt
8.30cd: ṭatādyau pūrvavad vargau nitamborvādiṣu nyaset
8.31ab: pādyaṃ pārśvadvaye pṛṣṭhe jaṭhare hṛdy anukramāt
8.31cd: tvagraktamāṃsasūtreṣu yavargaṃ parikalpayet
8.32ab: śādyam asthivasāśukraprāṇakopeṣu pañcakam
8.32cd: mūrtyaṅgāni tato dattvā śivam āvāhayed budhaḥ
8.33ab: prāṇopari nyasen nābhiṃ tadūrdhve dakṣiṇāṅgulim
8.33cd: vāmakarṇaprameyotaḥ sarvasiddhipradaḥ śivaḥ
8.34ab: sadbhāvaḥ paramo hy eṣaḥ bhairavasya mahātmanaḥ
8.34cd: aṅgāny anena kāryāṇi pūrvavat svarabhedataḥ
8.35ab: mūrtiḥ sṛṣṭis tritattvaṃ ca aṣṭau mūrtyaṅgasaṃyutāḥ
8.35cd: śivaḥ sāṅgaś ca ṣoḍhaiva nyāsaḥ saṃparikīrtitaḥ
8.36ab: asyopari tataḥ śāktaṃ kuryān nyāsaṃ yathā śṛṇu
8.36cd: mūrtau parāparāṃ nyasya tadvaktrāṇi ca mālinīm
8.37ab: parāditritayaṃ paścāc chikhāhṛtpādagaṃ nyaset
8.37cd: kavaktrakaṇṭhahṛnnābhiguhyorūpādagaṃ kramāt
8.38ab: aghoryādyaṣṭakaṃ nyasya vidyāṅgāni tu pūrvavat
8.38cd: tatas tv āvāhayec chaktiṃ sarvayoginamaskṛtām
8.39ab: jīvaḥ prāṇapuṭāntasthaḥ kālānalasamadyutiḥ
8.39cd: atidīptas tu vāmāṅghribhūṣito mūrdhni bindunā
8.40ab: dakṣajānuyutaś cāyaṃ sarvamātṛgaṇānvitaḥ
8.40cd: anena prīṇitāḥ sarvā dadate vāñchitaṃ phalam
8.41ab: sadbhāvaḥ paramo hy eṣa mātṛṇāṃ paripaṭhyate
8.41cd: tasmād enāṃ japen mantrī ya icchet siddhim uttamām
8.42ab: rudraśaktisamāveśo nityam atra pratiṣṭhitaḥ
8.42cd: yasmād eṣā parāśaktir bhedenānena kīrtitā
8.43ab: yāvatyaḥ siddhayas tantre sarvāḥ syur anayā kṛtāḥ
8.43cd: aṅgāni kalpayed asyāḥ pūrvavat svarabhedataḥ
8.44ab: mūrtiḥ savaktrā śaktiś ca vidyātritaya eva ca
8.44cd: aghoryādyaṣṭakaṃ ceti tathā vidyāṅgapañcakam
8.45ab: sāṅgāś caiva parā śaktir nyāsaḥ prokto .atha ṣaḍvidhaḥ
8.45cd: yāmalo 'yam ato nyāsaḥ sarvasiddhiprasiddhaye
8.46ab: vāmo vāyaṃ vidhiḥ kāryo muktimārgāvalambibhiḥ
8.46cd: varṇamantravibhedena pṛthag vā tatphalārthibhiḥ
8.47ab: yāvantaḥ kīrtitā bhedaiḥ śaṃbhuśaktyaṇuvācakāḥ
8.47cd: tāvatsv apy evam evāyaṃ nyāsaḥ pañcavidho mataḥ
8.48ab: kiṃ tu bāhyas tu yo yatra sa tatrāṅgasamanvitaḥ
8.48cd: ṣaṣṭhaḥ syād iti sarvatra ṣoḍhaivāyam udāhṛtaḥ
8.49ab: svānuṣṭhānāvirodhena bhāvābhāvavikalpanaiḥ
8.49cd: yāgadravyāṇi sarvāṇi kāryāṇi vidhivad budhaiḥ
8.50ab: tato 'rghapātram ādāya bhāvābhāvavikalpitam
8.50cd: tataś cāstrāgnisaṃdagdhaṃ śaktyambuplāvitaṃ śuci
8.51ab: kartavyā yasya saṃśuddhir anyasyāpy atra vastunaḥ
8.51cd: tasyānenaiva mārgeṇa prakartavyā vijānatā
8.52ab: na cāsaṃśodhitaṃ vastu kiñcid apy atra kalpayet
8.52cd: tena śuddhaṃ tu sarvaṃ yad aśuddham api tac chuci
8.53ab: tad ambunā samāpūrya ṣaḍbhir aṅgaiḥ samarpya ca
8.53cd: amṛtīkṛtya sarvāṇi tena dravyāṇi śodhayet
8.54ab: ātmānaṃ pūjayitvā tu kuryād antaḥkṛtiṃ yathā
8.54cd: tathā te kathayiṣyāmi sarvayogigaṇārcite
8.55ab: ādāvauāv ādhāraśaktiṃ tu nābhyadhaś caturaṅgulām
8.55cd: dharāṃ surodaṃ potaṃ ca kandaś ceti catuṣṭayam
8.56ab: ekaikāṅgulam etat syāc chūlasyāmalasārakam
8.56cd: tato nālam anantākhyaṃ daṇḍam asya prakalpayet
8.57ab: lambikāvadhitaś cātra śūlordhvaṃ granthir iṣyate
8.57cd: abhittvainaṃ mahādevi pāśajālamahārṇavam
8.58ab: na sa yogam avāpnoti śivena saha mānavaḥ
8.58cd: dharmaṃ jñānaṃ ca vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ ca catuṣṭayam
8.59ab: koṇeṣu cintayen mantrī āgneyādiṣv anukramāt
8.59cd: gātrakāṇāṃ catuṣkaṃ ca dikṣu pūrvādiṣu smaret
8.60ab: granther ūrdhvaṃ triśūlādho bhavitavyā catuṣkikā
8.60cd: vidyātattvaṃ tad evāhuś chadanatrayasaṃyutam
8.61ab: kakhalambikayor madhye tat tattvam anucintayet
8.61cd: padmākṛti kakhatattvam aiśvaraṃ cintayed budhaḥ
8.62ab: karṇikākesaropetaṃ sabījaṃ vikasat sitam
8.62cd: pūrvapatrāditaḥ paścād vāmādinavakaṃ nyaset
8.63ab: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca kālī ceti tathā parā
8.63cd: kalavikaraṇī caiva balavikaraṇī tathā
8.64ab: balapramathanī cānyā sarvabhūtadamany api
8.64cd: manonmanī ca madhye 'pi bhānumārgeṇa vinyaset
8.65ab: vibhvādinavakaṃ cānyad vilomāt parikalpayet
8.65cd: vibhur jñānī kriyā cecchā vāgīśī jvālinī tathā
8.66ab: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrī ca sarvāḥ kālānalaprabhāḥ
8.66cd: brahmaviṣṇuharāḥ pūrvaṃ ye śāktāḥ pratipāditāḥ
8.67ab: dalakesaramadhyasthā maṇḍalānāṃ ta īśvarāḥ
8.67cd: dhvani [?] cārkenduvahnīnāṃ saṃjñeyā paribhāvayet
8.68ab: īśvaraṃ ca mahāpretaṃ prahasantaṃ sacetanam
8.68cd: kālāgnikoṭivapuṣam ity evaṃ sarvam āsanam
8.69ab: tasya nābhyutthitaṃ śaktiśūlaśṛṅgatrayaṃ smaret
8.69cd: kakhatrayeṇa niryātaṃ dvādaśāntāvasānakam
8.70ab: cintayet tasya śṛṅgeṣu śāktaṃ padmatrayaṃ tataḥ
8.70cd: sarvādhiṣṭhāyakaṃ śuklamām ity etat paramāsanam
8.71ab: tatropari tato mūrtiṃ vidyākhyām anucintayet
8.71cd: ātmākhyāṃ ca tatas tasyāṃ pūrvanyāsaṃ śivātmakam
8.72ab: tato madhye parāṃ śaktiṃ dakṣiṇottarayor dvayam
8.72cd: parāparāṃ svarūpeṇa raktavarṇāṃ mahābalām
8.73ab: icchārūpadharāṃ dhyātvā kiṃ cid ugrāṃ na bhīṣaṇām
8.73cd: aparāṃ vāmaśṛṅge tu bhīṣaṇāṃ kṛṣṇapiṅgalām
8.74ab: icchārūpadharāṃ devīṃ praṇatārtivināśinīm
8.74cd: parāṃ cāpyāyanīṃ devīṃ candrakoṭyayutaprabhām
8.75ab: ṣaḍvidhe 'pi kṛte śākte mūrtyādāv api cintayet
8.75cd: vidyāṅgapañcakaṃ paścād āgneyyādiṣu vinyaset
8.76ab: agnīśarakṣovāyūnāṃ dakṣiṇe ca yathākrama
8.76cd: śaktyaṅgāni śivāṅgāni tathaiva vidhinā smaret
8.77ab: kiṃ tu śakrādidikṣv astramantraṃ madhye ca locanam
8.77cd: aghorādyaṣṭakaṃ dhyāyed aghoryādyaṣṭakānvitam
8.78ab: sarvāsām āvṛtatvena lokapālāṃś ca bāhyataḥ
8.78cd: sāstrān svamantraiḥ saṃcintya japaṃ paścāt samārabhet
8.79ab: svarūpe tallayo bhūtvā ekaikāṃ daśadhā smaret
8.79cd: jvalatpāvakasaṃkāśāṃ dhyātvā svāhāntam uccaret
8.80ab: sakṛd ekaikaśo mantrī homakarmaprasiddhaye
8.80cd: ity eva mānaso yāgaḥ kathitaḥ sāmudāyikaḥ
8.81ab: etat triśūlam uddiṣṭam ekadaṇḍaṃ triśaktikam
8.81cd: ittham etad avijñāya śaktiśūlaṃ varānane
8.82ab: baddhvāpi khecarīṃ mudrāṃ notpatayaty avanītalāt
8.82cd: ity etac chāmbhavaṃ proktam aṣṭāntaṃ śāktam iṣyate
8.83ab: turyāntam āṇavaṃ vidyād iti śūlatrayaṃ matam
8.83cd: pṛthag yāgavidhānena śakticakraṃ vicintayet
8.84ab: tenāpi khecarīṃ baddhvā tyajaty evaṃ mahītalam
8.84cd: tato 'bhimantrya dhānyāni mahāstreṇa trisaptadhā
8.85ab: nikṣiped dikṣu sarvāsu jvalatpāvakavat smaret
8.85cd: nirvighnaṃ tad gṛhaṃ dhyātvā saṃhṛtyeśadiśaṃ nayet
8.86ab: pañcagavyaṃ tataḥ kuryād vadanaiḥ pañcabhir budhaḥ
8.86cd: gomūtraṃ gomayaṃ caiva kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ tathā
8.87ab: mantrayed ūrdhvaparyantaiḥ ṣaḍaṅgena kuśodakam
8.87cd: mudre dravyāmṛtaṃ baddhvā tattvaṃ tasya vicintayet
8.88ab: tena saṃprokṣayed bhūmiṃ svalpenānyannidhāpayet
8.88cd: vāstuyāgaṃ tataḥ kuryān mālinyuccārayogataḥ
8.89ab: puṣpair añjalim āpūrya phakārādi samuccaret
8.89cd: dhyātvā śaktyantam adhvānaṃ nakārānte vinikṣipet
8.90ab: gandhadhūpādikaṃ dattvā gaṇeśānaṃ prapūjayet
8.90cd: ṣaḍuttham āsanaṃ nyasya praṇavena tatopari
8.91ab: gām ity anena vighneśaṃ gandhapuṣpādibhir yajet
8.91cd: asyāṅgāni gakāreṇa ṣaḍdīrghasvarayogataḥ
8.92ab: trinetraṃ muditaṃ dhyātvā gajāsyaṃ vāmanākṛtim
8.92cd: visarjya siddhikāmas tu mahāstram anupūjayet
8.93ab: dattvānantaṃ tathā dharmaṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyam eva ca
8.93cd: aiśvaryaṃ karṇikāṃ ceti ṣaḍuttham idam āsanam
8.94ab: asyopari nyased dhyātvā khaḍgakheṭakadhāriṇam
8.94cd: vikarālaṃ mahādaṃṣṭraṃ mahograṃ bhrūkuṭīmukham
8.95ab: svāṅgaṣaṭkasamopetaṃ diṅmātṛparivāritam
8.95cd: svārṇair evāṅgaṣaṭkaṃ tu phaṭkāraparidīpitam
8.96ab: tadrūpam eva saṃcintya tato mātraṣṭakaṃ yajet
8.96cd: indrāṇīṃ pūrvapatre tu savajrāṃ yugapat smaret
8.97ab: āgneyiṃ śaktihastāṃ tu yāmyāṃ daṇḍakarāṃ tataḥ
8.97cd: nairṛtīṃ varuṇānīṃ ca vāyavīṃ ca vicakṣaṇaḥ
8.98ab: khaḍgapāśadhvajair yuktāṃ cintayed yugapat priye
8.98cd: kauverīṃ mudgarakarām īśānīṃ śūlasaṃyutām
8.99ab: gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ pūjya svatantre homam ācaret
8.99cd: ādau ca kalaśaṃ kuryāt sahasrādhikamantritam
8.100ab: sahasraṃ homayet tatra tato japtvā visarjayet
8.100cd: śatam aṣṭottaraṃ pūrṇaṃ paścād yajanam ārabhet
8.101ab: tatrādau kumbham ādāya hemādimayam avraṇam
8.101cd: sarvamantrauṣadhīgarbhaṃ gandhāmbuparipūritam
8.102ab: cūtapallavavaktraṃ ca sraksūtrasitakaṇṭhakam
8.102cd: rakṣoghnatilakākrāntaṃ sitavastrayugāvṛtam
8.103ab: śatāṣṭottarasaṃjaptaṃ mūlamantraprapūjitam
8.103cd: vārdhāny api tathābhūtā kiṃ tu sāstreṇa pūjitā
8.104ab: vikirair āsanaṃ dattvā pūrvoktaṃ tu vicakṣaṇaḥ
8.104cd: indrādīn pūjayet paścāt svadikṣu proktasasvaraiḥ
8.105ab: avicchinnāṃ tato dhārāṃ vārdhānyā pratipādayet
8.105cd: bhrāmayet kalaśaṃ paścād brūyal lokeśvarān idam
8.106ab: bho bhoḥ śakra tvayā svasyāṃ diśi vighnapraśāntaye
8.106cd: sāvadhānena karmāntaṃ bhavitavyaṃ śivājñayā
8.107ab: nītvā tatrāsane pūrvaṃ mūrtibhūtaṃ ghaṭaṃ nyaset
8.107cd: tasya dakṣiṇadigbhāge vārdhānīṃ viniveśayet
8.108ab: ātmamūrtyādipūjyāntaṃ kumbhe vinyasya mantravit
8.108cd: gandhapuṣpādibhiḥ pūjya vārdhānyāṃ pūjayed imam
8.109ab: gandhair maṇḍalakaṃ kṛtvā brahmasthāne vicakṣanaḥ
8.109cd: tatra saṃpūjayet ṣaṭkaṃ trikaṃ vāpy ekam eva vā
8.110ab: kuṇḍasyollekhanaṃ lekhaḥ kuṭṭanaṃ copalepanam
8.110cd: catuṣpathākṣavāṭaṃ ca vajrasaṃsthāpanaṃ tathā
8.111ab: kuśāstaraṇaparidhiviṣṭarāṇāṃ ca kalpanam
8.111cd: sarvam astreṇa kūrvīta vidyām oṃ hrīm iti nyaset
8.112ab: śivam om iti vinyasya saṃpūjya dvitayaṃ punaḥ
8.112cd: tāmrapātre śarāve vā ānayej jātavedasam
8.113ab: śivaśukram iti dhyātvā vidyāyonau vinikṣipet
8.113cd: tatas tv āhūtayaḥ pañca vidyāṅgair eva homayet
8.114ab: jananādi tataḥ karma sarvam evaṃkṛte kṛtam
8.114cd: parāparām anusmṛtya dadyāt pūrṇāhutiṃ punaḥ
8.115ab: saṃpūjya mātaraṃ vahneḥ pitaraṃ ca visarjayet
8.115cd: carvādisādhanāyāgniṃ samuddhṛtya tataḥ punaḥ
8.116ab: jvalitasyāthavā vahneś citiṃ vāmena vāyunā
8.116cd: ākṛṣya hṛdi saṃkumbhya dakṣiṇena punaḥ kṣipet
8.117ab: pūrṇāṃ ca pūrvavad dadyāc chivāgner aparo vidhiḥ
8.117cd: śivarūpaṃ tam ālokya tasyātmāntaḥkṛtiḥ kramāt
8.118ab: kuryād antaḥkṛtiṃ mantrī tato homaṃ samārabhet
8.118cd: mūlaṃ śatena saṃtarpya tadaṅgāni ṣaḍaṅgataḥ
8.119ab: śeṣāṇāṃ mantrajātīnāṃ daśāṃśenaiva tarpaṇam
8.119cd: tataḥ praveśayec chiṣyāñ śucīn snātānupoṣitān
8.120ab: praṇamya devadeveśaṃ catuṣṭayagataṃ kramāt
8.120cd: pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ dadyād dantadhāvanam eva ca
8.121ab: hṛdayena caroḥ siddhir yājñikaiḥ kṣīrataṇḍulaiḥ
8.121cd: saṃpātaṃ saptabhir mantrais tataḥ ṣaḍbhāgabhājitam
8.122ab: śivāgniguruśiṣyāṇāṃ vārdhānīkumbhayoḥ samam
8.122cd: dantakāṣṭhaṃ tato dadyāt kṣīravṛkṣasamudbhavam
8.123ab: tasya pātaḥ śubhaḥ prācīsaumyaiśāpy ordhvadiggataḥ
8.123cd: aśubho 'nyatra tatrāpi homo 'ṣṭaśatiko bhavet
8.124ab: bahiḥkarma tataḥ kuryād dikṣu sarvāsu daiśikaḥ
8.124cd: oṃ kṣaḥ kṣaḥ sarvabhūtebhyaḥ svāheti manunāmunā
8.125ab: samācamya kṛtanyāsaḥ samabhyarcya ca śaṅkaram
8.125cd: [lacuna] gṛhe śuciḥ
8.126ab: nyāsaṃ kṛtvā tu śiṣyāṇām ātmanaś ca viśeṣataḥ
8.126cd: prabhāte nityakarmādi kṛtvā svapnaṃ vicārayet
8.127ab: śubhaṃ prakāśayet teṣāṃ aśubhe homam ācaret
8.127cd: tataḥ puṣpaphalādīnāṃ suveśābharaṇāḥ striyaḥ
8.128ab: āpaduttaraṇaṃ caiva śubhadeśāvarohaṇam
8.128cd: madyapānaṃ śiraśchedam āmamāṃsasya bhakṣaṇam
8.129ab: devatādarśanaṃ sākṣāt tathā viṣṭānulepanam
8.129cd: evaṃvidhaṃ śubhaṃ dṛṣṭvā siddhiṃ prāpnoty abhīpsitām
8.130ab: etad evānyathābhūtaṃ duḥsvapna iti kīrtyate
8.130cd: pakvamāṃsāśanābhyaṅgagartādipatanādikam
8.131ab: tantroktāṃ niṣkṛtiṃ kṛtvā dvijatvāpādanaṃ tataḥ
8.131cd: devāgnigurudevīnāṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā sadā budhaḥ
8.132ab: eteṣām anivedyaiva na kiṃ cid api bhakṣayet
8.132cd: devadravyaṃ gurudravyaṃ caṇḍīdravyaṃ ca varjayet
8.133ab: niṣphalaṃ naiva ceṣṭeta muhūrtam api mantravit
8.133cd: yogābhyāsarato bhūyān mantrābhyāsarato 'pi vā
8.134ab: ity evam ādisamayāñ śrāvayitvā visarjayet
8.134cd: devadevaṃ tataḥ snānaṃ śiṣyāṇām ātmano 'pi vā
8.135ab: kārayec chivakumbhena sarvaduṣkṛtahāriṇā
8.135cd: ity etat sāmayaṃ karma samāsāt parikīrtitam
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare samayādhikāro 'ṣṭamaḥ sargaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eighth chapter (<s>sarga</s>), on <s>samaya</s> (observances/pledges), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s> [Tantra].

body.text: kriyādikṣādhikāro navamaḥ
body.translated_text: The Ninth Chapter: On <s>Kriyā-dīkṣā</s> (Ritual Initiation)

body.text:
9.1ab: athaiṣāṃ samayasthānāṃ kuryād dīkṣāṃ yada guruḥ
9.1cd: tadādhivāsanaṃ kṛtvā [lacuna]
9.2ab: sa ca pūrvaṃ diśaṃ samyak sūtram āsphālayet tataḥ
9.2cd: tanmadhyāt pūrvavāruṇyā vaṅkayeta samāntaram
9.3ab: pūrvāparasamāsena sūtreṇottaradakṣiṇam
9.3cd: aṅkayed aparād aṅkād pūrvād api tathaiva te
9.4ab: matsyamadhye kṣipet sūtram āyataṃ dakṣiṇottare
9.4cd: matakṣetrārdhamānena madhyād dikṣv aṅkayet samam
9.5ab: tadvad diksthāc ca koṇeṣu anulomavilomataḥ
9.5cd: pātayet teṣu sūtrāṇi caturaśraprasiddhaye
9.6ab: vedāśrite hi haste prāk pūrvam ardhaṃ vibhājayet
9.6cd: hastārdhaṃ sarvatas tyaktvā pūrvodagyāmadiggatam
9.7ab: guṇāṅgulasamair bhāgaiḥ śeṣam asya vibhājayet
9.7cd: tryaṅgulaiḥ koṣṭakair ūrdhvais tiryak cāṣṭadvidhātmakaiḥ
9.8ab: dvau dvau bhāgau parityajya punar dakṣiṇasaumyagau
9.8cd: brahmaṇaḥ pārśvayor jīvāc caturthāt pūrvatas tathā
9.9ab: bhāgārdhabhāgamānaṃ tu khaṇḍacandradvayaṃ dvayam
9.9cd: tayor antas tṛtīye tu dakṣiṇottarapārśvayoḥ
9.10ab: jīve khaṇḍenduyugalaṃ kuryād antarbhramād budhaḥ
9.10cd: tayor aparamarmasthaṃ khaṇḍendudvayakoṭigam
9.11ab: bahir mukhabhramaṃ kuryāt khaṇḍacandradvayaṃ dvayam
9.11cd: tadvad brahmaṇi kurvīta bhāgabhāgārdhasaṃmitam
9.12ab: tato dvitīyabhāgānte brahmaṇaḥ pārśvayor dvayoḥ
9.12cd: dve rekhe pūrvage neye bhāgatryaṃśaśame budhaiḥ
9.13ab: ekārdhendūrdhvakoṭisthaṃ brahmasūtrāgrasaṃgataṃ
9.13cd: sūtradvayaṃ prakurvīta madhyaśṛṅgaprasiddhaye
9.14ab: tadagrapārśvayor jīvāt sūtram ekāntare śritam
9.14cd: ādidvitīyakhaṇḍendu koṇāt koṇāntam āśrayet
9.15ab: tayor evāparāj jīvāt prathamārdhendukoṇataḥ
9.15cd: tadvad eva nayet sūtraṃ śṛṅgadvitayasiddhaye
9.16ab: kṣetrārdhe cāpare daṇḍo dvikaracchannapañcakaḥ
9.16cd: dvikaraṃ pañca tadbhāgāḥ pañcapīṭhatirohitāḥ
9.17ab: śeṣam anyad bhaved dṛśyaṃ pṛthutvād bhāgasaṃmitam
9.17cd: ṣaḍvistṛtaṃ caturdīrghaṃ tadadho 'malasārakam
9.18ab: vedāṅgulaṃ ca tadadho mūlaṃ tīkṣṇāgram iṣyate
9.18cd: ādikṣetrasya kurvīta dikṣu dvāracatuṣṭayam
9.19ab: hastāyāmaṃ tadardhaṃ tu vistarād api atasamam
9.19cd: dviguṇaṃ bāhyataḥ kuryāt tataḥ padmaṃ yathā śṛṇu
9.20ab: ekaikabhāgamānāni kuryād vṛttāni vedavat
9.20cd: dikṣv aṣṭau punar apy aṣṭau jīvasūtrāṇi ṣoḍaśa
9.21ab: dvayor dvayoḥ punar madhye tatsaṃkhyātāni pātayet
9.21cd: eṣāṃ tṛtīyavṛttasthaṃ pārśvajīvasamaṃ bhramam
9.22ab: etad antaṃ prakurvīta tato jīvāgram ānayet
9.22cd: yatraiva kutra cit saṅgas tatsaṃbandhe sthirīkṛte
9.23ab: tatra kṛtvā nayen mantrī patrāgrāṇāṃ prasiddhaye
9.23cd: ekaikasmin dale kuryāt kesarāṇāṃ trayaṃ trayam
9.24ab: dviguṇāṣṭāṅgulaṃ kāryaṃ tadvac chṛṅgakajatrayam
9.24cd: tataḥ prapūjayen mantrī rajobhiḥ sitapūrakaiḥ
9.25ab: raktaiḥ kṛṣṇais tathāpītair haritaiś ca viśeṣataḥ
9.25cd: karṇikāḷpītavarṇena mūlamadhyāgradeśataḥ
9.26ab: sitaṃ raktaṃ tathā pītaṃ kāryaṃ kesarajālakam
9.26cd: dalāni śuklavarṇāni prativāraṇayā saha
9.27ab: pītaṃ tadvac catuṣkoṇaṃ karṇikārdhasamaṃ bahiḥ
9.27cd: sitaraktapītakṛṣṇais tatpādān vahnitaḥ kramāt
9.28ab: caturbhir api śṛṅgāṇi tribhir maṇḍalam iṣyate
9.28cd: daṇḍaḥ syān nīlaraktena pītamāmalasārakam
9.29ab: raktaṃ śūlaṃ prakurvīta yat tat pūrvaṃ prakalpitam
9.29cd: paścād dvārasya pūrveṇa tyaktvāṅgulacatuṣṭayam
9.30ab: dvāraṃ vedāśri vṛttaṃ vā saṃkīrṇaṃ vā vicitritam
9.30cd: ekadvitripuraṃ tulyaṃ sāmudgam atha vobhayam
9.31ab: kapālakaṇṭhaśobhopa śobhādibahucitritam
9.31cd: vicitrākārasaṃsthānaṃ vallīsūkṣmagṛhānvitam
9.32ab: evam atra suniṣpanne gandhavastreṇa mārjanam
9.32cd: kṛtvā snānaṃ prakurvīta pūrvoktenaiva karmaṇā
9.33ab: praviśya pūrvavan mantrī upaviśya yathā purā
9.33cd: nyasya pūrvoditaṃ sarvaṃ pañcadhā bhairavātmakam
9.34ab: uttare vinyasec chṛṅge devadevaṃ navātmakam
9.34cd: madhye bhairavasadbhāvaṃ dakṣiṇe ratiśekharam
9.35ab: raktatvaṅmāṃsasūtrais tu vāmakarṇavibhūṣitam
9.35cd: binduyuktaṃ prameyotaṃ ratiśekharam ādiśet
9.36ab: śāktaṃ ca pūrvavat kṛtvā tarpayet pūrvavad budhaḥ
9.36cd: punar abhyarcya deveśaṃ bhaktyā vijñāpayed idam
9.37ab: gurutvena tvayaivāham ājñātaḥ parameśvara
9.37cd: anugrāhyās tvayā śiṣyāḥ śivaśaktipracoditāḥ
9.38ab: tad ete tadvidhāḥ prāptās tvam eṣāṃ kurv anugraham
9.38cd: madīyāṃ tanum āviśya yenāhaṃ tvat samo bhavan
9.39ab: karomy evam iti prokto harṣād utphullalocanaḥ
9.39cd: tataḥ ṣaḍvidham adhvānam anenādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret
9.40ab: sṛṣṭyādipañcakarmāṇi niṣpādyāny asya cintayet
9.40cd: śaktibhir jīvamūrtiḥ syād dvidhaivāsya parāparā
9.41ab: mūrtāmūrtatvabhedena mām apy eṣānutiṣṭhati
9.41cd: karaṇatvaṃ prayānty asya mantrā ye hṛdayādayaḥ
9.42ab: evaṃbhūtaṃ śivaṃ dhyātvā tadgatenāntarātmanā
9.42cd: bhāvyaṃ tanmayam ātmānaṃ daśadhāvartayec chivam
9.43ab: triḥkṛtvā sarvamantrāṃś ca garbhāvaraṇasaṃsthitān
9.43cd: sitoṣṇīṣaṃ tato buddhvā saptajaptaṃ navātmanā
9.44ab: śivahastaṃ tataḥ kuryāt pāśaviśleṣakārakam
9.44cd: prakṣālya gandhatoyena hastaṃ hastena kena cit
9.45ab: gandhadigdho yajed devaṃ sāṅgam āsanavarjitam
9.45cd: ātmany ālabhanaṃ kuryād grahaṇaṃ yojanaṃ tathā
9.46ab: viyogaṃ ca tathoddhāraṃ pāśacchedādikaṃ ca yat
9.46cd: evaṃ patitvam āsādya prapañcavyāptitaḥ śivam
9.47ab: bhāvayet pṛthag ātmānaṃ tatsamānaguṇaṃ tataḥ
9.47cd: maṇḍalastho 'ham evāyaṃ sākṣīvākhilakarmasu
9.48ab: homādhikaraṇatvena vahnāv aham avasthitaḥ
9.48cd: ā yāgāntam ahaṃ kumbhe saṃsthito vighnaśāntaye
9.49ab: śiṣyadehe ca tatpāśa viśleṣatvaprasiddhaye
9.49cd: sākṣāt svadehasaṃstho 'haṃ kartānugrahakarmaṇaḥ
9.50ab: ity etat sarvam ālocya śodhyādhvānaṃ vicintayet
9.50cd: dīkṣāṃ yenādhvanā mantrī śiṣyāṇāṃ kartum icchati
9.51ab: tatraivālocayet sarvaṃ yāyāt padam anāmayam
9.51cd: tatra tenāpṛthagbhūtvā punaḥ saṃcintayed idam
9.52ab: aham eva paraṃ tattvaṃ mayi sarvam idaṃ jagat
9.52cd: adhiṣṭhātā ca kartā ca sarvasyāham avasthitaḥ
9.53ab: tatsamatvaṃ gato jantur mukta ity abhidhīyate
9.53cd: evaṃ saṃcintya bhūyo 'pi śodhyam ādyaṃ samāśrayet
9.54ab: śiṣyamaṇḍalavahnīnāṃ tatraikaṃ bhāvayet sthitam
9.54cd: śodhyādhvānaṃ tu śiṣyāṇāṃ nyasya dehe puroktavat
9.55ab: svena svenaiva mantreṇa svavyāptidhyānam āśrayet
9.55cd: āgantu sahajaṃ śāktaṃ buddhvādau pāśapañjaraṃ
9.56ab: bāhukaṇṭhaśikhāgreṣu triṣu (vṛt) triguṇatantunā
9.56cd: svamantreṇa tatas tattvam āvāhyeṣṭvā pratarpya ca
9.57ab: tatas tacchodhyayonīnāṃ vyāpinīṃ yoniṃ ānayet
9.57cd: māyānte 'dhvani tām eva śuddhe vidyāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
9.58ab: tasyāṃ saṃtarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā śiṣyam astreṇa tāḍayet
9.58cd: ālabhya hṛdaye vidvāñ chivahastena taṃ punaḥ
9.59ab: grahaṇaṃ tasya kūrvīta raśmimātrāviyogataḥ
9.59cd: nāḍīmārgeṇa gatvā tu haṃhṛnmantrapuṭīkṛtam
9.60ab: kṛtvātmasthaṃ tato yonau garbhādhānaṃ vicintayet
9.60cd: tryarṇārdhākṣarayā mantrī sarvagarbhakriyānvitam
9.61ab: bhogyabhoktṛtvasāmarthya niṣpattyā jananaṃ budhaḥ
9.61cd: dakṣaśṛṅgasthayā mantrī prakurvīta sulocane
9.62ab: pibatīpūrvikābhiś ca astrādyaiḥ parayāpi ca
9.62cd: samyag āhutayo dadyād daśa pañca vicakṣaṇaḥ
9.63ab: tato 'syāparayā kāryaṃ pāśavicchedanaṃ budhaiḥ
9.63cd: bhuvaneśam athāmantrya tattveśvaram athāpi vā
9.64ab: bhogabhāgā[lacuna] paścāt tam idam ādiśet
9.64cd: bhuvaneśa tvayā nāsya sādhakasya śivājñayā
9.65ab: pratibandhaḥ prakartavyo yātuḥ padam anāmayam
9.65cd: utkṣepaṇaṃ tataḥ kuryāt tayaivādhyuṣṭavarṇayā
9.66ab: avyāptimantrasaṃyogat pṛthaṅ mārgaviśuddhaye
9.66cd: dadyād ekaikaśo dhyātvā āhutīnāṃ trayaṃ trayam
9.67ab: tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dadyāt parayā vauṣaḍantayā
9.67cd: śiśum utkṣipya cātmasthaṃ taddehasthaṃ ca kārayet
9.68ab: āhutīnāṃ trayaṃ dadyād dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ budhaḥ
9.68cd: mahāpāśupatāstreṇa vilomādiviśuddhaye
9.69ab: visarjayitvā vāgīśīṃ tattvaṃ tu tadantaraṃ
9.69cd: vilīnaṃ bhāvayec chuddhaṃ aśuddhe parameśvari
9.70ab: kālāntavyāptisaṃśuddhau kṛtāyām evam ādarāt
9.70cd: bāhupāśaṃ tu taṃ chittvā homayed ājyasaṃyutam
9.71ab: māyātattve viśudhe tu kaṇṭhapāśe tathā budhaḥ
9.71cd: māyāntamārgasaṃśuddhau dīkṣākarmaṇi sarvataḥ
9.72ab: kriyāsv anuktamantrāsu yojayed aparām budhaḥ
9.72cd: vidyādisakalānte ca tadvad eva parāparām
9.73ab: yoyayen naiśvarād ūrdhvaṃ pibantyādikam aṣṭakam
9.73cd: na cāpi sakalād ūrdhvam aṅgaṣaṭkaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
9.74ab: niṣkale parayā kāryaṃ yat kiṃ cid vidhicoditam
9.74cd: viśuddhe sakalānte tu śikhāṃ chittvā vicakṣaṇaḥ
9.75ab: hutvā cājyaṃ tataḥ śiṣyaṃ snāpayed anupūrvataḥ
9.75cd: ācamyābhyarcya deveśaṃ sruvam āpūrya sarpiṣā
9.76ab: kṛtvā śiṣyaṃ tathātmasthaṃ mūlamantram anusmaret
9.76cd: śivaśaktiṃ tathātmānaṃ śiṣyaṃ sarpis tathānalam
9.77ab: ekīkurvañ chanair gacched dvādaśāntam ananyadhīḥ
9.77cd: tatra kumbhakam āsthāya dhyāyan sakalaniṣkalam
9.78ab: tiṣṭhet tāvad anudvigno yāvad ājyakṣayo bhavet
9.78cd: evaṃ yukte pare tattve guruṇa śivamūrtinā
9.79ab: na bhūyaḥ paśutāṃ eti dagdhamāyānibandhanaḥ
9.79cd: vidhir eṣa samākhyāto dīkṣākarmaṇi bhauvane
9.80ab: itarādhvavidhiṃ muktvā śivayogavidhiṃ tathā
9.80cd: vilomakarma saṃtyajya dviguṇas tattvavartmani
9.81ab: tadvac ca varṇamārge 'pi caturdhā padavartmani
9.81cd: aṣṭadhā mantramārge 'pi kalākhye 'pi ca tad dvidhā
9.82ab: trikhaṇḍe viṃśatiguṇaḥ sa eva parikīrtitaḥ
9.82cd: iti sarvādhvasaṃśuddhiḥ samāsāt parikīrtitā
9.83ab: sādhakācāryayoḥ karma kathyamānam ataḥ śṛṇu
body.translated_text:
(9.1) Now, when the <s>Guru</s> would perform <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation) for these who have taken the <s>samaya</s> (observances), having first performed the <s>adhivāsana</s> (preparatory consecration) [lacuna],
(9.2) He should properly lay the cord in the eastern direction; then from its middle, he should curve [it] evenly toward the northwest.
(9.3) By joining east and west with a cord, [and likewise] north and south, he should mark from the western mark and from the eastern one as well.
(9.4) In the middle of the fish[-shaped figure], he should cast a cord extended north-south; with half the measure of the field, he should mark evenly from the center in the [cardinal] directions.
(9.5) Likewise from the directional [points] to the corners, in forward and reverse order, he should drop cords in them for the completion of the quadrilateral.
(9.6) With [a measure of] four <s>Vedas</s> [= four] <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) in a hand[-span], he should first divide the eastern half; having left aside half a hand[-span] on all sides, [extending] toward the east, north, and southwest,
(9.7) He should divide the remainder with sections equal to three <s>aṅgulas</s> each — upward cells of three <s>aṅgulas</s> and horizontal [cells] of eight-and-two [= sixteen] kinds.
(9.8) Having left aside two sections each on the south and north sides, on both sides of <s>Brahman</s> [the central point], from the fourth life-line (<s>jīva</s>) eastward,
(9.9) With a measure of one section and one half-section, [he should draw] a pair of crescent moons on both sides; between them, in the third [position] on the south and north sides,
(9.10) The wise one should make a pair of crescents on the life-line by means of an inward curve; stationed at the vital point of those two at the back, reaching the tips of the pair of crescents,
(9.11) He should make a pair of crescent moons with an outward-facing curve; likewise on [the area of] <s>Brahman</s>, measured by one section and one half-section.
(9.12) Then at the end of the second section, on both sides of <s>Brahman</s>, the wise ones should draw two lines extending eastward, equal to one-third of a section.
(9.13) He should make two cords — [one] stationed at the upper tip of one half-crescent, joined to the tip of the <s>Brahma</s>-cord — for the completion of the central horn.
(9.14) On both sides of that tip, the cord resting at one interval from the life-line should extend from the corner of the first and second crescent to the [opposite] corner.
(9.15) From the back of those two, from the life-line, from the corner of the first half-crescent, he should likewise draw the cord for the completion of the two horns.
(9.16) In the other [western] half of the field, [there is] the staff (<s>daṇḍa</s>), concealed by a five[-fold] two-hand [measure]; two hands, five sections thereof, concealed by five seats (<s>pīṭha</s>).
(9.17) The remainder — another visible [portion], measured by [its] breadth — six [aṅgulas] in width, four in length; below that, the pure-essence (<s>amalasāraka</s>) [ornament].
(9.18) Four <s>Veda</s>-<s>aṅgulas</s> [in measure] and below that, the base — desired to be sharp-pointed. At the [four] directions of the initial field, he should make four doors,
(9.19) One hand[-span] in height, half that in width — and equal to that [on all sides]; on the outside, he should make [them] twice [that size]. Then hear how [to draw] the lotus:
(9.20) He should make circles one section in diameter, four-fold [in the cardinal directions]; in the eight directions, eight, and again eight life-cords — sixteen [in all].
(9.21) Between every two, he should drop the same number [of cords]; the curve stationed on the third circle of these, equal to the side life-cord,
(9.22) He should make ending at this [point]; then he should bring the tip of the life-cord wherever there is a connection; having established that junction,
(9.23) The <s>mantra</s>-knower should then draw [it] there for the completion of the petal-tips. On each petal, he should make three filaments each.
(9.24) He should make [the horn-cluster] of twice-eight <s>aṅgulas</s>; likewise the three horn-clusters. Then the <s>mantra</s>-knower should worship with colored powders — white, fillers,
(9.25) Red, black, yellow, and especially green. The pericarp with yellow color, [colored] at the base, middle, and tip portions;
(9.26) The filament-network should be made white, red, and yellow. The petals should be white-colored, together with the border.
(9.27) Likewise the quadrilateral, yellow, equal to half the pericarp, on the outside; its sides [colored] with white, red, yellow, and black — from the fire[-direction] onward in sequence.
(9.28) The four horns each with [their specified colors]; the <s>maṇḍala</s> (circle) is desired with three [colors]. The staff should be blue-and-red; the pure-essence yellow.
(9.29) The trident should be made red, which was previously designed. Behind the door, on the eastern [side], having left four <s>aṅgulas</s>,
(9.30) The door — with four <s>Veda</s>-sides, circular, mixed, or variegated; one, two, or three-towered, equal [on both sides], box-shaped, or both;
(9.31) Richly decorated with skull-designs, throat-ornaments, and sub-ornaments, of variegated shapes and forms, furnished with creeper-patterns and miniature temples.
(9.32) When this is well-completed, having cleaned [it] with a fragrant cloth, he should perform the bathing with the previously described ritual procedure.
(9.33) Having entered as before, the <s>mantra</s>-knower, having sat down as previously, having placed all that was previously described — the fivefold <s>Bhairava</s>-form:
(9.34) On the northern horn, he should place the god of gods (<s>Devadeva</s>), nine-formed; in the center, the true nature of <s>Bhairava</s>; on the southern [horn], <s>Ratiśekhara</s>,
(9.35) Adorned on the left ear with blood, skin, flesh, and cord, joined with <s>bindu</s>, measured by the knowable — he should designate <s>Ratiśekhara</s>.
(9.36) Having performed the <s>Śākta</s> [rite] as before, the wise one should offer libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) as before. Having again worshipped the Lord of the gods, he should devotedly make this request:
(9.37) "O Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>), by you alone have I been appointed as <s>Guru</s>. These disciples, impelled by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, are to be graced by you.
(9.38) These have arrived, being of such qualification — bestow your grace upon them, entering my body, whereby I, becoming equal to you,
(9.39) Shall act thus." Having spoken thus, with eyes blooming wide with joy, he should then contemplate the sixfold path (<s>ṣaḍadhvan</s>) as presided over by Him.
(9.40) He should contemplate the five acts beginning with creation (<s>sṛṣṭi</s>) as to be accomplished by Him. Through [His] <s>Śaktis</s>, [the Lord] assumes a living form; His [form] is twofold — supreme and intermediate (<s>parāparā</s>):
(9.41) Through the distinction of manifest and unmanifest — 'He also follows me.' The <s>mantras</s> — the heart (<s>hṛdaya</s>) and others — function as His instruments.
(9.42) Having meditated upon <s>Śiva</s> in this way, with one's inner self absorbed in Him, one should contemplate oneself as being of His nature. He should rotate <s>Śiva</s> tenfold,
(9.43) Thrice, and all the <s>mantras</s> stationed in the womb-enclosure. Then, having realized [Him] with a white turban, [recited] seven times with the nine-formed [<s>mantra</s>],
(9.44) He should then make the <s>Śiva</s>-hand, which causes the loosening of the bonds (<s>pāśa</s>). Having washed the hand with fragrant water, with one hand [touching] the other,
(9.45) Anointed with fragrance, he should worship the deity with [His] limbs, excluding the seat (<s>āsana</s>). He should perform on himself the touching (<s>ālabhana</s>), the grasping (<s>grahaṇa</s>), and the joining (<s>yojana</s>),
(9.46) And the separation (<s>viyoga</s>), the extraction (<s>uddhāra</s>), and the cutting of bonds (<s>pāśaccheda</s>). Thus, having attained lordship (<s>patitva</s>) through pervading the manifest world,
(9.47) He should meditate on <s>Śiva</s>; then separately [contemplate] himself as having qualities equal to His: 'I myself, stationed in the <s>maṇḍala</s>, am the witness in all ritual actions.
(9.48) As the substrate of the <s>homa</s> (fire offering), I am stationed in the fire. Until the end of the worship, I am stationed in the water-pot for the pacification of obstacles.
(9.49) And in the disciple's body, for the accomplishment of the loosening of his bonds. Directly stationed in my own body, I am the agent of the act of grace.'
(9.50) Having reflected upon all this, he should contemplate the path (<s>adhvan</s>) to be purified. Whichever path the <s>mantra</s>-knower wishes to initiate the disciples through,
(9.51) He should contemplate everything there — one would go to the state free from affliction. There, having become non-different from that [<s>Śiva</s>], he should again reflect thus:
(9.52) 'I alone am the supreme reality (<s>tattva</s>); in me [rests] all this world. I am established as both the presider and the agent of all.'
(9.53) A living being who has attained equality with that [<s>Śiva</s>] is called 'liberated.' Having reflected thus, he should again resort to the first [path] to be purified.
(9.54) He should contemplate one [<s>Śiva</s>] as stationed there in the disciple, the <s>maṇḍala</s>, and the fires. Having placed the path to be purified onto the disciples' bodies as previously described,
(9.55) He should resort to meditation on the pervasion of each [path] with its respective <s>mantra</s>. Having first recognized the adventitious (<s>āgantu</s>), innate (<s>sahaja</s>), and <s>Śākta</s> cages of bonds (<s>pāśapañjara</s>),
(9.56) On the arms, throat, and tip of the topknot — in three [places] with a three-stranded cord, with his own <s>mantra</s> — then having invoked the <s>tattva</s>, having worshipped and satiated [it],
(9.57) Then he should bring the <s>yoni</s> (source) that pervades those [impurities] to be purified — the discerning one [should recognize] that very [<s>yoni</s>] as the pure <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) on the path ending with <s>Māyā</s>.
(9.58) Having performed the satiation (<s>saṃtarpaṇa</s>) in her, he should strike the disciple with the <s>astra</s> (weapon-<s>mantra</s>). Having touched the heart, the learned one, with the <s>Śiva</s>-hand, should again
(9.59) Perform the grasping of him — through the non-separation of the mere ray. Having gone through the path of the <s>nāḍī</s> (channel), enclosed in the <s>haṃsa</s>-<s>hṛt</s>-<s>mantra</s> sheath,
(9.60) Having made [the soul] stationed in oneself, the <s>mantra</s>-knower should then contemplate the placing of the embryo (<s>garbhādhāna</s>) in the <s>yoni</s> — with all embryonic rites accomplished, with [the <s>vidyā</s>] of three-and-a-half syllables.
(9.61) The wise one should perform the birth (<s>janana</s>) — through the maturation of the capacity for being the enjoyer and the enjoyed — O beautiful-eyed one, the <s>mantra</s>-knower [should do this] with [the <s>vidyā</s>] stationed on the right horn.
(9.62) With the [<s>mantras</s>] beginning with 'she drinks' (<s>pibatī</s>) and with the <s>astra</s> and others and also with the supreme [<s>vidyā</s>], the discerning one should properly give ten and five oblations.
(9.63) Then the wise ones should perform the cutting of bonds (<s>pāśaviccheda</s>) with the <s>Aparā</s> [<s>vidyā</s>]. Having then addressed the Lord of worlds (<s>Bhuvaneśa</s>) or the Lord of realities (<s>Tattveśvara</s>),
(9.64) [After the share of enjoyment...] [lacuna] afterward, he should instruct him thus: 'O <s>Bhuvaneśa</s>, by the command of <s>Śiva</s>, to this practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>),
(9.65) No obstruction is to be made by you as he goes to the state free from affliction.' Then he should perform the uplifting (<s>utkṣepaṇa</s>) with that very presiding phoneme;
(9.66) Separately, through connection with the <s>mantra</s> of non-pervasion, for the purification of the path, he should give, having meditated one by one, three oblations each.
(9.67) Then he should give the full oblation (<s>pūrṇāhuti</s>) with the supreme [<s>vidyā</s>] ending in '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>.' Having lifted up the child [soul] and made it stationed in himself, he should then establish it in that [disciple's] body.
(9.68) The wise one should give three oblations; having given the full oblation, with the great <s>Pāśupata</s> weapon-[<s>mantra</s>], for the purification beginning with the reverse [order].
(9.69) Having dismissed <s>Vāgīśī</s> (the goddess of speech), [he should contemplate] the <s>tattva</s> within that [path] as dissolved and pure, O Supreme Goddess, in the impure [realm].
(9.70) When the purification through time-ending pervasion has been accomplished in this careful manner, having cut the arm-bond, he should offer it into the fire mixed with ghee.
(9.71) When the <s>Māyā</s>-<s>tattva</s> is purified — likewise the wise one [should cut] the throat-bond. When the purification of the path ending with <s>Māyā</s> is [complete], in all initiation rites,
(9.72) The wise one should employ <s>Aparā</s> in rituals where the <s>mantra</s> is not specified; and at the end of <s>Sakala</s> [the realm] beginning with <s>Vidyā</s>, likewise <s>Parāparā</s>;
(9.73) He should employ from above <s>Īśvara</s> onward the eight [<s>mantras</s>] beginning with 'she drinks' (<s>pibantī</s>). And the discerning one [should not employ] the six limb-[<s>mantras</s>] above <s>Sakala</s>.
(9.74) In the <s>Niṣkala</s> [realm], whatever is enjoined by the ritual rules should be done with the <s>Parā</s> [<s>vidyā</s>]. When the <s>Sakala</s>-end is purified, the discerning one, having cut the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>),
(9.75) Having offered ghee [into the fire], should then bathe the disciple in due order. Having sipped water (<s>ācamya</s>) and worshipped the Lord of gods, having filled the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) with ghee,
(9.76) Having made the disciple stationed in himself, he should remember the root <s>mantra</s> — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and likewise oneself, the disciple, the ghee, and the fire —
(9.77) Unifying [them all], he should slowly go to the <s>dvādaśānta</s> (the end of twelve [finger-breadths above the head]), with undivided attention. There, having assumed breath-retention (<s>kumbhaka</s>), meditating on the <s>Sakala-Niṣkala</s> [form],
(9.78) He should remain undisturbed as long as the ghee lasts. When thus joined with the supreme <s>tattva</s> by the <s>Guru</s> — the embodiment of <s>Śiva</s> —
(9.79) [The disciple] does not again enter the state of a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), his bondage of <s>Māyā</s> being burnt. This procedure has been declared for the initiation rite (<s>dīkṣākarma</s>) on the cosmic-world (<s>bhuvana</s>) [path].
(9.80) Leaving aside the procedure for the other paths and the procedure of <s>Śiva-yoga</s>, and leaving aside the reverse ritual — [the procedure] is doubled on the <s>tattva</s>-path;
(9.81) Likewise on the phoneme-path (<s>varṇamārga</s>) it is fourfold; on the word-path (<s>padavartman</s>) eightfold; and on the <s>mantra</s>-path likewise; and on [the path] called <s>kalā</s>, that is twofold.
(9.82) On the three-sectioned [complete path], it is proclaimed as twentyfold — that very same [procedure]. Thus the purification of all paths (<s>sarvādhvasaṃśuddhi</s>) has been proclaimed in brief.
(9.83) Now hear the ritual action described for the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) and the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>).

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre kriyādīkṣādhikāro navamaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the ninth chapter, on the ritual initiation (<s>kriyā-dīkṣā</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: abhiṣekādhikāro daśamaḥ
body.translated_text: The Tenth Chapter: On Consecration (<s>Abhiṣekādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
10.1ab: atha lakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ siddhisādhanatatparam
10.1cd: śāstrajñaṃ saṃyataṃ dhīram alubdham aśaṭhaṃ dṛḍham
10.2ab: aparīkṣya gurus tadvat sādhakatve niyojayet
10.2cd: samabhyarcya vidhānena pūrvavat parameśvaram
10.3ab: dvitīye pūrvavat kumbhaṃ hemādimayam avraṇam
10.3cd: sarvatra madhyapadmasya dakṣiṇaṃ dalam āśritam
10.4ab: nāyakānāṃ pṛthaṅ mantrān pūjayet kusumādibhiḥ
10.4cd: taṃ saṃtarpya sahasreṇa prakuryād abhiṣecanam
10.5ab: bhadrapīṭhe śubhe sthāpya śrīparṇe dārunirmite
10.5cd: pūrvāmukham udagvaktraṃ snātaṃ puṣpādyalaṅkṛtam
10.6ab: kṛtamantratanuḥ samyak samyak ca kṛtamaṅgalaḥ
10.6cd: śaṅkhabheryādinirghoṣair vedamaṅgalanisvanaiḥ
10.7ab: sarvarājopacāreṇa kṛtvā tasyābhiṣecanam
10.7cd: sadāśivasamaṃ dhyātvā tatas tam api bhūṣayet
10.8ab: punaḥ saṃpūjya deveśaṃ mantram asmai daded budhaḥ
10.8cd: puṣpākṣatatilopetaḥ sajala[lacuna]śvaraṃ nyaset
10.9ab: so 'pi mūrdhani taṃ tadvan mūrtim āśritya dakṣiṇam
10.9cd: abhiṣicya tato 'streṇa rudraśaktiṃ prakāśayet
10.10ab: sa tayāliṅgya tanmantraṃ sahasreṇa pratarpayet
10.10cd: tadā prabhṛti tanniṣṭhas tatsamānaguṇo bhavet
10.11ab: ācāryasyābhiṣeko 'yaṃ sa[lacuna]mantravidhiṃ vinā
10.11cd: kiṃ tu tasya [lacuna] adhivāsapadānvitam
10.12ab: evam etat padaṃ prāpyaṃ duṣprāpyam akṛtātmanām
10.12cd: sādhako mantrasiddhyarthaṃ mantravratam upācaret
10.13ab: evaṃ kṛtvābhiṣekoktaṃ snātvā vidyādhipaṃ japet
10.13cd: lakṣam ekaṃ daśāṃśena tasya tarpaṇam ācaret
10.14ab: pūrvavac cābhiṣekaṃ ca kṛtvā brahmaśiro japet
10.14cd: tallakṣyas tanmayo bhūtvā lakṣadvayam atandritaḥ
10.15ab: lakṣadvayaṃ ca rudrāṇīṃ catuṣkaṃ tu puruṣṭutam
10.15cd: lakṣāṇāṃ pañcakaṃ devi mahāpāśupataṃ japet
10.16ab: sitaraktapītakṛṣṇa vicitrāmbarabhūṣaṇaḥ
10.16cd: tataḥ saṃrakṣito mantrair ebhir apratimo bhavet
10.17ab: avācyaḥ sarvaduṣṭānāṃ mantratejopabṛṃhitaḥ
10.17cd: evaṃ cīrṇavrato bhūtvā yaṃ sādhayitum icchati
10.18ab: dattvārghaṃ tasya lakṣāṇāṃ japen navakam ādarāt
10.18cd: uttamadravyahomāc ca taddaśāṃśena tarpaṇam
10.19ab: mahākṣmāpapalāny āhur uttamādīni tadvidaḥ
10.19cd: madhyame dviguṇaṃ kṛtvā triguṇaṃ kanyase 'pi ca
10.20ab: ājyaguggulanṛsnehā mahāmāṃsasamāḥ matāḥ
10.20cd: dadhibilvapayaḥpadmāḥ kṣmāsamāḥ parikīrtitāḥ
10.21ab: dhātrīdurvāmṛtāmīnāḥ samyag ājyasamā matāḥ
10.21cd: tilādyair atha kurvīta navaṣaṭtriguṇaṃ kramāt
10.22ab: pūrvam evam imaṃ kṛtvā siddher arghaṃ daded budhaḥ
10.22cd: dattvārghaṃ tu japet tāvad yāvat siddhir abhīpsitā
10.23ab: lakṣeṇaikena pṛthvīśaḥ sabhṛtyabalavāhanaḥ
10.23cd: vaśam ānīyate devi dvābhyāṃ rājyam avāpnuyāt
10.24ab: tribhir nidhānasaṃsiddhiś caturbhir balasiddhayaḥ
10.24cd: pañcabhir medinī sarvā ṣaḍbhir apsarasāṃ gaṇaḥ
10.25ab: saptabhiḥ sapta lokāś ca daśabhis tatsamo bhavet
10.25cd: pañcāśadbhis tato gacched avyaktāntaṃ maheśvari
10.26ab: māyāntaṃ ṣaṣtibhir lakṣair īśvarāntam aśītibhiḥ
10.26cd: sakalāvaniparyantaṃ koṭijaptasya siddhyati
10.27ab: athavā vīracittaḥ syāt kṛtvā sevāṃ yathoditām
10.27cd: kṛṣṇabhūtadine rātrau vidhim enaṃ samācaret
10.28ab: kṛtvā pūrvoditaṃ yāgaṃ hutvā dravyam athottaram
10.28cd: ūrdhvakāyo japen mantrī suniṣkampottarāmukhaḥ
10.29ab: tāvad yāvat samāyātā yogeśvaryaḥ samantataḥ
10.29cd: kṛtvā kalakalārāvam atighoraṃ sudāruṇam
10.30ab: bhūmau nipatya tiṣṭhanti veṣṭyāntaḥ sādhakeśvaram
10.30cd: tāsāṃ kṛtvā namaskāraṃ bhittvā vāmāṅgam ātmanaḥ
10.31ab: tadutthena tatas tāsāṃ dattvārghaṃ tatsamo bhavet
10.31cd: ācāryo 'pi ca ṣaṇmāsaṃ maunī pratidinaṃ caret
10.32ab: daśa pañca ca ye mantrāḥ pūrvam uktā mayā tava
10.32cd: pūrvanyāsena saṃnaddhas trikālaṃ vahnikāryakṛt
10.33ab: dhyāyet pūrvoditaṃ śūlaṃ brahmacaryaṃ samāśritaḥ
10.33cd: kṛtvā pūrvoditaṃ yāgaṃ triśaktiparimaṇḍalam
10.34ab: abhiṣiñcet tadātmānam ādāv ante ca daiśikaḥ
10.34cd: evaṃ cīrṇavrato bhūtvā mantrī mantravid uttamaḥ
10.35ab: nigrahānugrahaṃ karma kurvan na pratihanyate
10.35cd: śuddhayor vinyasen mūla madhyāditritaye trayam
10.36ab: vāmāṅguṣṭhe tule netre tarjanyām astram eva ca
10.36cd: akṣahrīm iti khaṇḍena śabdarāśiṃ niveśayet
10.37ab: naphahrīm ityanenāpi śaktimūrtiṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
10.37cd: viparītamahāmudrā prayogān mūlam eva ca
10.38ab: svasthāneṣu tathāṅgāni nyāsaḥ sāmānya ity ayam
body.translated_text:
(10.1) Now, [the guru], having examined one who is endowed with [the proper] characteristics, devoted to the practice of attainments (<s>siddhi-sādhana</s>),
knowledgeable in the scriptures, self-controlled, steadfast, free from greed, without deceit, and firm —
(10.2) [only] after examining [him], should the guru appoint him as a practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>);
having worshipped the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>) with the prescribed rite as before,
(10.3) in the second [rite], as before, a water-jar (<s>kumbha</s>) made of gold or other [metals], without cracks,
everywhere placed at the southern petal of the central lotus —
(10.4) one should worship the mantras of the leaders (<s>nāyaka</s>) individually, with flowers and other [offerings];
having propitiated him with a thousand [recitations], one should perform the consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>).
(10.5) Having placed [the candidate] on an auspicious throne (<s>bhadrapīṭha</s>), made of <s>Śrīparṇa</s> wood,
facing east [or] facing north, bathed and adorned with flowers and other [decorations],
(10.6) with the mantra-body properly constituted and auspicious rites duly performed,
with the sounds of conch-shells, drums, and other instruments, and the auspicious recitation of the <s>Vedas</s>,
(10.7) having performed his consecration with all royal attendances,
meditating on him as equal to <s>Sadāśiva</s>, one should then adorn him.
(10.8) Having worshipped the Lord of Gods again, the wise one should give him the mantra;
with flowers, unbroken grain, and sesame, together with water, one should place [the mantra on] the Lord.
(10.9) He too, [placing it] on his head, likewise having assumed the form on the right [side],
should consecrate [him], and then with the weapon-mantra (<s>astra</s>), manifest the power of <s>Rudra</s> (<s>Rudra-śakti</s>).
(10.10) He, embraced by her [Śakti], should propitiate that mantra with a thousand [recitations];
from that time onward, devoted to that [practice], he becomes equal in qualities to that [deity].
(10.11) This is the consecration of the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), [performed] without the [full] mantra-procedure;
however, for him [the rite includes] the <s>adhivāsa</s> (preparatory) ceremonies.
(10.12) Thus this state is to be attained — [it is] hard to attain for those whose self is not purified;
for the accomplishment of mantras, the practitioner should undertake the mantra-vow (<s>mantra-vrata</s>).
(10.13) Having thus performed the consecration as prescribed, having bathed, one should recite [the mantra of] the lord of <s>vidyā</s>s
one hundred thousand times, and perform the oblation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) with a tenth of that.
(10.14) Having performed the consecration as before, one should recite the <s>Brahmaśiras</s> [mantra],
having that as one's focus, having become one with that, two hundred thousand times without sloth.
(10.15) And two hundred thousand [recitations] of <s>Rudrāṇī</s>, four hundred thousand of <s>Puruṣṭuta</s>,
five hundred thousand, O Goddess, of <s>Mahāpāśupata</s> one should recite.
(10.16) [Wearing] white, red, yellow, black, and multicolored garments and ornaments [respectively],
then, protected by these mantras, one becomes incomparable.
(10.17) Invincible to all malevolent beings, strengthened by the power of mantras;
having thus completed the vow, whatever [deity] one wishes to propitiate,
(10.18) having offered the <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering) to it, one should recite nine hundred thousand [times] with devotion;
and with the oblation of the finest substances, propitiation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) with a tenth of that.
(10.19) The great [substances of] earth-protectors are called the highest, and so on by the experts;
for the middle [grade], one should make it double, and triple for the lowest.
(10.20) Ghee, <s>guggulu</s> (resin), human fat, and the great flesh (<s>mahāmāṃsa</s>) are considered equal [in potency];
curd, <s>bilva</s> [fruit], milk, and lotus are declared equal to the earth[-substances].
(10.21) <s>Dhātrī</s> (gooseberry), <s>dūrvā</s> (grass), <s>amṛtā</s> (divine nectar), and fish are properly considered equal to ghee;
with sesame and so forth, one should perform [the offerings] nine, six, and three times, in order.
(10.22) Having first done this, the wise one should offer the <s>arghya</s> for attainment;
having offered the <s>arghya</s>, one should recite until the desired <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is achieved.
(10.23) With one hundred thousand [recitations], a lord of the earth with his servants, army, and vehicles
is brought under control, O Goddess; with two hundred thousand, one obtains sovereignty.
(10.24) With three hundred thousand, attainment of [hidden] treasures; with four hundred thousand, powers of strength;
with five hundred thousand, the entire earth; with six hundred thousand, the host of celestial nymphs (<s>Apsaras</s>).
(10.25) With seven hundred thousand, the seven worlds; with a million, one becomes equal to that [deity];
with five million, one then reaches up to the Unmanifest (<s>Avyakta</s>), O Great Goddess.
(10.26) Up to <s>Māyā</s> with six million; up to <s>Īśvara</s> with eight million;
up to the entire <s>Sakala</s> realm, [it] is accomplished by ten million recitations.
(10.27) Or, one who is heroic in spirit, having performed the worship as prescribed,
on a dark night of the <s>Bhūta</s> day, should perform this procedure at night:
(10.28) having performed the sacrifice described earlier, having offered the superior substance,
the mantrin, with body upright, firm and facing north, should recite,
(10.29) until the <s>Yogeśvarī</s>s (goddesses of yoga) come from all directions,
making a tumultuous, terrifying, and dreadful clamor,
(10.30) falling to the ground and standing, encircling the lord of practitioners;
having bowed to them, having cut open his own left limb,
(10.31) and with what arises from that, having offered <s>arghya</s> to them, he becomes equal to them.
And the <s>ācārya</s> too should practice silently each day for six months:
(10.32) the fifteen mantras that were previously told by me to you,
armed with the prior arrangement (<s>nyāsa</s>), performing the fire-rite three times [daily],
(10.33) meditating on the trident described before, devoted to celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>),
having performed the sacrifice as described, encircled by the three powers (<s>triśakti</s>),
(10.34) the preceptor (<s>daiśika</s>) should consecrate himself at the beginning and at the end;
having thus completed the vow, the mantrin, the supreme knower of mantras,
(10.35) performing acts of suppression and grace, is never obstructed.
On the two pure [fingers], one should place the root [mantra] and three [mantras] on the middle [finger] and the first triad;
(10.36) on the left thumb, the balance; on the eye, the forefinger, the weapon-mantra;
with the syllable 'AKṢA HRĪṂ,' one should place the mass of sounds by the fragment (<s>khaṇḍa</s>).
(10.37) With 'NAPHA HRĪṂ' also, the discerning one [places] the form of <s>Śakti</s>;
the practice of the inverted great <s>mudrā</s> and the root [mantra] itself —
(10.38) and the limbs [placed] in their respective positions — this is the common <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement).

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare 'bhiṣekādhikāro daśamaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the tenth chapter, on consecration (<s>abhiṣeka</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s> [Tantra].

body.text: dīkṣādhikāra ekādaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The Eleventh Chapter: On Initiation (<s>Dīkṣādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
11.1ab: athātaḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi dīkṣāṃ paramadurlabhām
11.1cd: bhuktimuktikarīṃ samyak sadyaḥpratyayakārikām
11.2ab: nāsyāṃ maṇḍalakuṇādi kiṃ cid apy upayujyate
11.2cd: na ca nyāsādikaṃ pūrvaṃ snānādi ca yathecchayā
11.3ab: praviśya yāgasadanaṃ sūpaliptaṃ sucarcitam
11.3cd: prāṅmukhodaṅmukho vāpi supuṣpāmbarabhūṣitaḥ
11.4ab: dīptāṃ śaktim anusmṛtya pādāgrān mastakāvadhi
11.4cd: mahāmudrāprayogena nirdagdhāṃ cintayet tanum
11.5ab: anulomaprayogāc ca mālinīm amṛtaprabhām
11.5cd: cintayet tanuniṣpattyai taddhyānagatamānasaḥ
11.6ab: śodhyādhvānaṃ tato dehe pūrvoktam anucintayet
11.6cd: tataḥ saṃśodhya vastūni śaktyaivāmṛtatāṃ nayet
11.7ab: parāsaṃpuṭamadhyasthāṃ mālinīṃ sarvakarmasu
11.7cd: yojayet vidhānajñaḥ parāṃ vā kevalāṃ priye
11.8ab: gaṇeśaṃ pūjayitvā tu purā vighnapraśāntaye
11.8cd: tataḥ svagurum ārabhya pūjayed gurupaddhatim
11.9ab: gaṇeśādhas tataḥ sarvaṃ yajen mantrakadambakam
11.9cd: tatpatīnāṃ tato 'rghaṃ tatraiva paripūjayet
11.10ab: antyādhaḥ pūjayed vidyāṃ tadvad vidyāṃ maheśvarīm
11.10cd: mantravidyāgaṇasyāntaḥ kulaśaktiṃ niveśayet
11.11ab: pūrvayāmyāparodakṣu māheśyādicatuṣṭayam
11.11cd: indrāṇīpūrvakaṃ tadvad aiśādidala antagam
11.12ab: tatropari nyased devaṃ kūṭarūpāṇunāmunā
11.12cd: jīvaṃ daṇḍasamākrāntaṃ śūlasyopari saṃsthitam
11.13ab: dakṣāṅguliṃ tato 'dhastāt tato vāmapayodharam
11.13cd: nābhikaṇṭhau tatodhastād vāmaskandhavibhūṣaṇau
11.14ab: śivajihvānvitaḥ paścāt tadūrdhvoṣṭhena copari
11.14cd: sarvayoginicakrāṇām adhipo 'yam udāhṛtaḥ
11.15ab: asyāpy uccāraṇād eva saṃvittiḥ syāt paroditā
11.15cd: tato vīrāṣṭakaṃ paścāc chaktyuktavidhinā yajet
11.16ab: prabhūtair vividhair iṣṭvā gandhadhūpaiḥ sragādibhiḥ
11.16cd: śrīkārapūrvakaṃ nāma pādāntaṃ parikalpayet
11.17ab: tataḥ śiṣyaṃ samāhūya bahudhā suparīkṣitam
11.17cd: rudraśaktyā tu saṃprokṣya devāgre viniveśayet
11.18ab: bhujau tasya samālokya rudraśaktyā pradīpayet
11.18cd: tathaivāpy arpayet puṣpaṃ karayor gandhadigdhayoḥ
11.19ab: nirālambau tu tau dhyātvā śaktyākṛṣṭau vicintayet
11.19cd: śaktimantritanetreṇa baddhvā netre tu pūrvavat
11.20ab: tataḥ prakṣepayet puṣpaṃ sā śaktis tatkarasthitā
11.20cd: yatra tat patate puṣpaṃ tatkulaṃ tasya lakṣayet
11.21ab: mukham udghāṭya taṃ paścāt pādayoḥ pratipātayet
11.21cd: tato 'sya mastake cakraṃ hastayoś cārcya yogavit
11.22ab: taddhastau prerayec chaktyā yāvan mūrdhāntam āgatau
11.22cd: śivahastavidhiḥ proktaḥ sadyaḥpratyayakārakaḥ
11.23ab: carukaṃ dāpayet paścāṭ kharjūrādiphalodbhavam
11.23cd: śaktyālambāṃ tanuṃ kṛtvā sthāpayed agrataḥ śiśoḥ
11.24ab: puṣpakṣepaprayogena hastam ākṛṣya dakṣiṇam
11.24cd: carukaṃ grāhayen mantrī taddhyānagatamānasaḥ
11.25ab: śivahastaprayogena samāropya mukhaṃ nayet
11.25cd: anenaiva vidhānena kṣīravṛkṣasamudbhavam
11.26ab: dantakāṣṭhaṃ dadet devi ṣoḍaśāṅgulam āyatam
11.26cd: eteṣāṃ cālanān mantrī śaktipātaṃ parīkṣayet
11.27ab: mandatīvrādibhedena mandatīvrādikān budhaḥ
11.27cd: ity ayaṃ samayī proktaḥ saṃsthitoktena vartmanā
11.28ab: cikīrṣuś ca yadāḷdīkṣām asyaivārpitamānasaḥ
11.28cd: tad iṣṭvā pūrvavad yogī kuleśaṃ tam anukramāt
11.29ab: saṃpūjya pūrvavac chiṣyam ṛjudehe vilokayet
11.29cd: śaktiṃ saṃcintya pādāgrān mastakāntaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
11.30ab: śodhyādhvānaṃ tato nyasya sarvādhvavyāptibhāṣanām
11.30cd: śaktitattvādibhedena pūrvoktena ca vartmanā
11.31ab: upaviśya tatas tasya vidhānam idam ācaret
11.31cd: mūlaśodhyāt samārabhya śaktiṃ dīptānalaprabhām
11.32ab: yojayec chodhyasaṃśuddhi bhāvanāgatamānasaḥ
11.32cd: evaṃ sarvāṇi śodhyāni nirdahantīm anāmayām
11.33ab: śive saṃcintayel līnāṃ niṣkale sakale 'pi vā
11.33cd: yoginā yojitā mārge svajātīyasya poṣaṇam
11.34ab: kurute nirdahaty anyad bhinnajātikadambakam
11.34cd: anayā śodhyamānasya śiṣyasyāsya mahāmatiḥ
11.35ab: lakṣayec cihnasaṃghātam ānandādikam ādarāt
11.35cd: ānanda udbhavaḥ kampo nidrā ghūrṇiś ca pañcamī
11.36ab: evam āviṣṭayā śaktyā mandatīvrādibhedataḥ
11.36cd: pāśastobhapaśugrahau prakurvīta yathecchayā
11.37ab: gṛhītasya punaḥ kuryān niyogaṃ śeṣabhuktaye
11.37cd: athavā kasya cin nāyam āveśaḥ saṃprajāyate
11.38ab: tad enaṃ yugapac chaktyā sabāhyābhyantare dahet
11.38cd: tayā saṃdahyamāno 'sau cchinnamūla iva drumaḥ
11.39ab: patate kāśyapīpṛṣṭhe ākṣepaṃ vā karoty asau
11.39cd: yasya tv evam api syān na taṃ caivopalavat tyajet
11.40ab: pṛthaktattvavidhau dīkṣāṃ yogyatāvaśyavarjinaḥ
11.40cd: tattvābhyāsavidhānena vakṣyamāṇena kārayet
11.41ab: iti saṃdīkṣitasyāsya mumukṣoḥ śeṣavartanam
11.41cd: kulakrameṣṭir ādeśyā pañcāvasthāsamanvitā
11.42ab: bubhukṣos tu prakurvīta samyagyogābhiṣecanam
11.42cd: tatreṣṭvā pūrvavad dehaṃ vistīrṇair vibudhair budhaiḥ [?]
11.43ab: hemādidīpakān aṣṭau ghṛtenāruṇavartikān
11.43cd: kulāṣṭakena saṃbodhya śivaṃ śaṅkhe prapūjayet
11.44ab: sarvaratnauṣadhīgarbhe gandhāmbuparipūrite
11.44cd: tenābhiṣecayet taṃ tu śivahastoktavartmanā
11.45ab: ācāryasyābhiṣeko 'yam adhikārapadānvitaḥ
11.45cd: kuryāt piṇḍādibhis tadvac catuḥṣaṣṭiṃ pradīpakān
11.46ab: abhiṣiktavidhāv eva sarvayogigaṇena tu
11.46cd: viditau bhavatas tatra gurur mokṣaprado bhavet
11.47ab: anayoḥ kathayej jñānaṃ trividhaṃ sarvam apy alam
11.47cd: svakīyājñāṃ daded yogī svakriyākaraṇaṃ prati
body.translated_text:
Now, hereafter I shall explain the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), supremely rare,
which bestows both <s>bhukti</s> (worldly enjoyment) and <s>mukti</s> (liberation), and produces immediate conviction.
In this [initiation], no <s>maṇḍala</s> (ritual diagram), <s>kuṇḍa</s> (fire-pit), or anything else is required,
nor are <s>nyāsa</s> (placement of mantras) and such preliminaries needed; bathing and the like are done as one wishes.
Having entered the <s>yāgasadana</s> (sacrificial hall), well-smeared and beautifully decorated,
facing east or facing north, adorned with fine flowers and garments,
recollecting the blazing <s>śakti</s> (power) from the tips of the feet up to the crown of the head,
one should visualize the body as consumed by the application of <s>mahāmudrā</s> (the great seal).
And by the forward application [of the <s>mātṛkā</s>], one should contemplate <s>Mālinī</s>, radiant with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar),
for the re-creation of the body, with the mind absorbed in meditation upon her.
Then one should contemplate the <s>adhvan</s> (path-levels) to be purified in the body, as previously described;
then, having purified the substances, one should lead them to the state of <s>amṛta</s> (immortality) through <s>śakti</s> alone.
<s>Mālinī</s>, situated within the enclosure of <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme), in all ritual actions,
should be employed by the knower of the procedure; or <s>Parā</s> alone [may be used], O dear one.
Having first worshipped <s>Gaṇeśa</s> for the pacification of obstacles,
then beginning with one's own <s>guru</s>, one should worship the lineage of <s>gurus</s>.
Below <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, then one should worship the entire assemblage of <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulae);
then one should fully worship the <s>argha</s> (offering vessel) of their lords right there.
Below the last, one should worship the <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-mantra), and likewise the <s>vidyā</s> of <s>Maheśvarī</s> (the Great Goddess);
within the group of <s>mantras</s> and <s>vidyās</s>, one should install the <s>kulaśakti</s> (clan-power).
In the east, south, west, and north, [one should place] the group of four beginning with <s>Māheśī</s>,
and likewise, beginning with <s>Indrāṇī</s>, [extending] from the northeast petal to the last.
Above that, one should place the deity, by means of the <s>kūṭa</s> (seed-syllable) form with these syllables:
the <s>jīva</s> (life-syllable) surmounted by the <s>daṇḍa</s> (staff), situated upon the <s>śūla</s> (trident),
then below it the right finger[-vowel], then the left breast[-vowel],
then below that the navel and throat, adorning the left shoulder.
Connected behind with the tongue of <s>Śiva</s>, and above with his upper lip --
this one is declared the lord of all the circles of <s>yoginīs</s>.
Merely by the utterance of this [mantra], the supreme awakening arises.
Then afterward one should worship the <s>vīrāṣṭaka</s> (eight heroes) by the method prescribed by <s>Śakti</s>.
Having worshipped with abundant and various offerings of fragrance, incense, garlands, and the like,
one should formulate the name preceded by <s>śrīkāra</s> ('Śrī'), ending with <s>pāda</s> (feet).
Then, having summoned the disciple, who has been thoroughly tested in many ways,
and having sprinkled him with <s>rudraśakti</s> (the power of Rudra), one should seat him before the deity.
Examining his two arms, one should illuminate [them] with <s>rudraśakti</s>;
likewise one should also offer a flower upon his hands, which are smeared with fragrant paste.
Having meditated upon those [hands] as without support, one should visualize them as drawn by <s>śakti</s>;
with eyes consecrated by <s>śakti</s>, having blindfolded the eyes as before,
then one should cause [the disciple] to cast the flower -- that <s>śakti</s> is stationed in his hand;
wherever that flower falls, one should recognize that as his <s>kula</s> (clan/family).
Afterward, having uncovered his face, one should cause him to fall at the feet [of the deity];
then the knower of <s>yoga</s> should draw the <s>cakra</s> (wheel) on his head and worship it upon his hands.
One should impel those hands with <s>śakti</s> until they reach the crown of the head --
this is declared the procedure of <s>śivahasta</s> (Śiva's hand), which produces immediate conviction.
Afterward one should give him the <s>caruka</s> (ritual food-offering), made from dates and other fruits;
having made the body supported by <s>śakti</s>, one should place [it] before the disciple.
By the method of flower-casting, having drawn the right hand,
the <s>mantrī</s> (mantra-adept) should cause [the disciple] to grasp the <s>caruka</s>, with his mind absorbed in meditation upon it.
By the <s>śivahasta</s> (Śiva's hand) method, having raised it up, one should bring it to the mouth;
by this very same procedure, [one should give] a tooth-stick produced from a milk-tree,
O Goddess, sixteen finger-breadths in length.
By the movements of these, the <s>mantrī</s> should examine the <s>śaktipāta</s> (descent of power),
the wise one [discerning] mild, intense, and other grades through the distinction of mild, intense, and so forth.
Thus this one is declared a <s>samayī</s> (pledged initiate), established on the path as described.
And when [the <s>guru</s>] desires to perform the [full] <s>dīkṣā</s>, with his mind directed toward this very [disciple],
having worshipped as before, the <s>yogī</s> should [worship] the lord of the <s>kula</s> (clan) in due order.
Having honored the disciple as before, the discerning one should examine [him] with body upright,
contemplating the <s>śakti</s> from the tips of the feet to the crown of the head.
Then, having placed the <s>adhvan</s> (path-levels) to be purified, which pervades all paths,
by the division of <s>śakti</s>, <s>tattva</s> (principle), and the rest, and by the method previously described,
then having sat down, one should perform this procedure for him:
beginning from the lowest element to be purified, one should apply the <s>śakti</s>, blazing with the radiance of fire,
with the mind absorbed in the contemplation of the purification of each element to be purified.
Thus, [one should visualize the <s>śakti</s>] burning all the elements to be purified, free from affliction,
and contemplate her as dissolved in <s>Śiva</s>, whether in the formless or in the form-bearing [aspect].
