The <s>śakti</s>, when applied on the path by the <s>yogī</s> (practitioner), nourishes what is of the same class
and burns away everything of a different class.
As this disciple is being thus purified, the great-minded one
should carefully observe the assemblage of signs beginning with <s>ānanda</s> (bliss):
<s>ānanda</s> (bliss), <s>udbhava</s> (arising), <s>kampa</s> (trembling), <s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>ghūrṇi</s> (swaying) as the fifth.
Thus, by means of the <s>śakti</s> that has entered [the disciple], according to the distinctions of mild, intense, and so forth,
one should effect the seizing of the bonds and the grasping of the bound soul, as one wishes.
For one who has been seized, one should again prescribe the injunction for the enjoyment of the remainder [of karma].
Or alternatively, for someone this <s>āveśa</s> (possession by śakti) may not arise at all;
in that case, one should burn him simultaneously with <s>śakti</s>, both externally and internally.
Being consumed by her, he falls upon his back like a tree whose roots have been cut,
or he makes a convulsion.
But for one in whom even this does not occur, one should not abandon him like a stone;
[rather,] in the procedure of initiating [him] through each <s>tattva</s> (principle) separately, for those who necessarily lack fitness,
one should perform the <s>dīkṣā</s> by the method of <s>tattvābhyāsa</s> (practice of the principles), which will be described.
Thus, for this one who has been [fully] initiated and who seeks liberation, the remaining conduct
to be prescribed is the <s>kulakrameṣṭi</s> (clan-sequence worship), endowed with the five states.
But for one who seeks [worldly] enjoyment, one should properly perform the <s>yogābhiṣecana</s> (consecration through yoga);
there, having worshipped as before, [one should worship] the body with extensive [rites] by the wise sages.
Eight lamps of gold and other [metals], with wicks [soaked] in ghee and reddened,
having awakened them with the eight <s>kula</s>-[mantras], one should worship <s>Śiva</s> in a conch shell,
filled with scented water, containing the essence of all gems and herbs;
with that one should consecrate him by the method prescribed for <s>śivahasta</s> (Śiva's hand).
This is the consecration of the <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor), accompanied by the station of authority.
One should likewise make sixty-four lamps with <s>piṇḍa</s> (rice-balls) and other [offerings];
in the very procedure of consecration, with the entire host of <s>yoginīs</s>,
both [guru and disciple] become known there -- the <s>guru</s> becomes the bestower of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
To both of these one should teach all three kinds of knowledge completely;
the <s>yogī</s> should give his own command regarding the performance of his [ritual] activities.

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre dīkṣādhikāra ekādaśaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the eleventh chapter, on initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: dhāraṇādhikāro dvādaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The Twelfth Chapter: On Concentration (<s>Dhāraṇādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
12.1ab: athaitāṃ devadevasya śrutvā vācam atisphuṭām

12.10cd: trividhaṃ kīrtitaṃ vyoma daśadhā bindur iṣyate

12.11cd: śuklādibhedabhedena eko 'pi daśadhā mataḥ

12.12cd: vigrahaḥ svāṇubhedāc ca dvidhā bhinno 'py anekadhā

12.14cd: ekam eva phalaṃ yatra cittabhedas tv asau mataḥ

12.15cd: yaṃ siṣādhayiṣur yogam ādāv eva samācaret

12.16cd: mahāmudrāprayogena viparītavidhau budhaḥ

12.21ab: sa vāsanānubhāvena bhūmikājayam ārabhet
12.21cd: gaṇanāthaṃ namaskṛtya saṃsmṛtya trigurukramam
12.22ab: samyag āviṣṭadehaḥ syād iti dhyāyed ananyadhīḥ
12.22cd: svadehaṃ hemasaṅkāśaṃ turyāśraṃ vajralāñchitam

12.24cd: vajradehas tribhiś cābdair navanāgaparākramaḥ

12.25cd: ādyā pūrvodite devi bhede pañcadaśātmake

12.34ab: sakalaṃ hṛdayāntaḥstham ātmānaṃ kanakaprabham
12.34cd: svaprabhādyotitāśeṣa dehāntam anucintayet
12.35ab: savyāpārādibhedena saptalokīṃ tu pūrvavat

12.36cd: brahmalokam avāpnoti pūrvoktenaiva vartmanā
12.37ab: adhaḥprakāśakaṃ pītaṃ dvirūpaṃ pūrvavan mahat
12.37cd: cintayen matsamo bhūtvā mallokam anugacchati

12.38cd: cintayec chatarudrāṇām adhipatvam avāpnuyāt
12.39ab: ity evaṃ pṛthivītattvam abhyasyaṃ daśapañcadhā
12.39cd: yogibhir yogasiddhyarthaṃ tatphalāni bubhukṣayā

12.41ab: yo yatra yojitas tattve sa tasmān na nivartate

12.42ab: ayukto 'py adhvasaṃśuddhiṃ saṃprāpya bhuvaneśataḥ
12.42cd: śuddhaḥ śivatvam āyāti dagdhasaṃsārabandhanaḥ
body.translated_text:
(12.1) Then, having heard this most clear speech of the God of gods, with eyes blooming wide with great joy, she who causes bliss to the world,
(12.2) the Goddess, worshipped by hosts of gods, satiated with the nectar of contentment, having bowed to the slayer of <s>Andhaka</s>, again spoke these words:
(12.3) 'You have previously stated that the <s>yogin</s> should practice <s>yoga</s>. How is that practice to be performed? Let it be explained, O Destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>.'
(12.4) Thus addressed by the Mother of the world, <s>Bhairava</s>, the destroyer of fear, of noble intellect, spoke these words, serene and profound:
(12.5) 'Listen, O Goddess, to the method of <s>yoga</s> practice as I expound it, by which, becoming steady, the <s>yogin</s> shall attain <s>siddhi</s> (perfection) here.
(12.6) In a cave, or in an underground chamber, soundless and most delightful, free from all disturbances, the <s>yogin</s> should practice <s>yoga</s>,
(12.7) having conquered his posture, conquered his mind, conquered his breath, conquered his senses, conquered sleep, conquered anger, conquered agitation, free from pain.
(12.8) Either through the differentiation of objects of focus (<s>lakṣya</s>), or through the differentiation of consciousness (<s>citta</s>), the lord of <s>yogin</s>s should perfect [the path] from earth (<s>dharā</s>) to <s>Śakti</s>.
(12.9) Through the differentiation of space (<s>vyoma</s>), form (<s>vigraha</s>), point of light (<s>bindu</s>), phoneme (<s>varṇa</s>), world (<s>bhuvana</s>), and sound (<s>dhvani</s>) — the differentiation of objects of focus is said to be sixfold; it is taught as it truly is.
(12.10) Space (<s>vyoma</s>) is declared to be threefold, through the distinction of external, internal, and combined; the point of light (<s>bindu</s>) is considered tenfold.
(12.11) Having the form of a <s>kadamba</s> flower-cluster, radiant with flickering starlight — though one, it is considered tenfold through the sub-divisions of white and other [colors].
(12.12) Sound (<s>dhvani</s>) is tenfold through the varieties of [sounds like] the tamarind [seed rattle], the cricket, and so forth; form (<s>vigraha</s>) is divided twofold through the distinction of one's own and atomic forms, yet [further] into many.
(12.13) The worlds (<s>bhuvana</s>s) are innumerable; the phonemes (<s>varṇa</s>s) number fifty. Even when accomplishing one [of these], one may incidentally perceive
(12.14) other fruits as well — that is called the differentiation of objects. Where there is only one fruit, that is considered the differentiation of consciousness.
(12.15) One whose self has been purified by fire-ritual (<s>homa</s>) and initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>), who has received instruction in <s>samāveśa</s> (divine possession), should first practice whatever <s>yoga</s> he wishes to accomplish.
(12.16) Having placed the supreme seed-mantra (<s>parā-bīja</s>) upon the hands, the wise one should contemplate <s>Śakti</s> through the application of <s>Mahāmudrā</s>, in the reverse procedure:
(12.17) resembling blazing fire, from the tips of the feet to the crown of the head. Then, afterward, having formed the salutation [mudrā], with breath held at the heart,
(12.18) one should contemplate the supreme seed-mantra (<s>parā-bīja</s>), exceedingly radiant, in its own form. One should meditate on its three measures (<s>mātrā</s>s), issuing from the three openings (<s>kha-traya</s>).
(12.19) Then, after a hundred beats, the <s>yogin</s> attains <s>samāveśa</s> (divine absorption). Even a slayer of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, [practicing] daily for seven days [achieves this].
(12.20) One whose body is thus possessed should perform the prescribed rite. But one who has first had the procedure of possession performed by the <s>guru</s>,
(12.21) by the power of residual impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>), should begin the conquest of the stages (<s>bhūmikā</s>s). Having saluted <s>Gaṇanātha</s> (Lord of the Gaṇas) and having remembered the succession of the three <s>guru</s>s,
(12.22) one whose body is properly possessed should meditate with single-pointed mind: [visualizing] one's own body as golden in appearance, seated on the fourth seat (<s>turyāśra</s>), marked with a <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt).
(12.23) Then weightiness comes within twenty-seven days; from the seventh day onward, rigidity also arises.
(12.24) In six months, having conquered disease, one becomes like molten gold in appearance; with a <s>vajra</s>-body in three years, with the might of nine elephants.
(12.25) This is declared to you as the pure earth (<s>pārthivī</s>) <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), the first among the previously stated divisions of fifteen, O Goddess.
(12.26) One should contemplate the body with activity, radiant like molten gold, seated on the fourth seat in a circle adorned with <s>vajra</s>s.
(12.27) In seven days, weightiness comes; in a month, freedom from disease. In six months, one knows everything within the earth in its true nature.
(12.28) In three years, one enjoys the earth girdled by seven oceans. The second division has been described; now hear the third.
(12.29) One should contemplate the body in the same way, but without activity. One obtains the previously stated fruit, along with [mastery over] the underworlds (<s>pātāla</s>).
(12.30) In the fourth, one should meditate [upon the form] situated in the heart, twelve finger-breadths in extent, in the form of the previously described phoneme, with activity, without laziness.
(12.31) Having obtained all that was previously stated, one becomes lord of the underworlds. The same [result] is obtained firmly in the fifth [division], which is without activity.
(12.32) In the sixth, [one should contemplate it as] yellow, resembling the flickering sun, enveloped by a dark cloud. In the seventh also, the wise one should contemplate it likewise, without waves.
(12.33) When both of these become steady, one knows and enjoys the three [worlds] — <s>bhūḥ</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>svaḥ</s> — within the previously stated years.
(12.34) One should contemplate the complete Self situated within the heart, golden in radiance, illuminating the entire interior of the body with its own light.
(12.35) Through the divisions beginning with 'with activity,' the wise one, when the ninth division becomes steady, knows and enjoys the seven worlds as before.
(12.36) One should contemplate the two [forms] as yellow, resembling the orb of the sun, as before. One attains <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of <s>Brahmā</s>) by the same path as previously stated.
(12.37) One should contemplate [it as] illuminating downward, yellow, having two forms, great, as before — having become equal to me, one follows to my world.
(12.38) One should contemplate the radiance as yellow, illuminating everything, both externally and internally — one attains sovereignty over a hundred <s>Rudra</s>s.
(12.39) Thus the earth-<s>tattva</s> (earth principle) is to be practiced in fifteen ways by <s>yogin</s>s for the attainment of <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic perfection), and its fruits [are enjoyed] through the desire for experience.
(12.40) In whichever [tattva] a natural inclination (<s>vāsanā</s>) has arisen for anyone, by the force of fitness, the discerning ones should direct him to that very [practice] at the time of initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>).
(12.41) One who is yoked to a particular <s>tattva</s> does not turn back from it. Having attained all its fruits, united with <s>Śiva</s>, one is liberated.
(12.42) Even one who is not [directly] yoked, having attained the purification of the path (<s>adhva</s>) from [the level of] the lord of the worlds (<s>bhuvaneśa</s>), becomes pure, attains the state of <s>Śiva</s>, with the bonds of <s>saṃsāra</s> burned away.'

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre prathamadhāraṇādhikāro dvādaśaḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twelfth chapter, on the first concentration (<s>Prathamadhāraṇādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: jalādimahābhūtajayādhikāras trayodaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The thirteenth chapter: On the Conquest of Water and Other Great Elements (<s>Jalādi-mahābhūta-jayādhikāra</s>).

body.text:
13.1ab: athātaḥ sampravakṣyāmi dhāraṇāṃ vāruṇīm imām
13.1cd: yayā saṃsiddhayogena jalāntādhipatir bhavet
13.2ab: jalāntaḥsthaṃ smared dehaṃ sitaṃ śītaṃ suvartulam
13.2cd: sabāhyābhyantaraṃ yogī nānyad astīti cintayet
13.3ab: evam abhyasyatas tasya saptāhāt klinnatā bhavet
13.3cd: pittavyādhiparityakto māsena bhavati dhruvam
13.4ab: snigdhāṅgaḥ snigdhadṛṣṭiś ca nīlakuñcitamūrdhajaḥ
13.4cd: bhavaty abdena yogīndras tribhir varṣati meghavat
13.5ab: ity eṣā vāruṇī proktā prathamā śuddhadhāraṇā
13.5cd: adhunā saṃpravakṣyāmi bhedair bhinnām imāṃ punaḥ
13.6ab: pūrvavac cintayed dehaṃ savyāpāraṃ sitaṃ svakam
13.6cd: jalopari sthitaṃ devi tadgatenāntarātmanā
13.7ab: saptāhān mucyate rogaiḥ sarvaiḥ pittasamudbhavaiḥ
13.7cd: ṣaṇmāsāj jāyate sthairyaṃ yadi tanmayatāṃ gataḥ
13.8ab: jalāvaraṇavijñānam abdair asya tribhir bhavet
13.8cd: nirvyāpāraprabhede 'pi sarvatra varuṇopamaḥ
13.9ab: sa yāti vāruṇaṃ tattvaṃ bhūmikāḥ kramaśo 'bhyaset
13.9cd: pūrvavat kaṇṭhamadhyastham ātmānaṃ dvādaśāṅgulam
13.10ab: saṃsmarañ jalatattveśaṃ prapaśyaty acirād dhruvam
13.10cd: taddṛṣṭiḥ sthiratām eti svarūpe pañcame sthire
13.11ab: dvibhede 'pi sthirībhūte candrabimbe ghanāvṛte
13.11cd: tatsamānatvam abhyeti tataḥ sakalarūpiṇī
13.12ab: cintyate deham āpūrya sitavarṇena tejasā
13.12cd: tad eva sthiratām eti tatra susthiratāṃ gate
13.13ab: ghanamuktendubimbābhaṃ tataḥ samanucintayet
13.13cd: tatpatitvaṃ samabhyeti dvitīye sthiratāṃ vrajet
13.14ab: adhaḥprakāśakaṃ śuklaṃ tatas tejo vicintayet
13.14cd: vidyeśvaratvam āpnoti jalāvaraṇasaṃbhavam
13.15ab: svadehavyāpini dhyāte tatrasthe śuklatejasi
13.15cd: sarvādhipatyam āpnoti susthire tatra susthiram
13.16ab: dhyeyatattvasamānatvam avasthātritaye sthire
13.16cd: dvitaye ca tadīśāna saṃvittir upajāyate
13.17ab: dvitaye 'nyatra tattulyaḥ sthiro bhavati yogavit
13.17cd: ṣaṭke sarveśatām eti dvitaye 'nyatra tu cyutiḥ
13.18ab: ity ayaṃ sarvatattveṣu bhede pañcadaśātmake
13.18cd: jñeyo vidhir vidhānajñaiḥ phalapañcakasiddhidaḥ
13.19ab: tat phalāntaram etasmād uktaṃ yac cāpi vakṣyate
13.19cd: anuṣaṅgaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ tat sarvam avicārataḥ
13.20ab: itīyaṃ vāruṇī proktā prabhedair daśapañcabhiḥ
13.20cd: yogināṃ yogasiddhyartham āgneyīm adhunā śṛṇu
13.21ab: trikoṇaṃ cintayed dehaṃ raktajvālāvalīdharam
13.21cd: svaśarīrotthito vahnir jvalan vai sarvadāhakaḥ
13.22ab: saptabhir divasair devi taikṣṇyam asyopajāyate
13.22cd: vātaśleṣmabhavaiḥ sarvair māsān mucyati sādhakaḥ
13.23ab: nidrāhīnaś ca bahvāśī svalpaviṇmūtrakṛd bhavet
13.23cd: icchayā nirdahed yad yat spṛṣṭaṃ vastu ṛtukṣayāt
13.24ab: tryabdād agnisamo bhūtvā krīḍaty agnir yathecchayā
13.24cd: sarvaṃ nirdahati kruddhaḥ saśailavanakānanam
13.25ab: trikoṇamaṇḍalārūḍham ātmānam anucintayet
13.25cd: savyāpārādibhedena sarvatrāpi vicakṣaṇaḥ
13.26ab: saptāhād vyādhibhir hīnaḥ ṣaṇmāsād agnivad bhavet
13.26cd: tribhir abdaiḥ sa saṃpūrṇaṃ tejastattvaṃ prapaśyati
13.27ab: yacchaktibhede yad dṛṣṭaṃ tat tadbhede sthirībhavet
13.27cd: pūrvavat tālumadhyastham ātmānaṃ jvalanaprabham
13.28ab: dhyāyan prapaśyate tejas tattveśān akhilān kramāt
13.28cd: dhūmākrāntāgnisaṃkāśaṃ ravibimbasamākṛtim
13.29ab: dhyāyaṃs tanmadhyatas tejas tattveśasamatāṃ vrajet
13.29cd: prabhāhatatamojālaṃ vidhūmāgnisamaprabham
13.30ab: tatraiva sakalaṃ dhyāyet tatpatitvam avāpnuyāt
13.30cd: divasāgniprabhākāraṃ tatra tejo vicintayet
13.31ab: tanmantreśvaratām eti tatra susthiratām gataḥ
13.31cd: maṇipradīpasaṃkāśaṃ tejas tatra prakāśayet
13.32ab: mantreśeśatvam abhyeti yogī tanmayatāṃ gataḥ
13.32cd: sabāhyābhyantaraṃ tejo dhyāyan sarvatra tadgataḥ
13.33ab: tasmān na cyavate sthānād āsaṃhāram akhaṇḍitaḥ
13.33cd: saṃhāre tu paraṃ śāntaṃ padam abhyeti śāṅkaram
13.34ab: ity eṣā pañcadaśadhā kathitā vahnidhāraṇā
13.34cd: svadehaṃ cintayet kṛṣṇaṃ vṛttaṃ ṣaḍbindulāñchitam
13.35ab: calaṃ sacūcūśabdaṃ ca vāyavīṃ dhāraṇāṃ śritaḥ
13.35cd: calatvaṃ kaphajavyādhivicchedād vāyuvad bhavet
13.36ab: ṣaṇmāsam abhyased yogī tadgatenāntarātmanā
13.36cd: yojanānāṃ śataṃ gatvā muhūrtād ety akhedataḥ
13.37ab: vatsarais tu tribhiḥ sākṣād vāyurūpadharo bhavet
13.37cd: cūrṇayaty adrisaṃghātaṃ vṛkṣān unmūlayaty api
13.38ab: kruddhaś cālayate śakraṃ sabhṛtyabalavāhanam
13.38cd: nīlāñjananibhaṃ deham ātmīyam anucintayet
13.39ab: pūrvoktaṃ sarvam āpnoti ṣaṇmāsān nātra saṃśayaḥ
13.39cd: tryabdāt prapaśyate vāyu tattvaṃ tanmayatāṃ gataḥ
13.40ab: bhruvor madhye smared rūpam ātmano 'ñjanasaṃnibham
13.40cd: paśyate vāyutattveśān āśugān akhilān api
13.41ab: ghanāvṛtendranīlābharavibimbasamākṛtim
13.41cd: dhyāyaṃs tatsamatām eti tatsaṃlīno yadā bhavet
13.42ab: bhinnendranīlasaṃkāśaṃ sakalaṃ tatra cintayet
13.42cd: tanmantreśatvam āpnoti tatas tasyeśatām api
13.43ab: sarvavyāpini tadvarṇe dhyāte tejasy avāpnuyāt
13.43cd: tadāpradhṛṣyatām eti tatrādhordhvavisarpiṇi
13.44ab: itīyaṃ kathitā divyā dhāraṇā vāyusambhavā
13.44cd: svadehaṃ vāyuvad dhyātvā tadabhāvam anusmaran
13.45ab: divasaiḥ saptabhir yogī śūnyatāṃ pratipadyate
13.45cd: māsamātreṇa bhogīndrair api daṣṭo na muhyati
13.46ab: sarvavyādhiparityakto valīpalitavarjitaḥ
13.46cd: ṣaṇmāsād gaganākāraḥ sūkṣmarandhrair api vrajet
13.47ab: vatsaratritayāt sākṣād vyomavac ca bhaviṣyati
13.47cd: icchayaiva mahākāyaḥ sūkṣmadehas tathecchayā
13.48ab: acchedyaś cāpy abhedyaś ca cchidrāṃ paśyati medinīm
13.48cd: śatapuṣparasocchiṣṭam ūṣāgarbhakhavan nijam
13.49ab: dehaṃ cintayatas tryabdād vyomajñānaṃ prajāyate
13.49cd: pūrvoktaṃ ca phalaṃ sarvaṃ saptāhādikam āpnuyāt
13.50ab: lalāṭe cintayet tadvad dvādaśāṅgulam āyatam
13.50cd: tattattveśān kramāt sarvān prapaśyaty agrataḥ sthitān
13.51ab: rāhugrastendubimbābhaṃ dhyāyaṃs tatsamatāṃ vrajet
13.51cd: sakalaṃ candrabimbābham tatrastham anucintayet
13.52ab: tanmantreśatvam āpnoti jyotsnayā cendratām api
13.52cd: tayaivādhovisarpiṇyā sabāhyābhyantaraṃ budhaḥ
13.53ab: mantreśvareśatām āpya vijñānam atulaṃ labhet
13.53cd: tayā cordhvavisarpiṇyā jyotsnayāmṛtarūpayā
13.54ab: svatantratvam anuprāpya na kva cit pratihanyate
13.54cd: ity evaṃ pañcatattvānāṃ dhāraṇāḥ parikīrtitāḥ
13.55ab: śuddhādyasthā tu saṃvittir bhūtāveśo 'tra pañcadhā
13.55cd: tāsv eva saṃdadhac cittaṃ viṣādikṣaya ātmanaḥ
13.56ab: anyasyām api saṃvittau yasyām eva nijecchayā
13.56cd: cetaḥ samyak sthirīkuryāt tayā tatphalam aśnute
13.57ab: ekāpi bhāvyamāneyam avāntaravibhedataḥ
13.57cd: antarāyatvam abhyeti tatra kuryān na saṃsthitim
13.58ab: saṃsthitiṃ tatra kurvanto na prāpsyanty uttamaṃ phalam
13.58cd: dhāraṇāpañcake siddhe piśācādyā guṇāṣṭakāḥ
13.59ab: aindrāntāḥ pañca siddhyanti yogināṃ bhedato 'pi vā
13.59cd: iṣṭāḥ pañcadaśāvasthāḥ krameṇaiva samabhyasan
13.60ab: tryabdād ādyāṃ prasādhyānyāṃ dvābhyām ekena cāparām
13.60cd: ṣaṇmāsāt pañcabhiś cānyāṃ caturbhis tribhir eva ca
13.61ab: dvābhyām ekena pakṣeṇa daśabhiḥ pañcabhir dinaiḥ
13.61cd: tribhir dvābhyām athaikena vyastecchoḥ pūrvavat kramaḥ
13.62ab: śāśvataṃ padam āpnoti bhuktvā siddhiṃ yathepsitām
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre bhūtajayādhikāras trayodaśaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirteenth chapter, on the conquest of elements (<s>bhūtajaya</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: tanmātradhāraṇādhikāraś caturdaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The Fourteenth Chapter: On the Concentration upon Subtle Elements (<s>Tanmātradhāraṇādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
14.1ab: atha gandhādipūrvāṇāṃ tanmātrāṇām anukramāt
14.1cd: dhāraṇāḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi tatphalānāṃ prasiddhaye
14.2ab: pītakaṃ gandhatanmātraṃ turyāśraṃ parvasaṃmitam
14.2cd: nāsārandhrāgragaṃ dhyāyed vajralāñchanalāñchitam
14.3ab: daśamād divasād ūrdhvaṃ yogino 'nanyacetasaḥ
14.3cd: kvāpi gandhaḥ samāyāti dvidhābhūto 'py anekadhā
14.4ab: tato 'sya ṛtumātreṇa śuddho gandhaḥ sthirībhavet
14.4cd: ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ svayaṃ gandha maya eva bhaviṣyati
14.5ab: yo yatra rocate gandhas taṃ tatra kurute bhṛśam
14.5cd: tryabdāt siddhim avāpnoti prepsitāṃ pāñcabhautikīm
14.6ab: tadūrdhvam ātmano rūpaṃ tatra saṃcintayed yadi
14.6cd: gandhāvaraṇavijñānaṃ tribhir abdair avāpnuyāt
14.7ab: īṣaddīptiyutaṃ tatra tanmaṇḍalavivarjitam
14.7cd: dhyāyan prapaśyate sarvān gandhāvaraṇavāsinaḥ
14.8ab: dharātattvoktabimbābhaṃ tatraivam anucintayan
14.8cd: tatsamānatvam abhyeti pūrvavad dvitaye sthire
14.9ab: svarūpaṃ tatra saṃcintya bhāsayantam adhaḥsthitam
14.9cd: tadīśatvam avāpnoti pūrvoktenaiva vartmanā
14.10ab: dharātattvoktavat sarvam ata ūrdhvam anusmaran
14.10cd: tadrūpaṃ phalam āpnoti gandhāvaraṇasaṃsthitam
14.11ab: rasarūpām ato vakṣye dhāraṇāṃ yogisevitām
14.11cd: yayā sarvarasāvāptir yoginaḥ saṃprajāyate
14.12ab: jalabudbudasaṃkāśaṃ rājanāḍyagrasaṃsthitaṃ
14.12cd: cintayed rasatanmātraṃ jihvāgrādhāram ātmanaḥ
14.13ab: suśītaṃ ṣaḍrasaṃ snigdhaṃ tadgatenāntarātmanā
14.13cd: tato 'sya māsamātreṇa rasāsvādaḥ pravartate
14.14ab: lavaṇādīn parityajya yadā madhuratāṃ gataḥ
14.14cd: tadā tan nigiran yogī ṣaṇmāsān mṛtyujid bhavet
14.15ab: jarāvyādhivinirmuktaḥ kṛṣṇakeśo 'cyutadyutiḥ
14.15cd: jīved ācandratārārkam abhyasyaṃś ca kva cit kva cit
14.16ab: pūrvoktabudbudākāraṃ svarūpam anucintayan
14.16cd: nīrāvaraṇavijñānam āpnotīti kim adbhutam
14.17ab: tam eva dyutisaṃyuktaṃ dhyāyann ādhāravarjitam
14.17cd: paśyate vatsaraiḥ sarvaṃ rasāvaraṇam āśritam
14.18ab: jalatattvoktabimbādi tadūrdhvam anucintayan
14.18cd: pūrvoktaṃ sarvam āpnoti rasāvaraṇajaṃ sphuṭam
14.19ab: ato rūpavatīṃ vakṣye divyadṛṣṭipradāṃ śubhām
14.19cd: dhāraṇāṃ sarvasiddhyarthaṃ rūpatanmātram āśritām
14.20ab: ekāntastho yadā yogī bahirmīlitalocanaḥ
14.20cd: śaratsaṃdhyābhrasaṃkāśaṃ yat tat kiṃ cit prapaśyati
14.21ab: tatra cetaḥ samādhāya yāvad āste daśāhnikam
14.21cd: tāvat sa paśyate tatra bindūn sūkṣmatamān api
14.22ab: ke cit tatra sitā raktāḥ pītā nīlās tathāpare
14.22cd: tān dṛṣṭvā teṣu saṃdadhyān mano 'tyantam ananyadhīḥ
14.23ab: ṣaṇmāsāt paśyate teṣu rūpāṇi subahūni ca
14.23cd: tryabdāt tāny eva tejobhiḥ pradīptāni sthirāṇi ca
14.24ab: tāny abhyasyaṃs tato dvyabdād bimbākārāṇi paśyati
14.24cd: tato 'bdāt paśyate tejaḥ ṣaṇmāsāt puruṣākṛti
14.25ab: trimāsād vyāpakaṃ tejo māsāt sarvaṃ visarpitam
14.25cd: kālakramāc ca pūrvoktaṃ rūpāvaraṇam āśritam
14.26ab: sarvaṃ phalam avāpnoti divyadṛṣṭiś ca jāyate
14.26cd: itīyaṃ kalpanāśūnyā dhāraṇākṛtakoditā
14.27ab: daśapañcavidho bhedaḥ svayam evātra jāyate
14.27cd: ato 'syāṃ niścayaṃ kuryāt kim anyaiḥ śāstraḍambaraiḥ
14.28ab: ataḥ sparśavatīm anyāṃ kathayāmi tavādhunā
14.28cd: dhāraṇāṃ tu yayā yogī vajradehaḥ prajāyate
14.29ab: ṣaṭkoṇamaṇḍalāntaḥstham ātmānaṃ paribhāvayet
14.29cd: rūkṣam añjanasaṃkāśaṃ pratyaṅgasphuritākulam
14.30ab: tato 'sya daśabhir devi divasais tvaci sarvataḥ
14.30cd: bhavet pipīlikāsparśas tatas tam anucintayan
14.31ab: vajradehatvam āsādya pūrvoktaṃ pūrvaval labhet
14.31cd: pūrvoktamaṇḍalākāraṃ pūrvarūpaṃ vicintayan
14.32ab: sparśatattvāvṛtijñānaṃ labhan kena nivāryate
14.32cd: hīnamaṇḍalam ātmānaṃ dhyāyet tatpatisiddhaye
14.33ab: yayā saṃsiddhayā sarva sparśavedī bhaviṣyati
14.33cd: karṇau pidhāya yatnena nimīlitavilocanaḥ
14.34ab: saṃśṛṇoti mahāghoṣaṃ cetas tatrānusaṃdadhet
14.34cd: dīpyate jāṭharo vahnis tato 'sya daśabhir dinaiḥ
14.35ab: dūrāc chravaṇavijñānaṃ ṣaṇmāsād upajāyate
14.35cd: yas tasyānte dhvanir mandaḥ kiṃ cit kiṃ cid vibhāvyate
14.36ab: sakalātmā sa vijñeyas tadabhyāsād ananyadhīḥ
14.36cd: śabdāvaraṇavijñānam āpnoti sthiratāṃ gatam
14.37ab: yaḥ punaḥ śrūyate śabdas tadante śaṅkhanādavat
14.37cd: pralayākalarūpaṃ tad abhyasyaṃ tatphalepsubhiḥ
14.38ab: sa evātitarām anyaśabdapracchādako yadā
14.38cd: vijñānākala ity uktas tadāsāv aparājite
14.39ab: manohlādakaro yo 'nyas tadante saṃvibhāvyate
14.39cd: sa mantra iti vijñeyo yogibhir yogakāṅkṣibhiḥ
14.40ab: tatas tu śrūyate yo 'nyaḥ śāntaghaṇṭāninādavat
14.40cd: sa mantreśa iti proktaḥ sarvasiddhiphalapradaḥ
14.41ab: ghaṇṭānādavirāmānte yaḥ śabdaḥ saṃprajāyate
14.41cd: mantreśeśapadaṃ tad dhi siddhīnāṃ kāraṇaṃ mahat
14.42ab: anilenāhatā vīṇā yādṛṅ nādaṃ vimuñcati
14.42cd: tādṛśo yo dhvanis tatra taṃ vidyāc chāmbhavaṃ padaṃ
14.43ab: pṛthag vā kramaśo vāpi sarvān etān samabhyaset
14.43cd: prāpnoti sarvavit siddhīḥ śabdāvaraṇam āśritāḥ
14.44ab: ity etāḥ kathitāḥ pañca tanmātrāṇāṃ tu dhāraṇāḥ
body.translated_text:
(14.1) Now I shall declare, in order, the concentrations (<s>dhāraṇā</s>) upon the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra</s>) beginning with smell (<s>gandha</s>), for the attainment of their fruits.
(14.2) One should meditate upon the smell-<s>tanmātra</s> — yellow, of the fourth [triangular] form, measured as a <s>parvan</s> (finger-joint), stationed at the tip of the nostrils, marked with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) emblem.
(14.3) After the tenth day, for the <s>yogin</s> of undivided mind, a fragrance arrives from somewhere — becoming twofold and then manifold.
(14.4) Then, within a season, the pure fragrance becomes stable for him. Within six months, he himself will become pervaded by fragrance.
(14.5) Whatever fragrance pleases [him] wherever, he produces that intensely there. Within three years, he attains the desired <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment) pertaining to the five elements.
(14.6) Beyond that, if he contemplates his own form there, he would attain the knowledge of the smell-envelope (<s>gandhāvaraṇa</s>) within three years.
(14.7) Meditating there [upon it] endowed with slight radiance, devoid of that [outer] sphere, he perceives all beings dwelling in the smell-envelope.
(14.8) Contemplating there a reflection resembling what is described for the earth-<s>tattva</s>, he attains equality with that, as before, when the two [stages] are stabilized.
(14.9) Contemplating one's own form there, illuminating [all] that is below, he attains lordship over that, by the very path previously described.
(14.10) Recollecting all that above, as described for the earth-<s>tattva</s>, he obtains the fruit of that form, stationed in the smell-envelope.
(14.11) I shall now describe the concentration upon taste (<s>rasa</s>), practiced by <s>yogins</s>, by which the <s>yogin</s> attains the acquisition of all tastes.
(14.12) One should contemplate the taste-<s>tanmātra</s> — resembling a water-bubble, stationed at the tip of the royal channel (<s>rāja-nāḍī</s>), supported at the tip of one's own tongue.
(14.13) Cool, possessing the six tastes, unctuous — with one's inner self absorbed in that. Then, within merely a month, the experience of taste arises for him.
(14.14) When, having abandoned salt and the other [tastes], he has attained sweetness, then the <s>yogin</s>, swallowing that, becomes a conqueror of death within six months.
(14.15) Freed from old age and disease, with black hair and unfading radiance, he lives as long as the moon, stars, and sun endure, practicing here and there.
(14.16) Contemplating one's own form in the previously described bubble-shape, one attains the knowledge of the water-envelope (<s>nīrāvaraṇa</s>) — what is surprising in that?
(14.17) Meditating upon that very [form] endowed with radiance, devoid of support, within [some] years one perceives all that belongs to the taste-envelope.
(14.18) Contemplating above that the reflection described for the water-<s>tattva</s> and beyond, one clearly attains all that was previously described, born of the taste-envelope.
(14.19) Now I shall describe the auspicious concentration upon form (<s>rūpa</s>), which grants divine sight (<s>divyadṛṣṭi</s>), for the accomplishment of all <s>siddhis</s>, based on the form-<s>tanmātra</s>.
(14.20) When the <s>yogin</s>, seated in solitude, with eyes half-closed outward, perceives something resembling the clouds at an autumnal twilight,
(14.21) Fixing his mind there, he remains for ten days — then he perceives therein even the most subtle points (<s>bindu</s>).
(14.22) Some of these are white, red, yellow; others blue. Having seen them, he should fix his mind upon them with complete single-pointed attention.
(14.23) Within six months, he perceives among them very many forms; within three years, those very [forms] become radiant with splendor and stable.
(14.24) Practicing those, within two years he perceives orb-shaped [forms]; then within a year, he perceives radiance; within six months, a human figure;
(14.25) Within three months, all-pervading radiance; within a month, [radiance] fully diffused. And in the course of time, the previously described [fruit] belonging to the form-envelope
(14.26) — he obtains all fruit, and divine sight (<s>divyadṛṣṭi</s>) arises. Thus is this concentration, free from conceptual construction, arisen from practice.
(14.27) The fifteen-fold division arises here spontaneously. Therefore, one should establish certainty in this — what need is there for the grandiloquence of other <s>śāstras</s>?
(14.28) Now I shall describe to you another [concentration], that of touch (<s>sparśa</s>), by which the <s>yogin</s> attains a <s>vajra</s>-body (diamond body).
(14.29) One should contemplate oneself stationed within a hexagonal <s>maṇḍala</s> — rough, resembling collyrium, agitated with trembling in every limb.
(14.30) Then, O <s>Devī</s>, within ten days, [there arises] a sensation like ants crawling all over the skin. Then, contemplating that,
(14.31) Having attained the state of a <s>vajra</s>-body, one obtains the previously described [fruits] as before. Contemplating the previously described <s>maṇḍala</s>-form and previous appearance,
(14.32) One obtains the knowledge of the touch-<s>tattva</s> envelope — by whom can [such a one] be obstructed? One should meditate upon oneself with a diminished <s>maṇḍala</s> for the attainment of lordship over that [envelope].
(14.33) By which accomplishment one will become a knower of all touches. Having carefully blocked both ears, with eyes closed,
(14.34) One hears a great sound; one should fix the mind there. The gastric fire blazes; then, within ten days,
(14.35) The knowledge of distant hearing arises within six months. That soft sound which is slightly perceived at its end —
(14.36) That should be known as the <s>Sakala</s>-form (the embodied). Through practice of that, with undivided mind, one attains the knowledge of the sound-envelope, having reached stability.
(14.37) The sound that is then heard at its end, like the tone of a conch — that is of the form of <s>Pralayākala</s> (the dissolved); it should be practiced by those desiring its fruit.
(14.38) When that very [sound], surpassing [all others], conceals other sounds, O invincible one, then it is called <s>Vijñānākala</s> (the pure knower).
(14.39) The other [sound] that is perceived at its end, which delights the mind — that should be known by <s>yogins</s> desiring <s>yoga</s> as the <s>Mantra</s> [level].
(14.40) Then another [sound] that is heard, like the tone of a gently [struck] bell — that is called <s>Mantreśa</s> (Lord of <s>Mantras</s>), bestowing the fruit of all <s>siddhis</s>.
(14.41) The sound that arises at the cessation of the bell-tone — that is indeed the level of <s>Mantreśeśa</s> (Lord of <s>Mantra</s>-Lords), the great cause of [all] <s>siddhis</s>.
(14.42) The sound resembling that which an unstruck <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) releases — that sound [heard] there, one should know as the <s>Śāmbhava</s> (of <s>Śambhu</s>) level.
(14.43) Either separately or in sequence, one should practice all these. One obtains all-knowing <s>siddhis</s> belonging to the sound-envelope.
(14.44) Thus have been described these five concentrations upon the <s>tanmātras</s> (subtle elements).

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre tanmātradhāraṇādhikāraś caturdaśaḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, on concentration upon the subtle elements (<s>tanmātra-dhāraṇā</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: akṣadhāraṇādhikāraḥ pañcadaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The Fifteenth Chapter: On Concentration upon the Senses (<s>Akṣa-dhāraṇādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
15.1ab: atha vāgindriyādīnāṃ manontānām anukramāt
15.1cd: dhāraṇāḥ saṃpravakṣyāmi daśaikāñ ca samāsataḥ
15.2ab: vadanāntar namaḥśabdam ātmanaś cintayed budhaḥ
15.2cd: gṛhītavāktvam abhyeti maunena madhusūdani
15.3ab: sarvatrāskhalitā vāṇī ṣaḍbhir māsaiḥ pravartate
15.3cd: sarvaśāstrārthavettṛtvaṃ vatsarād upajāyate
15.4ab: vāg evāsya pravarteta kāvyālaṅkārabhūṣitā
15.4cd: tribhir abdaiḥ svayaṃ kartā śāstrāṇāṃ saṃprajāyate
15.5ab: tatraiva cintayed dehaṃ svakīyam anurūpataḥ
15.5cd: bhūyas tam eva dhavalam īṣattejovabhāsitam
15.6ab: rasāntaḥsomabimbāditejontaṃ tam anusmaret
15.6cd: sarvaṃ phalam avāpnoti vāgāvaraṇajaṃ kramāt
15.7ab: pāṇau cittaṃ samādāya ṣaṇmāsād dūrasaṃsthitam
15.7cd: vastu gṛhṇāty asaṃdehāt tryabdāt pāre 'pi vāridheḥ
15.8ab: tatrātmadehapūrvaṃ tu padmābham anucintayan
15.8cd: savyāpārādibhedena caturdaśakam ādarāt
15.9ab: puroktakālaniyamāt pūrvoktenaiva vartmanā
15.9cd: sarvaṃ phalam avāpnoti hastāvṛtisamāśritam
15.10ab: pādāv evaṃvidhau dhyāyan vatsaratrayam ādarāt
15.10cd: muhūrtena samudrāntām aśrānto bhramati kṣitim
15.11ab: caturdaśa samabhyarcya svadehādikam abhyasan
15.11cd: prāpnoti pūrvavat sarvaṃ phalaṃ pādāvṛtisthitam
15.12ab: pāyāv api manastattvaṃ sthirīkurvann avāpsyati
15.12cd: māsena tadbhavavyādhi vimuktim avilambataḥ
15.13ab: puṇyaślokatvam āpnoti tribhir abdair anādarāt
15.13cd: caturdaśavidhaṃ cātra pūrvavat phalam āpsyati
15.14ab: svarūpataḥ smarel liṅgaṃ māsamātrāj jitendriyaḥ
15.14cd: ṣaḍbhir māsair anāyāsād icchākāmitvam āpnuyāt
15.15ab: caturdaśavidhe bhede tatrābhyaste mahāmatiḥ
15.15cd: liṅgāvaraṇajaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvaval labhate phalam
15.16ab: svajihvām induvarṇābhāṃ cintayed daśabhir dinaiḥ
15.16cd: prāpnoty anubhavaṃ yogī jihvābhāvam ivātmanaḥ
15.17ab: āsvādayati dūrasthaṃ ṣaṇmāsād ekamānasaḥ
15.17cd: vatsarais tu tribhiḥ sākṣāl leḍhy asau paramāmṛtam
15.18ab: yenāsau bhavate yogī jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ
15.18cd: apeyādiprasakto 'pi na pāpaiḥ paribhūyate
15.19ab: pūrvavat sarvam anyac ca svadehādy anucintayan
15.19cd: phalam āpnoty asaṃdehād rasanāvṛtisaṃbhavam
15.20ab: kanakābhaṃ svakaṃ ghrāṇam anucintayataḥ śanaih
15.20cd: divasair daśabhir ghrāṇaśunyatānubhavo bhavet
15.21ab: ṣaṇmāsād gandham āghrāti dūrasthasyāpi vastunaḥ
15.21cd: ghātayed gandham āghrāya yasya ruṣṭo bhaviṣyati
15.22ab: vatsarais tu tribhir divyaṃ gandham āsādya yogavit
15.22cd: jarāmaraṇanairguṇyayukto divyatvam arhati
15.23ab: sarvam anyad yathoddiṣṭaṃ tathaiva ca vicintayet
15.23cd: kramikaṃ phalam āpnoti ghrāṇāvaraṇam āsthitam
15.24ab: udayādityasaṃkāśe cintayaṃś cakṣuṣī nije
15.24cd: daśāhāc cakṣuṣo raktasrāvānubhavam āpsyati
15.25ab: vedanā mahatī cāsya lalāṭe saṃprajāyate
15.25cd: na bhetavyaṃ mahādevi na cābhyāsaṃ parityajet
15.26ab: saṃtyajann andhatām eti tena yatnāt samabhyaset
15.26cd: ṣaḍbhir māsair mahāyogī divyadṛṣṭiḥ prajāyate
15.27ab: chidrāṃ prapaśyate bhūmiṃ kaṭāhāntām atandritaḥ
15.27cd: ādhruvāntam athordhvaṃ ca karāmalakavad budhaḥ
15.28ab: vatsarais tu tribhir yogī brahmāṇḍāntaṃ prapaśyati
15.28cd: tadantar yoginījñānaṃ śarīrasthaṃ prajāyate
15.29ab: svadehādikam anyac ca pūrvoktaṃ pūrvavat smaran
15.29cd: nayanāvṛtijaṃ sarvam āpnotīti kim adbhutam
15.30ab: sarvatrāñjanapatrābhāṃ nistaraṅgāṃ tvacaṃ smaran
15.30cd: śastrair api na māsena chettuṃ śakyo bhaviṣyati
15.31ab: ṣaṇmāsād atitīvreṇa nāgnināpy eṣa dahyate
15.31cd: vatsaratritayād yogī vajropalaviṣāhibhiḥ
15.32ab: pīḍyate na kadā cit syād ajarāmaratāṃ gataḥ
15.32cd: sparśāvṛtijavijñāna gītavac ca caturdaśa
15.33ab: bhedāḥ saha phalair jñeyāḥ pūrvakālānusārataḥ
15.33cd: kiṃ tv atra cintayed dehaṃ svadehādibhir āvṛtam
15.34ab: saṃdadhānaḥ svakaṃ cetaḥ śrotrākāśe vicakṣaṇaḥ
15.34cd: dūrāc chravaṇavijñānaṃ ṣaṇmāsād upajāyate
15.35ab: tribhiḥ saṃvatsarair devi brahmāṇḍāntar udīritam
15.35cd: śṛṇoti sa sphuṭaṃ sarvaṃ jarāmaraṇavarjitaḥ
15.36ab: tatrākāśoktavat sarvaṃ svadehādy anucintayet
15.36cd: śrotrāvaraṇajaṃ sarvaṃ phalam āpnoti pūrvavat
15.37ab: manovatīm ato vakṣye dhāraṇāṃ sarvasiddhidām
15.37cd: yayā saṃsiddhayā devi sarvasiddhiphalaṃ labhet
15.38ab: mana eva manuṣyāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ bandhamokṣayoḥ
15.38cd: tasmāt tad abhyasen mantrī yadīcchen mokṣam akṣayam
15.39ab: tad ardhacandrasaṃkāśam adhovaktraṃ hṛdi sthitam
15.39cd: cintayan māsamātreṇa pratibhāṃ pratipatsyate
15.40ab: akasmāt paśyate kiṃ cid akasmāc chṛṇute tathā
15.40cd: sarvendriyātmakaṃ jñānaṃ akasmāc ca kva cit kva cit
15.41ab: svasvakendriyavijñānaṃ saṃpaśyed vatsaratrayāt
15.41cd: bhavate yogayuktasya yoginaḥ suparisphuṭam
15.42ab: svadehādikam apy atra pūrvoktavad anusmaran
15.42cd: cittāvaraṇavijñānaṃ prāpya somaguṇaṃ labhet
15.43ab: ity ekādaśa gītāni samabhyasyāni te tathā
15.43cd: indriyāṇi yataḥ sarvaṃ phalam eṣu pratiṣṭhitam
15.44ab: bandhamokṣāv ubhāv etāv indriyāṇi jagur budhāḥ
15.44cd: vigṛhītāni bandhāya vimuktāni vimuktaye
15.45ab: etāni vyāpake bhāve yadā syur manasā saha
15.45cd: vimuktānīti vidvadbhir jñātavyāni tadā priye
15.46ab: yadā tu viṣaye kvāpi pradeśāntaravartini
15.46cd: saṃsthitāni tadā tāni baddhānīti pracakṣate
15.47ab: ity ayaṃ dvividho bhāvaḥ śuddhāśuddhaprabhedataḥ
15.47cd: indriyāṇāṃ samākhyātaḥ siddhayogīśvarīmate
body.translated_text:
15.1ab: Now I shall briefly expound the eleven <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations)
15.1cd: for the sense organs (<s>indriya</s>) beginning with speech, ending with mind, in sequence.
15.2ab: The wise one should contemplate the sound '<s>namaḥ</s>' within the mouth, of one's own self;
15.2cd: through silence, O <s>Madhusūdanī</s>, one attains the mastery of speech.
15.3ab: In six months, unfailing speech flows forth everywhere;
15.3cd: from a year onward, the ability to know the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s> arises.
15.4ab: His speech alone would flow forth, adorned with poetic ornaments (<s>kāvyālaṅkāra</s>);
15.4cd: in three years, he becomes a self-made author of <s>śāstras</s>.
15.5ab: In that same [mouth], one should visualize one's own body in its proper form,
15.5cd: then that same [body] as white, slightly illumined with radiance,
15.6ab: one should meditate on it as ending in the radiance of the moon-disc within the essence;
15.6cd: one obtains all fruits arising from the covering of speech, in sequence.
15.7ab: Placing the mind on the hand, in six months one grasps
15.7cd: an object situated far away, without doubt; in three years, even beyond the ocean.
15.8ab: Therein, beginning with one's own body, contemplating [it] as lotus-colored,
15.8cd: with the distinction of operation and so forth, the fourteen [aspects], with diligence,
15.9ab: according to the previously stated time-rules, through the path described before,
15.9cd: one obtains all fruits situated in the covering of the hands.
15.10ab: Meditating on the two feet in this manner for three years with diligence,
15.10cd: in a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), one traverses the earth up to the ocean's end, untired.
15.11ab: Having practiced the fourteen [aspects] beginning with one's own body,
15.11cd: one obtains, as before, all fruits situated in the covering of the feet.
15.12ab: Establishing the mind-principle (<s>manas-tattva</s>) even in the organ of excretion, one will attain
15.12cd: freedom from diseases arising therefrom, without delay, in one month.
15.13ab: One attains the state of being praised [in verse] (<s>puṇyaślokatva</s>) in three years, effortlessly;
15.13cd: and here too one will obtain the fourteen kinds of fruit as before.
15.14ab: Contemplating the generative organ (<s>liṅga</s>) in its natural form, the one who has conquered the senses, in merely a month;
15.14cd: in six months, without effort, one would attain the power of fulfilling desires at will.
15.15ab: When practiced in the fourteen-fold distinction, the great-minded one
15.15cd: obtains all fruit arising from the covering of the generative organ, as before.
15.16ab: Contemplating one's own tongue as moon-colored for ten days,
15.16cd: the <s>yogin</s> attains the experience of the tongue's disappearance, as it were, of the self.
15.17ab: In six months, with concentrated mind, one tastes [flavors of objects] situated far away;
15.17cd: in three years, one directly licks the supreme <s>amṛta</s> (nectar),
15.18ab: by which that <s>yogin</s> becomes free from old age and death;
15.18cd: even if engaged in [consuming] what is improper to drink, one is not overcome by sins.
15.19ab: Everything else as before, contemplating beginning with one's own body—
15.19cd: one obtains, without doubt, the fruit arising from the covering of the tongue.
15.20ab: Gradually contemplating one's own nose as golden-colored,
15.20cd: in ten days, the experience of the nose's voidness arises.
15.21ab: In six months, one smells the fragrance of an object situated far away;
15.21cd: by smelling [a person's] scent, one can destroy the one toward whom one is angered.
15.22ab: In three years, the knower of <s>yoga</s>, having obtained a divine fragrance,
15.22cd: endowed with freedom from old age, death, and deficiency, becomes worthy of divine status.
15.23ab: Everything else, as previously described, one should contemplate in the same manner;
15.23cd: one obtains sequentially the fruit situated in the covering of the nose.
15.24ab: Contemplating one's own two eyes as resembling the rising sun,
15.24cd: in ten days, one will attain the experience of a flow of blood from the eyes.
15.25ab: And a great pain arises in the forehead;
15.25cd: one should not be afraid, O Great Goddess, nor should one abandon the practice.
15.26ab: Abandoning [the practice], one becomes blind; therefore one should practice with effort.
15.26cd: In six months, the great <s>yogin</s> attains divine vision.
15.27ab: The diligent one sees the earth with its chasms, up to the bottom of the cosmic bowl;
15.27cd: and upward to the pole-star, like a myrobalan fruit in the hand, the wise one [sees].
15.28ab: In three years, the <s>yogin</s> sees [everything] up to the end of the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>);
15.28cd: within that, the knowledge of <s>yoginīs</s> dwelling in the body arises.
15.29ab: Everything else beginning with one's own body, remembering as previously stated—
15.29cd: one obtains all [fruits] arising from the covering of the eyes; what wonder is there?
15.30ab: Contemplating the skin everywhere as resembling a collyrium-leaf, waveless,
15.30cd: within a month, one cannot be cut even by weapons.
15.31ab: In six months, one is not burned even by the most intense fire;
15.31cd: in three years, the <s>yogin</s> is never afflicted by thunderbolts, stones, poison, or serpents,
15.32ab: having attained the state of being without old age and death.
15.32cd: The fourteen distinctions of knowledge arising from the covering of touch,
15.33ab: together with their fruits, should be known following the time-sequence described before;
15.33cd: but here one should contemplate the body as enveloped by one's own bodies and so forth.
15.34ab: The discerning one, placing one's own mind in the space of the ear (<s>śrotrākāśa</s>),
15.34cd: knowledge of hearing from afar arises in six months.
15.35ab: In three years, O Goddess, one hears clearly everything
15.35cd: uttered within the cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>), free from old age and death.
15.36ab: Therein, everything should be contemplated as described for [the element of] space, beginning with one's own body;
15.36cd: one obtains all fruits arising from the covering of the ear, as before.
15.37ab: Now I shall describe the <s>dhāraṇā</s> of the mind, which grants all <s>siddhis</s>;
15.37cd: by whose perfection, O Goddess, one obtains the fruit of all <s>siddhis</s>.
15.38ab: The mind alone is the cause of bondage and liberation for human beings;
15.38cd: therefore the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should train it, if one desires imperishable liberation.
15.39ab: Contemplating it as resembling a half-moon, facing downward, situated in the heart,
15.39cd: in merely one month, one attains <s>pratibhā</s> (intuitive insight).
15.40ab: One spontaneously sees something; one spontaneously hears likewise;
15.40cd: knowledge that is the essence of all senses [arises] spontaneously, here and there.
15.41ab: In three years, the <s>yogin</s> united with <s>yoga</s>
15.41cd: sees clearly the knowledge of each sense organ through its own [faculty].
15.42ab: Here also, remembering beginning with one's own body as previously described,
15.42cd: having attained the knowledge of the covering of the mind, one obtains the quality of <s>Soma</s> (the moon).
15.43ab: Thus these eleven [<s>dhāraṇās</s>] have been declared; you should practice them accordingly,
15.43cd: [for they concern] the sense organs, since all fruits are established in these.
15.44ab: Both bondage and liberation—the wise have declared [them to be] the sense organs:
15.44cd: when seized [by objects], they lead to bondage; when liberated, to liberation.
15.45ab: When these [sense organs], together with the mind, abide in the all-pervading state,
15.45cd: they should be known by the wise as liberated, O dear one.
15.46ab: But when they are established in any sense-object, in some other location,
15.46cd: then they are declared to be bound.
15.47ab: Thus this twofold condition of the sense organs has been proclaimed,
15.47cd: according to the distinction of pure and impure, in the doctrine of the <s>Siddhayogīśvarī</s>.

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre 'kṣadhāraṇādhikāraḥ pañcadaśaḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, on concentration upon the senses (<s>akṣa-dhāraṇā</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: dhāraṇādhikāraḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The Sixteenth Chapter: On Concentration (<s>Dhāraṇādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
16.1ab: atha garvamayīṃ divyāṃ dhāraṇāṃ dhāraṇottamām
16.1cd: mahāgarvakarīṃ vakṣye yogināṃ yogavandite
16.2ab: ṣoḍaśāraṃ smarec cakram ātmadeham ananyadhīḥ
16.2cd: eṣo 'ham iti saṃcintya svakāryaparivāritam
16.3ab: apradhṛṣyo bhaved yogī vatsaratritayena tu
16.3cd: mamatvam acyutaṃ tasya bhavet sarvatra kutra cit
16.4ab: tādṛgrūpasya cakrasya nābhiṃ mūrtiṃ svakāṃ smaran
16.4cd: cintayet sarvam evāhaṃ mayi sarvam avasthitam
16.5ab: tato 'haṅkāravijñānaṃ prāpnotīti kim adbhutam
16.5cd: hṛccakre samanudhyāyan matsvarūpam atandritaḥ
16.6ab: avilambam avāpnoti garvāvaraṇajaṃ phalam
16.6cd: bimbādikaṃ kramāt sarvaṃ cintayan nīlalohitam
16.7ab: tadbhavaṃ sarvam āpnoti daśāvasthāpracoditam
16.7cd: iti garvamayī proktā prajāpatiguṇapradā
16.8ab: udyadādityabimbābhaṃ hṛdi padmam anusmaran
16.8cd: dharmādibhāvasaṃyuktam aṣṭapatraṃ sakarṇikam
16.9ab: māsena sthirabuddhiḥ syāt ṣaḍbhiḥ śrutidharo bhavet
16.9cd: tribhir abdaiḥ svayaṃ kartā śāstrāṇāṃ saṃprajāyate
16.10ab: svāṃ tatra cintayen mūrtiṃ buddhitattvaṃ prapaśyati
16.10cd: tadīśajñānam āpnoti brahmāṇam anucintayan
16.11ab: vedān udgirate suptaḥ samādhistho 'thavā muniḥ
16.11cd: susthirās te sadābhyāsād anadhītā api sphuṭam
16.12ab: bimbādikaṃ kramāt sarvaṃ pūrvoktam anucintayan
16.12cd: prāpnoti brāhmam aiśvaryaṃ buddhyāvaraṇam āśritam
16.13ab: hṛdi bimbaṃ raver dhyāyet tadantaḥ somamaṇḍalam
16.13cd: evam abhyasatas tasya ṣaṇmāsād upajāyate
16.14ab: divyacakṣur anāyāsāt siddhiḥ syād vatsaratrayāt
16.14cd: svadehaṃ cintayaṃs tatra guṇajñānam avāpsyati
16.15ab: liṅgākāraṃ smaran dīptaṃ tadīśatvam avāpnuyāt
16.15cd: bimbādi pūrvavad dhyāyan daśakaṃ daśakātmakam
16.16ab: phalam āpnoty asaṃdehād guṇāvaraṇasaṃsthitam
16.16cd: caturviṃśaty amī proktāḥ pratyekaṃ daśapañcadhā
16.17ab: dhāraṇāḥ kṣmāditattvānāṃ samāsād yogināṃ hitāḥ
16.17cd: trayodaśātmake bhede ṣaḍ anyāḥ saṃsthitā yathā
16.18ab: yoginām anuvarṇyante tathā yogaprasiddhaye
16.18cd: dehaṃ muktvā svarūpeṇa nānyat kiṃ cid iti smaret
16.19ab: sitapadmāsanāsīnaṃ maṇḍalatritayopari
16.19cd: evam atra sthirībhūte māsamātreṇa yogavit
16.20ab: sarvavyādhivinirmukto bhavatīti kim adbhutam
16.20cd: ṣaṇmāsād asya vijñānaṃ jāyate pṛthivītale
16.21ab: abdāj jarādinirmuktas tribhiḥ puṃstattvadṛg bhavet
16.21cd: hṛdadhaḥ paṅkaje 'traiva dvādaśārdhāṅgulāṃ tanum
16.22ab: hṛdantāṃ bhāvayet svākyāṃ ṣaṇmāsān mṛtyujid bhavet
16.22cd: tribhir abdaiḥ samāpnoti puṃstattveśvaratulyatām
16.23ab: bimbādau pūrvavat sarvaṃ tatra saṃcintite sati
16.23cd: phalam āpnoty asaṃdehāt puruṣāvaraṇasthitam
16.24ab: etad vedāntavijñānaṃ samāsād upavarṇitam
16.24cd: kapilasya purā proktam etad vistaraśo mayā
16.25ab: śaratsaṃdhyābhrasaṃghābhaṃ svadeham anucintayan
16.25cd: vītarāgatvam abhyeti ṣaḍbhir māsair na saṃśayaḥ
16.26ab: jarāmaraṇanirmukto varṣeṇaivopajāyate
16.26cd: tryabdāj jñānam avāpnoti rāgāvaraṇajaṃ mahat
16.27ab: raktaṃ saṃcintayed dehaṃ saṃpūrṇābhroparisthitam
16.27cd: māsaṣaṭkam anudvigno vītarāgatvasiddhaye
16.28ab: smaran saṃvatsare samyaṅ mṛtyunā na prapīḍyate
16.28cd: tribhir abdair jitadvandvo rāge ca samatāṃ vrajet
16.29ab: raktapadmasthitaṃ raktaṃ pañcaparvaṃ hṛdāvadhi
16.29cd: dhyāyan phalam avāpnoti pūrvoktam akhilaṃ kramāt
16.30ab: bimbādi cātra pūrvoktam anucintayato muhuḥ
16.30cd: phalaṃ bhavati niḥśeṣaṃ rañjakāvṛtisaṃbhavam
16.31ab: hṛdi padmaṃ sitaṃ dhyāyed dvyaṣṭapatraṃ sakesaram
16.31cd: sarvāmṛtamayaṃ divyaṃ candrakalpitakarṇikam
16.32ab: niścalaṃ tatra saṃyamya ceto nidrāntam ātmanaḥ
16.32cd: tato yat paśyate svapne tathyaṃ tat tasya jāyate
16.33ab: evam abhyasatas tasya buddhipadmoditaṃ phalam
16.33cd: sarvaṃ prajāyate tasya tatkālakramayogataḥ
16.34ab: caturaṅguladehādi sarvaṃ tatra vicintayan
16.34cd: pūrvavat sarvam āpnoti vidyātattvasamudbhavam
16.35ab: hṛdayād ekam ekaṃ tu vyatikramyārdham aṅgulam
16.35cd: pṛthak cakratrayaṃ dhyāyed raktanīlāsitaṃ kramāt
16.36ab: tatratyadvyekaparvaṃ tu puruṣaṃ tatsamadyutim
16.36cd: bimbādikaṃ ca yat proktaṃ tattvatrayam idaṃ mahat
16.37ab: trayodaśātmakaṃ bhedam etadantaṃ vidur budhāḥ
16.37cd: ekādaśaprabhedena tattvadvayam athocyate
16.38ab: kaṇṭhakūpāvadhau cakre pañcāre nābhisaṃsthitam
16.38cd: dhyāyet svarūpam ātmīyaṃ dīptanetropalabdhavat
16.39ab: kṣityādikālatattvānte yad vastu sthitam adhvani
16.39cd: sarvaṃ prasādhya yogīndro na kālenābhibhūyate
16.40ab: bimbādike 'pi tatrasthe yoginām anucintite
16.40cd: bhavatīti kilāścaryam anāyāsena tatphalam
16.41ab: kaṇṭhākāśe sthiraṃ cetaḥ kurvan yogī dine dine
16.41cd: māyotthaṃ phalam āpnoti bimbādāv api tatrage
16.42ab: kaṇṭhakūpavidhānābhaṃ rāhugrastendubimbavat
16.42cd: cintayan na punar yāti māyāder vaśavartitām
16.43ab: tad eva tatra svarbhānumuktavat paricintayan
16.43cd: tejodehādikaṃ cāpi prāpnoti parameśatām
16.44ab: madhyandinakarākāraṃ lambakasthaṃ vicintayet
16.44cd: samastamantracakrasya rūpaṃ yat sāmudāyikam
16.45ab: tataḥ kālakramād yogī mantratvam adhigacchati
16.45cd: anuṣaṅgaphalaṃ cātra pūrvoktaṃ sarvam iṣyate
16.46ab: mūrtiṃ tatraiva saṃcintya mantreśatvam avāpnuyāt
16.46cd: tadadhodīpakaṃ tejo dhyātvā tatpatitāṃ vrajet
16.47ab: sabāhyābhyantaraṃ tasmād adhordhvaṃ vyāpi ca smaran
16.47cd: tejo mantreśvareśānapadān na cyavate naraḥ
16.48ab: baddhvā padmāsanaṃ yogī parābījam anusmaran
16.48cd: bhruvor madhye nyasec cittaṃ tadbahiḥ kiṃ cid agrataḥ
16.49ab: nimīlitākṣo hṛṣṭātmā śabdālokavivarjite
16.49cd: paśyate puruṣaṃ tatra dvādaśāṅgulam āyatam
16.50ab: tatra cetaḥ sthiraṃ kuryāt tato māsatrayopari
16.50cd: sarvāvayavasaṃpūrṇaṃ tejorūpam acañcalam
16.51ab: prasannam indusaṃkāśaṃ paśyati divyacakṣuṣā
16.51cd: taṃ dṛṣṭvā puruṣam divyaṃ kālajñānaṃ pravartate
16.52ab: aśiraske bhaven mṛtyuḥ ṣaṇmāsābhyantareṇa tu
16.52cd: vañcanaṃ tatra kurvīta yatnāt kālasya yogavit
16.53ab: brahmarandhropari dhyāyec candrabimbam akalmaṣam
16.53cd: sravantam amṛtaṃ divyaṃ svadehāpūrakaṃ bahu
16.54ab: tenāpūritam ātmānaṃ cetonālānusarpiṇā
16.54cd: sabāhyābhyantaraṃ dhyāyan daśāhān mṛtyujid bhavet
16.55ab: mahāvyādhivināśe 'pi yogam enaṃ samabhyaset
16.55cd: pratyaṅgavyādhināśāya pratyaṅgagam anusmaran
16.56ab: dhūmravarṇaṃ yadā paśyen mahāvyādhis tadā bhavet
16.56cd: kṛṣṇe kuṣṭham avāpnoti nīle śītalikābhayam
16.57ab: hīnacakṣuṣi tadrogaṃ nāsāhīne tadātmakam
16.57cd: yad yad aṅgaṃ na paśyeta tatra tadvyādhim ādiśet
16.58ab: ātmano vā pareṣāṃ vā yogī yogapathe sthitaḥ
16.58cd: varṣais tu pañcabhiḥ sarvam vidyātattvāntam īśvari
16.59ab: vetti bhuṅkte ca satataṃ na ca tasmāt prahīyate
16.59cd: tatrasthe tejasi dhyāte sarvadehavisarpiṇi
16.60ab: pūrvoktaṃ sarvam āpnoti tatkālakramayogataḥ
16.60cd: athordhvavyāpini dhyāne tatra tasmād akhaṇḍitaḥ
16.61ab: sarvamantreśvareśatvān na bhūyo 'pi nivartate
16.61cd: evaṃ lalāṭadeśe 'pi mahādīptam anusmaran
16.62ab: prapaśyaty acirād eva varṇāṣṭakayutaṃ kramāt
16.62cd: indranīlapratīkāśaṃ śikhikaṇṭhasamadyuti
16.63ab: rājāvartanibhaṃ cānyat tathā vaiḍūryasaṃnibham
16.63cd: puṣparāganibhaṃ cānyat pravālakasamadyuti
16.64ab: padmarāgapratīkāśam anyac candrasamadyuti
16.64cd: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramāṃ jyotsnāṃ divyajñānaṃ pravartate
16.65ab: vihārapādacārādi tataḥ sarvaṃ pravartate
16.65cd: adhordhvaṃ vyāpini dhyāte na tasmāc cyavate padāt
16.66ab: ity etat sarvam ākhyātaṃ lakṣyabhedavyavasthitam
16.66cd: adhunā cittabhedo 'pi samāsād upadiśyate
16.67ab: piśācānantaparyantaguṇāṣṭakasamīhayā
16.67cd: tattadrūpaguṇaṃ kuryāt samyag īśe sthiraṃ manaḥ
16.68ab: itīśvarapadāntasya mārgasyāsya pṛthak pṛthak
16.68cd: yathopāsā tathākhyātā yogināṃ yogasiddhaye
body.translated_text:
(16.1) Now I shall expound the divine concentration imbued with supreme self-awareness (<s>garva</s>), the best of concentrations, which produces great self-awareness — O you who are honored in <s>yoga</s> by <s>yogin</s>s.
(16.2) With single-pointed mind, one should contemplate one's own body as a wheel with sixteen spokes, thinking 'This am I,' surrounded by one's own retinue.
(16.3) The <s>yogin</s> becomes invincible within three years; unfailing self-possession becomes his everywhere, in all circumstances.
(16.4) Contemplating one's own form as the hub of such a wheel, one should think: 'I am everything; everything is established in me.'
(16.5) Then one attains the knowledge of ego-consciousness — what is wondrous in that? Meditating without laziness upon my own form in the heart-wheel,
(16.6) one swiftly obtains the fruit arising from the veil of self-awareness. Contemplating everything in sequence beginning with the [reflected] image, as blue-red,
(16.7) one obtains everything that arises from that, impelled by the ten states. Thus the <s>garva</s>-filled (self-awareness) [concentration] is declared, which bestows the qualities of <s>Prajāpati</s>.
(16.8) Contemplating in the heart a lotus resembling the orb of the rising sun, possessing eight petals and a pericarp, endowed with the dispositions of <s>dharma</s> (virtue) and the rest,
(16.9) in one month the intellect becomes steady; in six [months] one becomes a retainer of scripture. In three years, one spontaneously becomes a creator of <s>śāstra</s>s (treatises).
(16.10) Contemplating one's own form therein, one perceives the <s>buddhi-tattva</s> (principle of intellect). One attains the knowledge of its lord; meditating on <s>Brahmā</s>,
(16.11) the <s>muni</s> (sage), whether asleep or established in <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), recites the <s>Veda</s>s. Through constant practice, they become firmly established — even without formal study, clearly.
(16.12) Contemplating everything previously stated, in sequence beginning with the [reflected] image, one attains the sovereignty of <s>Brahmā</s>, situated within the veil of intellect.
(16.13) One should meditate on the orb of the sun in the heart, and within it the circle of the moon. For one who practices thus, after six months,
(16.14) the divine eye (<s>divya-cakṣus</s>) arises effortlessly; <s>siddhi</s> comes in three years. Contemplating one's own body therein, one will obtain knowledge of the <s>guṇa</s>s (qualities).
(16.15) Contemplating a radiant <s>liṅga</s> form, one would attain lordship over it. Meditating as before on the [reflected] image and so forth, the tenfold [set] of ten,
(16.16) one undoubtedly obtains the fruit situated within the veil of the <s>guṇa</s>s. These twenty-four [concentrations] are declared, each fifteen-fold,
(16.17) as concentrations on the <s>tattva</s>s beginning with earth, summarized for the benefit of <s>yogin</s>s. In the thirteen-fold division, six others are established as follows;
(16.18) they are described for <s>yogin</s>s, for the accomplishment of <s>yoga</s>. Having abandoned the body, one should contemplate in one's own form, nothing else.
(16.19) Seated on a white lotus, upon three circles — thus, when this becomes steady, the knower of <s>yoga</s>, within a mere month,
(16.20) becomes freed from all diseases — what is wondrous in that? In six months, knowledge of the earth-plane arises for him.
(16.21) In a year, freed from old age and the like; in three [years], one becomes a perceiver of the <s>puṃs-tattva</s> (soul-principle). In a lotus below the heart, right here, [one should contemplate] a body of six and a half finger-breadths,
(16.22) extending to the heart, as one's own — in six months one becomes a conqueror of death. In three years one attains equality with the lord of the <s>puṃs-tattva</s>.
(16.23) When everything is contemplated there, beginning with the [reflected] image as before, one undoubtedly obtains the fruit situated within the veil of <s>puruṣa</s> (the individual soul).
(16.24) This knowledge of <s>Vedānta</s> has been described in summary. This was previously taught to <s>Kapila</s>; by me it [is now taught] in detail.
(16.25) Contemplating one's own body as resembling masses of autumnal twilight clouds, one attains freedom from attachment in six months — without doubt.
(16.26) Freedom from old age and death arises within a year. In three years, one attains the great knowledge arising from the veil of attachment (<s>rāga</s>).
(16.27) One should contemplate the body as red, situated upon a complete cloud, for six months without agitation, for the attainment of freedom from attachment.
(16.28) Contemplating thus properly for a year, one is not afflicted by death. In three years, having conquered the pairs of opposites, one attains equanimity regarding attachment.
(16.29) Meditating on [a form] red, situated on a red lotus, five joints [in extent] up to the heart, one obtains all the previously stated fruit in sequence.
(16.30) And contemplating repeatedly the [reflected] image and so forth as stated before here, the complete fruit arises, born from the veil of the coloring [principle] (<s>rañjaka</s>).
(16.31) One should meditate on a white lotus in the heart, with sixteen petals and stamens, entirely composed of nectar, divine, with a pericarp fashioned as the moon.
(16.32) Having steadied the mind there, motionless, up to the point of sleep — then whatever one sees in dreams, that becomes true for him.
(16.33) For one who practices thus, all the fruit arising from the lotus of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) is produced, in accordance with the appropriate time and sequence.
(16.34) Contemplating everything there — a four-finger body and so forth — as before, one obtains everything arising from the <s>vidyā-tattva</s> (knowledge principle).
(16.35) One should meditate on three wheels, each separated by half a finger-breadth above the heart, in sequence red, blue, and dark.
(16.36) The <s>puruṣa</s> therein, spanning two or one joints, of the same radiance — and the [reflected] image and so forth as previously described — this great triad of <s>tattva</s>s,
(16.37) the wise know as the thirteen-fold division ending with this. Now the two <s>tattva</s>s in eleven-fold division are described.
(16.38) In the wheel with five spokes, located at the hollow of the throat, situated at the navel, one should meditate on one's own form, as if perceived through blazing eyes.
(16.39) Having perfected everything that exists in the path, from earth to the time-<s>tattva</s>, the lord of <s>yogin</s>s is not overcome by time.
(16.40) When the [reflected] image and so forth, situated there, is contemplated by <s>yogin</s>s, their fruit arises effortlessly — how marvelous indeed!
(16.41) The <s>yogin</s>, making the mind steady day after day in the space of the throat, attains the fruit arising from <s>Māyā</s>, and also when [the mind] is directed toward the [reflected] image and so forth.
(16.42) Contemplating [it as] resembling the arrangement of the throat-hollow, like the moon's disk seized by <s>Rāhu</s>, one does not again fall under the control of <s>Māyā</s> and the rest.
(16.43) Contemplating that very [form] there as if released from <s>Svarbhānu</s> (<s>Rāhu</s>), one attains the body of radiance and so forth — the state of <s>Parameśa</s> (the Supreme Lord).
(16.44) One should contemplate [it] resembling the midday sun, situated at the <s>lambaka</s> (soft palate), the collective form of the entire circle of <s>mantra</s>s.
(16.45) Then, through the process of time, the <s>yogin</s> attains <s>mantra</s>-hood. The incidental fruit here, as previously stated, is all accepted.
(16.46) Contemplating one's own form right there, one would attain <s>Mantreśa</s>-hood (lordship of <s>mantra</s>s). Meditating on the radiance that illuminates below it, one attains the state that has fallen from that.
(16.47) Contemplating the radiance pervading both externally and internally, below and above, a person does not fall from the stations of <s>Mantreśvara</s> and <s>Mantreśvareśa</s>.
(16.48) Having assumed <s>padmāsana</s> (the lotus posture), the <s>yogin</s>, contemplating the supreme seed-mantra (<s>parā-bīja</s>), should place the mind between the eyebrows, slightly outward and in front of it.
(16.49) With eyes closed, with a joyful heart, in [a place] devoid of sound and light, one sees there a <s>puruṣa</s> (being), twelve finger-breadths in extent.
(16.50) One should make the mind steady there; then, after three months, complete in all limbs, of the form of radiance, unmoving,
(16.51) serene, resembling the moon — one sees [it] with the divine eye. Having seen that divine being, knowledge of time arises.
(16.52) If [the being appears] headless, death [will come] within six months. The knower of <s>yoga</s> should strive to deceive death in that case.
(16.53) Above the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (the aperture at the crown), one should meditate on the stainless disk of the moon, streaming copious divine nectar that fills one's own body.
(16.54) Meditating on oneself as filled by that [nectar], creeping along the channel of consciousness, both externally and internally — within ten days one becomes a conqueror of death.
(16.55) For the destruction of great diseases too, one should practice this <s>yoga</s>. For the destruction of disease in each limb, one should contemplate [the nectar flowing] to each limb.
(16.56) When one sees a smoky color, a great disease will arise. If black, one will develop leprosy; if blue, there is danger of smallpox.
(16.57) If the eye is deficient, that disease [will arise]; if the nose is deficient, a disease of that nature. Whatever limb one does not see, one should diagnose that disease there.
(16.58) The <s>yogin</s>, established in the path of <s>yoga</s>, for himself or for others — in five years, everything up to the <s>vidyā-tattva</s> (knowledge principle), O Sovereign Goddess,
(16.59) he knows and enjoys constantly, and does not fall from that [state]. When the radiance pervading the entire body is meditated upon there,
(16.60) one obtains everything previously stated, in accordance with the appropriate time and sequence. When meditating on the upward-pervading [radiance] there, unbroken from that,
(16.61) one does not return again from the lordship over all <s>Mantreśvara</s>s and <s>Mantreśvareśa</s>s. Thus, also in the forehead region, contemplating the greatly blazing [radiance],
(16.62) one sees before long, in sequence, eight colors: resembling an indigo sapphire, of the same radiance as a peacock's throat,
(16.63) and another resembling a <s>rājāvarta</s> (lapis lazuli), and like a <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (cat's eye gem), another resembling a topaz (<s>puṣparāga</s>), of the same radiance as coral,
(16.64) resembling a ruby (<s>padmarāga</s>), and another of the same radiance as the moon. Having seen that supreme moonlight, divine knowledge arises.
(16.65) Flying, walking through the air, and other [powers] — then everything manifests. When meditating on [radiance] pervading below and above, one does not fall from that station.
(16.66) Thus all this has been expounded, established through the differentiation of objects of focus. Now the differentiation of consciousness (<s>citta-bheda</s>) is also taught in summary.
(16.67) Through the endeavor of the eightfold qualities, from <s>Piśāca</s> (spirit) to <s>Ananta</s> (the Infinite), one should make the mind steadily [assume] the respective form and quality [directed toward] the Lord.
(16.68) Thus the worship appropriate to each stage of this path, up to the station of the Lord, has been declared separately for <s>yogin</s>s, for the accomplishment of <s>yoga</s>.'

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre dhāraṇādhikāraḥ ṣoḍaśaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, on concentration (<s>Dhāraṇādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: saptadaśaḥ ṣaḍaṅgayogādhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: The seventeenth chapter: On the Six-Limbed Yoga (<s>Ṣaḍaṅga-yogādhikāra</s>).

body.text:
17.1ab: athaitat sarvam uddiṣṭaṃ yadi na sphuṭatāṃ vrajet
17.1cd: sphuṭīkṛte 'sthire tatra na manas tiṣṭhate sphuṭam
17.2ab: gatibhaṅgaṃ tatas tasya prāṇāyāmena kārayet
17.2cd: sa ca pañcavidhaḥ proktaḥ pūrakādiprabhedataḥ
17.3ab: pūrakaḥ kumbhakaś caiva recako hy apakarṣakaḥ
17.3cd: utkarṣaḥ pañcamo jñeyas tadabhyāsāya yogibhiḥ
17.4ab: pūrakaḥ pūraṇād vāyor dvedhā ṣoḍhā ca gīyate
17.4cd: svabhāvapūraṇād eko virecyānyaḥ prapūritaḥ
17.5ab: nāsāmukhordhvatālūnāṃ randhrabhedād vibhidyate
17.5cd: bhinnaḥ ṣoḍhātvam abhyeti punar bhedair anantatām
17.6ab: kumbhaḥ pañcavidho jñeyas tatraikaḥ pūritād anu
17.6cd: vidhṛto recakāt paścād dvitīyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
17.7ab: dvayor ante dvayaṃ cānyat svabhāvasthaś ca pañcamaḥ
17.7cd: sthānāntaraprabhedena gacchaty eṣo 'py anantatām
17.8ab: recakaḥ pūrvavaj jñeyo dvidhābhūtaḥ ṣaḍātmakaḥ
17.8cd: sthānasaṃstambhito vāyus tasmād utkṛṣya nīyate
17.9ab: yo 'nyapradeśasaṃprāptyai sa utkarṣaka iṣyate
17.9cd: tasmād api punaḥ sthānaṃ yato nītas tadāhṛtaḥ
17.10ab: apakarṣaka ity ukto dvāv apy etāv anekadhā
17.10cd: eṣām abhyasanaṃ kuryāt padmakādyāsanasthitaḥ
17.11ab: adhamaḥ sakṛdudghāto madhyamo dviguṇo mataḥ
17.11cd: jyeṣṭhaḥ syād yas trirudghātaḥ sa ca dvādaśamātrakaḥ
17.12ab: trirjānuveṣṭanān mātrā triguṇāc choṭikātrayāt
17.12cd: ajitāṃ nākramen mātrāṃ vāyudoṣanivṛttaye
17.13ab: pratyaṅgadhāraṇād vāyuṃ na ca cakṣuṣi dhārayet
17.13cd: nābhihṛttālukāntasthe vidhṛte maruti kramāt
17.14ab: catasro dhāraṇā jñeyāḥ śikhyambvīśāmṛtātmikāḥ
17.14cd: yad yatra cintayed dravyaṃ tat tat sarvagataṃ smaret
17.15ab: bindunādātmakaṃ rūpam īśānī dhāraṇā śritā
17.15cd: amṛtāyāṃ smared induṃ kālatyāgoktavartmanā
17.16ab: dhāraṇābhir ihaitābhir yogī yogapathe sthitaḥ
17.16cd: heyaṃ vastu parityajya yāyāt padam anāmayam
17.17ab: trivedadvīndusaṅkhyātasamudghātās tv imā matāḥ
17.17cd: etābhir apy adho 'py uktaṃ phalaṃ prāpnoty anuttamam
17.18ab: yogāṅgatve samāne 'pi tarko yogāṅgam uttamam
17.18cd: heyādyālocanāt tasmāt tatra yatnaḥ praśasyate
17.19ab: mārge cetaḥ sthirībhūtaṃ heye 'pi viṣayecchayā
17.19cd: prerya tenānayet tāvad yāvat padam anāmayam
17.20ab: tadarthabhāvanāyuktaṃ mano dhyānam udāhṛtam
17.20cd: tad eva paramaṃ jñānaṃ bhāvanāmayam iṣyate
17.21ab: muhūrtād eva tatrasthaḥ samādhiṃ pratipadyate
17.21cd: tatrāpi ca suniṣpanne phalaṃ prāpnoty abhīpsitam
17.22ab: yat kiṃ cic cintayed vastu nānyatvaṃ pratipadyate
17.22cd: tena tanmayatām āpya bhavet paścād abhāvavat
17.23ab: pañcatām iva saṃprāptas tīvrair api na cālyate
17.23cd: tataḥ śabdādibhir yogī yoginīkulanandanaḥ
17.24ab: ity anena vidhānena pratyāhṛtya mano muhuḥ
17.24cd: prāṇāyāmādikaṃ sarvaṃ kuryād yogaprasiddhaye
17.25ab: sarvam apy athavā bhogaṃ manyamāno virūpakam
17.25cd: svaśarīraṃ parityajya śāśvataṃ padam ṛcchati
17.26ab: tadā pūrvoditaṃ nyāsaṃ kālānalasamaprabham
17.26cd: viparītavidhānena kuryāt skṛkchindiyuggatam
17.27ab: āgneyīṃ dhāraṇāṃ kṛtvā sarvamarmapratāpinīm
17.27cd: pūrayed vāyunā deham aṅguṣṭhān mastakāntikam
17.28ab: tam utkṛṣya tato 'ṅguṣṭhād brahmarandhrāntam ānayet
17.28cd: chedayet sarvamarmāṇi mantreṇānena yogavit
17.29ab: jīvam ādidvijārūḍhaṃ śiromālādisaṃyutam
17.29cd: kṛtvā tadagre kurvīta dvijam ādyam ajīvakam
17.30ab: ity eṣā kathitā kāla rātrir marmanikṛntanī
17.30cd: naināṃ samuccared devi ya icched dīrghajīvitam
17.31ab: śatārdhoccārayogena jāyate mūrdhni vedanā
17.31cd: evaṃ pratyayam ālocya mṛtyujiddhyānam āśrayet

17.32cd: vegād utkṛṣya tatrasthaṃ kālarātryā visarjayet
17.33ab: anena kramayogena ane yojitaḥ parame pade
17.33cd: samayy api mahādevi dīkṣoktaṃ phalam aśnute
17.34ab: [lacuna] siddhayogeśvarīmate
17.34cd: tatsakāśād bhavet siddhiḥ sarvamantroktalakṣaṇā
17.35ab: tad eva mantrarūpeṇa manuṣyaiḥ samupāsyate
17.35cd: eṣa te jñeyasadbhāvaḥ kathitaḥ suravandite
17.36ab: abhaktasya guhasyāpi nākhyeyo jātucit tvayā
17.36cd: udaraṃ sarvam āpūrya brahmarandhrāntam āgatam
17.37ab: vāyuṃ bhramaṇayogena tatas taṃ prerayet tathā
17.37cd: yāvat prāṇapradeśāntaṃ yogināṃ manasepsitam
17.38ab: prāpyate punar āvṛtya tathaiva nābhimaṇḍalam
17.38cd: evaṃ samabhyaset tāvad yāvad vāsarasaptakam
17.39ab: tadāprabhṛti saṃyuktaḥ karṣayet tridaśān api
17.39cd: anenākṛṣya vijñānaṃ sarvayoginiṣevitam
17.40ab: gṛhṇīyād yogayuktātmā kim anyaiḥ kṣudraśāsanaiḥ
17.40cd: prathamaṃ mahatī ghūrṇir abhyāsāt tasya jāyate
17.41ab: tataḥ prakampo deveśi jvalatīva tato 'py aṇuḥ
body.translated_text:
(17.1) Now, if all this that has been pointed out does not come to clarity, or if, when made clear, the mind does not remain steadily there,
(17.2) Then one should cause the interruption of its movement through <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). That is declared to be fivefold, based on the divisions beginning with <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation).
(17.3) <s>Pūraka</s> (filling), <s>kumbhaka</s> (retention), <s>recaka</s> (exhalation), <s>apakarṣaka</s> (drawing down), and <s>utkarṣa</s> (raising up) should be known as the fifth — for the practice of <s>yogins</s>.
(17.4) <s>Pūraka</s>, from the filling of breath, is said to be twofold and sixfold: one [arises] from natural filling, the other is deliberately filled after exhalation.
(17.5) It is divided according to the different apertures of the nostrils, mouth, upper [palate], and palate. Thus divided, it attains sixfold [variety], and through further divisions, infinitude.
(17.6) <s>Kumbhaka</s> (retention) should be known as fivefold: the first is held after filling; the second is declared as [held] after exhalation.
(17.7) Two others [are held] at the end of both [inhalation and exhalation]; and the fifth is the natural state. Through the division of different locations, this too reaches infinitude.
(17.8) <s>Recaka</s> (exhalation) should be known as before — becoming twofold, of six kinds. When the breath is arrested at a [particular] location, it is then drawn upward from there;
(17.9) That which [is done] for reaching another location is called <s>utkarṣaka</s> (the raiser). And from there again, [returning] to the place from which it was brought —
(17.10) That is called <s>apakarṣaka</s> (the drawer-down); both of these are also manifold. One should practice these while seated in the lotus posture (<s>padmaka</s>) or other <s>āsanas</s>.
(17.11) The lowest [grade] is one expulsion (<s>udghāta</s>); the middle is considered double; the highest would be three expulsions, and that is of twelve <s>mātrās</s> (measures).
(17.12) A <s>mātrā</s> [is measured by] three encirclings of the knee; three [snaps] make a threefold finger-snap. One should not proceed to an unconquered <s>mātrā</s>, to avoid the fault of [disturbing] the breath.
(17.13) Through concentration on each limb, one should hold the breath — but not in the eyes. When the breath is held successively at the navel, heart, and end of the palate,
(17.14) Four <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations) should be known — of the nature of fire (<s>śikhā</s>), water (<s>ambu</s>), the Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), and nectar (<s>amṛta</s>). Whatever substance one contemplates wherever, one should remember that as all-pervading.
(17.15) The form consisting of <s>bindu</s> and <s>nāda</s> — that is the <s>Īśānī</s> concentration. In the <s>amṛta</s> [concentration], one should remember the moon, by the path described for the abandonment of time [i.e., death].
(17.16) Through these <s>dhāraṇās</s>, the <s>yogin</s> established on the path of <s>yoga</s>, having abandoned the object to be discarded, goes to the state free from affliction.
(17.17) These are considered [to have] expulsions numbered as three, four, two, and one [bindu]. Through these too, one obtains the unsurpassed fruit described below.
(17.18) Although equal as limbs of <s>yoga</s>, <s>tarka</s> (reasoned contemplation) is the supreme limb of <s>yoga</s>, because it involves the examination of what is to be abandoned, etc. Therefore, effort therein is praiseworthy.
(17.19) When the mind, though stabilized on the path, is impelled toward what is to be abandoned by desire for objects, one should lead it back until [it reaches] the state free from affliction.
(17.20) The mind engaged in the contemplation of that goal is called <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). That very [state], when supreme, consisting of contemplation, is considered <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge).
(17.21) Within a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), one established there attains <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). When that too is well-perfected, one obtains the desired fruit.
(17.22) Whatever object one contemplates does not assume otherness. Having thereby attained identity with that, one afterward becomes as if non-existent.
(17.23) Having reached a state resembling death, the <s>yogin</s> — the delight of the family of <s>Yoginīs</s> — is not disturbed even by intense sounds and the like.
(17.24) By this method, having repeatedly withdrawn the mind, one should perform all [practices] beginning with <s>prāṇāyāma</s> for the attainment of <s>yoga</s>.
(17.25) Or, considering all enjoyment as distorted, abandoning one's own body, one reaches the eternal state.
(17.26) Then one should perform the previously described <s>nyāsa</s> (placement), radiant as the fire of dissolution (<s>kālānala</s>), in reverse order, stationed at the two corners of the mouth.
(17.27) Having performed the fiery <s>dhāraṇā</s> which burns all the vital points (<s>marma</s>), one should fill the body with breath from the toes to the top of the head.
(17.28) Having drawn that up from the toe, one should bring it to the end of the <s>brahmarandhra</s> (aperture at the crown). The knower of <s>yoga</s> should sever all vital points with this <s>mantra</s>.
(17.29) Having mounted the life-force (<s>jīva</s>) upon the first consonant, joined with the head-garland etc., one should then make the first consonant without the <s>jīva</s> at its tip.
(17.30) This is called the 'Night of Death' (<s>Kālarātri</s>), the cutter of vital points. O <s>Devī</s>, one who desires long life should not utter it.
(17.31) Through the practice of uttering it fifty times, a sensation arises at the crown of the head. Having observed this evidence, one should resort to the meditation that conquers death.
(17.32) Then, pressing that [breath] there, contemplating <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, etc., having forcefully drawn up [the life-force] stationed there, one should release it through <s>Kālarātri</s>.
(17.33) Through this sequential <s>yoga</s>, the one joined to the supreme state — even at the time of death, O <s>Mahādevī</s> — attains the fruit described in <s>dīkṣā</s>.
(17.34) [Lacuna] ...according to the doctrine of <s>Siddhayogeśvarī</s>. From that, <s>siddhi</s> arises, having all the characteristics described for <s>mantras</s>.
(17.35) That very [reality] is worshipped by humans in the form of <s>mantras</s>. This true nature of what is to be known has been told to you, O one praised by the gods.
(17.36) This should never be told by you to one lacking devotion, even to <s>Guha</s> (<s>Skanda</s>). Having filled the entire belly [with breath], brought up to the <s>brahmarandhra</s>,
(17.37) One should then propel that breath by the method of rotation, until it reaches the region of <s>prāṇa</s> — as desired by the minds of <s>yogins</s>.
(17.38) Having reached [there], returning again to the circle of the navel — one should practice thus until seven days [have passed].
(17.39) From that time onward, [the <s>yogin</s>] thus joined can attract even the gods. By this [method], having attracted the knowledge served by all <s>Yoginīs</s>,
(17.40) The one whose self is joined with <s>yoga</s> should seize it — what need is there for other petty teachings? First, a great whirling arises from the practice of that;
(17.41) Then trembling, O queen of the gods; then the individual soul blazes as it were.

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre saptadaśo yogāṅgādhikāraḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the seventeenth chapter, on the limbs of yoga (<s>Yogāṅgādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: paramavidyādhikāro 'ṣṭādaśaḥ
body.translated_text: The eighteenth chapter: On the Supreme Knowledge (<s>Paramavidyādhikāra</s>).

body.text:
18.1ab: śṛṇu devi paraṃ guhyam aprāpyam akṛtātmanām
18.1cd: yan na kasya cid ākhyātaṃ tad adya kathayāmi te
18.2ab: sarvam anyat parityajya cittam atra niveśayet
18.2cd: mṛcchailadhāturatnādibhavaṃ liṅgaṃ na pūjayet
18.3ab: yajed ādhyātmikaṃ liṅgaṃ yatra līnaṃ carācaram
18.3cd: bahir liṅgasya liṅgatvam anenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yataḥ
18.4ab: ataḥ prapūjayed etat paramādvaitam āśritaḥ
18.4cd: anudhyānena deveśi pareṇa paramāṇunā
18.5ab: yo 'nudhyātaḥ sa evaital liṅgaṃ paśyati nāparaḥ
18.5cd: yad etat spandanaṃ nāma hṛdaye samavasthitam % 5
18.6ab: tatra cittaṃ samādhāya kampa udbhava eva ca
18.6cd: tatra praśāntim āpnoti māsenaikena yogavit
18.7ab: hṛdayād utthitaṃ liṅgaṃ brahmarandhrāntam īśvari
18.7cd: svaprabhoddyotitāśeṣadehāntam amaladyuti
18.8ab: tatraiva paśyate sarvaṃ mantrajālaṃ mahāmatiḥ
18.8cd: tanmastakaṃ samāruhya māsamātram ananyadhīḥ
18.9ab: tatas tatra suniṣpanne ṣaṇmāsāt sarvasiddhayaḥ
18.9cd: etal liṅgam avijñāya yo liṅgī liṅgam āśrayet
18.10ab: vṛthāḷpariśramas tasya na liṅgaphalam aśnute
18.10cd: śaivam etan mahāliṅgam ātmaliṅge [na] siddhyati
18.11ab: siddhe 'tra liṅgaval liṅgī liṅgastho liṅgavarjitaḥ
18.11cd: bhavatīti kim āśrayam etasmāl liṅgaliṅitaḥ
18.12ab: anena liṅgaliṅgena yadā yogī bahir vrajet
18.12cd: tadā liṅgīti vijñeyaḥ purāntaṃ liṅgam iṣyate
18.13ab: etasmāl liṅgavijñānād yogino liṅgitāḥ smṛtāḥ
18.13cd: anenādiṣṭhitāḥ mantrāḥ śāntaraudrādibhedataḥ
18.14ab: bhavantīti kimāścaryaṃ tadbhāvagatacetasaḥ
18.14cd: raudraṃ bhāvaṃ samśritya yadi yogaṃ samabhyaset
18.15ab: durnirīkṣyo bhavet sarvaiḥ sadevāsuramānuṣaiḥ
18.15cd: gamāgamavinirmuktaḥ sarvadṛṣṭir akātaraḥ
18.16ab: muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭhate yāvat tāvad eveśam āpnuyāt
18.16cd: āviṣṭaḥ paśyate sarvaṃ sūryakoṭisamadyuti
18.17ab: yat tad akṣaram avyaktaṃ śaivaṃ bhairavam ity api
18.17cd: taṃ dṛṣṭvā vatsarārdhena yogī sarvajñatām iyāt
18.18ab: ya evainaṃ samāsādya yas tṛptim adhigacchati
18.18cd: na ca kṛtrimayogeṣu sa muktaḥ sarvabandhanaiḥ
18.19ab: prāṇāyāmādikair liṅgair yogāḥ syuḥ kṛtrimā matāḥ
18.19cd: tena te 'kṛtakasyāsya kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm
18.20ab: etat samabhyasan yogī divyacihnāni paśyati
18.20cd: upaviṣṭa ṛjur yogī na kiñ cid api cintayet
18.21ab: muhūrtān nirdahet sarvaṃ dehastham akṛtaṃ kṛtam
18.21cd: dahyamānasya tasyeha prakampānubhavo bhavet
18.22ab: tatas tatra sthirībhūte jyotir antaḥ prakāśate
