18.22cd: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā paramāṃ dīptiṃ divyajñānaṃ pravartate
18.23ab: svatantraśivatām eti bhuñjāno viṣayān api
18.23cd: animīlitadivyākṣo yāvad āste muhūrtakam
18.24ab: tasmāt sarvagataṃ bhāvam ātmanaḥ pratipadyate
18.24cd: tam eva bhāvayed yatnāt sarvasiddhiphalepsayā
18.25ab: tatas taṃ bhāvayed yogī kampamāno 'tyanulbaṇam
18.25cd: tataḥ prapaśyate tejo lalāṭāgre samantataḥ
18.26ab: dṛṣṭvā tatparamaṃ tejo divyajñānam avāpnuyāt
18.26cd: ṣaḍbhir māsair anāyāsād vatsareṇa prasiddhyati
18.27ab: śivatulyabalo bhūtvā yatreṣṭaṃ tatra gacchati
18.27cd: cetaḥ sarvagataṃ kṛtvā muhūrtād eva yogavit
18.28ab: śakyāveśam avāpnoti prakampānubhavātmakam
18.28cd: tatas tatra sthirībhūte māsamātreṇa yogavit
18.29ab: śāktaṃ prapaśyate tejaḥ sabāhyābhyantare sthiram
18.29cd: tatra samyak suniṣpanne sarvendriyajam ādarāt
18.30ab: tatra sphuṭam avāpnoti vijñānam anivāritam
18.30cd: sarvagaṃ cātra vijñeyaṃ yad akṣarthena saṃgatam
18.31ab: evamevedam ākhyātaṃ tattvaṃ paryāyabhedataḥ
18.31cd: karmendriyāṇi buddhyantaṃ parityajya samastakam
18.32ab: bhāvayet paramāṃ śaktiṃ sarvatraiva vicakṣaṇaḥ
18.32cd: niścalaṃ tu manaḥ kṛtvā yāvat tanmayatāṃ gataḥ
18.33ab: tāvat sarvagata bhāvaṃ kṣaṇamātrāt prapadyate
18.33cd: nirdahya pāśajālāni yatheṣṭaṃ phalam āpnuyāt
18.34ab: tasmāt samabhyased enaṃ kṛtvā niścayam ātmanaḥ
18.34cd: yatrādhāravinirmukto jīvo layam avāpsyati
18.35ab: tatsthānaṃ sarvamantrāṇām utpattikṣetram iṣyate
18.35cd: dvividhaṃ tatparijñeyaṃ bāhyābhyantarabhedataḥ
18.36ab: prayātavādhikāḷmātrā sā jñeyā sarvasiddhidā
18.36cd: athavā gacchatas tasya svapnavṛttyā vicakṣaṇaḥ
18.37ab: nirodhaṃ madhyame sthāne kurvīta kṣaṇamātrakam
18.37cd: paśyate tatra cicchaktiṃ tuṭimātrām akhaṇḍitām
18.38ab: tad eva paramaṃ tattvaṃ tasmāj jātam idaṃ jagat
18.38cd: sa eva mantradehas tu sidhhayogīśvarīmate
18.39ab: tenaivāliṅgitā mantrāḥ sarvasiddhiphalapradāḥ
18.39cd: īṣadvyāvṛttavarṇas tu heyopādeyavarjitaḥ
18.40ab: yāṃ saṃvittim avāpnoti śivatattvaṃ tad ucyate
18.40cd: tatra cittaṃ sthirīkurvan sarvajñatvam avāpnuyāt
18.41ab: tatraiva divyacihnāni paśyate ca na saṃśayaḥ
18.41cd: yatraiva kutra cid gātre vikāra upajāyate
18.42ab: saṃkalpapūrvako devi tat tattvaṃ tattvam uttamam
18.42cd: tad abhyasen mahāyogī sarvajñatvajigīṣayā
18.43ab: prāpnoti paramaṃ sthānaṃ bhuktvā siddhiṃ yathepsitām
18.43cd: gandhapuṣpādibhir yogī nityam ātmānam ādarāt
18.44ab: brahmarandhrapradeśe tu pūjayed bhāvato 'pi vā
18.44cd: dravaddravyasamāyogāt snapanaṃ tasya jāyate
18.45ab: gandhapuṣpādigandhasya grahaṇaṃ yajanaṃ matam
18.45cd: ṣaḍrasāsvādanaṃ tasya naivedyāya prakalpate
18.46ab: yam evoccārayed varṇaṃ sa japaḥ parikīrtitaḥ
18.46cd: tatra cetaḥ samādhāya dahyamānasya vastunaḥ
18.47ab: jvālanatas tiṣṭhate yāvat tāvad dhomaḥ kṛto bhavet
18.47cd: yad eva paśyate rūpaṃ tad eva dhyānam iṣyate
18.48ab: prasaṅgād idam uddiṣṭam advaitayajanaṃ mahat
18.48cd: udayārkasamābhāsam ūrdhvadvāre manaḥ sthiram
18.49ab: hṛdi vāḷtat tathā kuryād dvādaśānte 'thavāpnuyāt
18.49cd: tato māsārdhamātreṇa tadrūpam upalabhyate
18.50ab: upalabdhaṃ tad abhyasya sarvajñatvāya kalpate
18.50cd: vastreṇa mukham ācchādya yogī lakṣye niyojayet
18.51ab: nābhikandād adhastāt tu yāvat tattvaṃ śikhāv adhi
18.51cd: sūkṣmatārakasaṃkāśaṃ raśmijvālākarālitam
18.52ab: prāṇaśaktyavasāne tu paśyate rūpam ātmanaḥ
18.52cd: tad evābhyāsato devi vikāsam upagacchati
18.53ab: tanmukhaṃ sarvamantrāṇāṃ sarvatantreṣu paṭhyate
18.53cd: tato 'sya māsamātreṇa kā cit saṃvittir iṣyate
18.54ab: yataḥ sarvaṃ vijānāti hṛdaye saṃvyavasthitaṃ
18.54cd: tāṃ jñātvā kasya cid yogī na samyak pratipādayet
18.55ab: adhyāyāt kathanaṃ kuryān nākāle mṛtyum āpnuyāt
18.55cd: mṛto 'pi śvabhrasaṃghāte krameṇa paripacyate
18.56ab: evaṃ jñātvāḷmahādevi svahitaṃ samupārjayet
18.56cd: śiṣyo 'py anyāyato gṛhṇan narakaṃ pratipadyate
18.57ab: na ca tatkālam āpnoti vacas tv avitathaṃ mama
18.57cd: nyāyena jñānam āsādya paścān na pratipadyate
18.58ab: tadā tasya prakurvīta vijñānāpahṛtiṃ budhaḥ
18.58cd: dhyātvā tam agrataḥ sthāpya svarūpeṇaiva yogavit
18.59ab: ṣaḍvidhaṃ vinyasen mārgaṃ tasya dehe puroktavat
18.59cd: tatas taṃ dīpam ālokya tadaṅguṣṭhāgrataḥ kramāt
18.60ab: nayet tejaḥ samāhṛtya dvādaśāntam ananyadhīḥ
18.60cd: tatas taṃ tatra saṃcintya śivenaikatvam āgatam
18.61ab: tatra dhyāyet tamorūpaṃ tirobhāvanaśīlanam
18.61cd: patantīṃ tena mārgeṇa hy aṅguṣṭhāgrāntam āgatām
18.62ab: sabāhyābhyantaraṃ dhyāyen niviḍāñjanasaprabhām
18.62cd: anena vidhinā tasya mūḍhabuddher durātmanaḥ
18.63ab: vijñānamantravidyādyā na kurvanty upakāritām
18.63cd: cittābhisandhimātreṇa hy adṛṣṭasyāpi jāyate
18.64ab: kathaṃ cid upalabdhasya nityam evāpakāriṇaḥ
18.64cd: athavā sūryabimbābhaṃ dhyātvā vicchedyam agrataḥ
18.65ab: svarbhānurūpayā śaktyā grastaṃ tam anucintayet
18.65cd: aparādhasahasrais tu kopena mahtānvitah
18.66ab: vidhim enaṃ prakurvīta krīḍārthaṃ na tu jātu cit
18.66cd: anena vidhinā bhraṣṭo vijñānād apareṇa ca
18.67ab: na śakyo yojituṃ bhūyo yāvat tenaiva noddhṛtaḥ
18.67cd: karuṇākṛṣṭacittas tu tasya kṛtvā viśodhanam
18.68ab: prāṇāyāmādibhis tīvraiḥ prāyaścittaiṛ vidhiśrutaiḥ
18.68cd: tatas tasya prakurvīta dīkṣāṃ pūrvoktavartmanā
18.69ab: tataḥ sarvam avāpnoti phalaṃ tasmād ananyadhīḥ
18.69cd: evaṃ jñātvā prayatnena gurum āsādayet sudhīḥ
18.70ab: yataḥ saṃtoṣa utpannaḥ śivajñānāmṛtātmakaḥ
18.70cd: na tasyānveṣayed vṛttaṃ śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
18.71ab: sa eva tad vijānāti yuktaṃ vāyuktam eva vā
18.71cd: akāryeṣu yadā saktaḥ prāṇadvayāpahāriṣu
18.72ab: tadā nivāraṇīyo 'sau praṇatena vipaścitā
18.72cd: tenātivāryamāṇo 'pi yady asau na nivartate
18.73ab: tadānyatra kva cid gatvā śivam evānucintayet
18.73cd: eṣa yogavidhiḥ proktaḥ samāsād yogināṃ hitaḥ
18.74ab: nātra śuddhir na cāśuddhir na bhakṣyādivicāraṇam
18.74cd: na dvaitaṃ nāpi cādvaitaṃ liṅgapūjādikaṃ na ca
18.75ab: na cāpi tatparityāgo niṣparigrahatāpi vā
18.75cd: saparigrahatā vāpi jaṭābhasmādisaṃgrahaḥ
18.76ab: tattyāgo na vratādīnāṃ caraṇācaraṇaṃ ca yat
18.76cd: kṣetrādisaṃpraveśaś ca samayādiprapālanam
18.77ab: parasvarūpaliṅgādi nāmagotrādikaṃ ca yat
18.77cd: nāsmin vidhīyate kiṃ cin na cāpi pratiṣidhyate
18.78ab: vihitaṃ sarvam evātra pratiṣiddham athāpi vā
18.78cd: kiṃ tv etad atra deveśi niyamena vidhīyate
18.79ab: tattve cetaḥ sthirīkāryaṃ suprayatnena yoginā
18.79cd: tac ca yasya yathaiva syāt sa tathaiva samācaret
18.80ab: tattve niścalacittas tu bhuñjāno viṣayān api
18.80cd: na saṃspṛśyeta doṣaiḥ sa padmapatram ivāmbhasā
18.81ab: viṣāpahārimantrādisaṃnaddho bhakṣayann api
18.81cd: viṣaṃ na muhyate tena tadvad yogī mahāmatiḥ
18.82ab: ity etat kathitaṃ devi kim anyat paripṛcchasi
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre paramavidyādhikāro 'ṣṭādaśaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>, the eighteenth chapter on the supreme <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge).

body.text: kulacakrādhikāra ekonaviṃśaḥ
body.translated_text: The nineteenth chapter on the <s>kulacakra</s> (circle of clans).

body.text:
19.1ab: athainaṃ paramaṃ yogavidhim ākarṇya śāṅkarī
19.1cd: punar āha prasannāsyā praṇipatya jagadgurum
19.2ab: sādhyatvena śrutā deva bhinnayonis tu mālinī
19.2cd: vidyātrayaṃ savidyāṅgaṃ vidhivac cāvadhāritam
19.3ab: adhunā śrotum icchāmi hy abhinnā sādhyate katham
19.3cd: hitāya sādhakendrāṇāṃ prasādād vaktum arhasi
19.4ab: evam ukto maheśānyā jagatāṃ patir ādarāt
19.4cd: vikasadvadanāmbhojaḥ pratyuvāca vaco 'mṛtam
19.5ab: ārirādhayiṣuḥ śaṃbhuṃ kuloktavidhinā budhaḥ
19.5cd: kulacakraṃ yajed ādau budho dīkṣoktavartmanā
19.6ab: tato japet parām śaktiṃ lakṣam ekam akhaṇḍitam
19.6cd: parābījapuṭāntaḥsthāṃ na drutāṃ na vilambitām
19.7ab: tadvat khaṇḍāṣtakaṃ cāsyā lakṣaṃ lakṣam akhaṇḍitam
19.7cd: japet kuleśvarasyāpi lakṣaṣaṭkam ananyadhīḥ
19.8ab: homayitvā daśāṃśena dravyaṃ pūrvoditaṃ budhaḥ
19.8cd: nityānusmṛtiśīlasya vāksiddhiḥ saṃprajāyate
19.9ab: svakule japayuktasya aśaktasyāpi sādhane
19.9cd: bhavanti kanyasā devi saṃsāre bhogasaṃpadaḥ
19.10ab: śaktas tu sādhayet siddhiṃ madhyamām uttamām api
19.10cd: kṛtasevāvidhiḥ pṛthvīṃ bhramed udbhrāntapantrivat
19.11ab: nagare pañcarātraṃ tu trirātraṃ pattane tu vai
19.11cd: grāme 'pi caikarātraṃ tu sthitvainaṃ vidhim ācaret
19.12ab: yan nāmādyakṣaraṃ yatra varge tat tasya vastunaḥ
19.12cd: kulam uktaṃ vidhānajñair nagarāder na saṃśayaḥ
19.13ab: yā yatra devatā varge vācyatve saṃvyavasthitā
19.13cd: saiva tasya patitvena dhyeyā pūjyā ca sādhakaiḥ
19.14ab: tasya kiṃ cit samāsādya nagarādikam ādarāt
19.14cd: svadigvargasthito bhūtvā cakraṃ yojya nijodaye
19.15ab: avā [lacuna] samekaika udite [lacuna]
19.15cd: devatā māheśvara [lacuna]
19.16ab: krameṇaiva yathā rātrau [lacuna] tathāḷdivā
19.16cd: svadiśi svodaye vargaṃ tam evānusmared budhaḥ
19.17ab: tiṣṭhed anyodayaṃ yāvat tataḥ svāṃ diśam āśrayet
19.17cd: svakulaṃ cintayan yāyāt taddeśakulam eva vā
19.18ab: yāvad anyāṃ diśaṃ mantrī tatas tad anucintayet
19.18cd: evaṃ yāvat svakaṃ sthānaṃ kulacakroktavartmanā
19.19ab: bhramitvā punar āyāti pūrvakālakrameṇa ca
19.19cd: tāvad āgatya deveśi tadeśakulanāyikā
19.20ab: daded bhakṣyādikaṃ kiṃ cid dāpayed vātha kena cit
19.20cd: anena vidhinā yukto guptācāro dṛḍhavrataḥ
19.21ab: yoginīmelakaṃ prāpya ṣaṇmāsenaiva siddhyati
19.21cd: duṣkaro 'yaṃ vidhir devi sattvahīnair narādhamaiḥ
19.22ab: sarvasiddhikaro mukhyaḥ kulaśāstreṣu sarvataḥ
19.22cd: athaikasminn api grāme pattane nagare 'pi vā
19.23ab: tad digbhāgaṃ samāśritya tad evajapate kulam
19.23cd: tribhir abdair anāyāsāt sādhayed uttamaṃ phalam
19.24ab: lokayātrāparityakto grāsamātraparigrahaḥ
19.24cd: athavā nābhicakre tu dhyānacakraṃ kulātmakam
19.25ab: cetasā bhramaṇaṃ kuryāt sarvakālakrameṇa tu
19.25cd: tato 'sya vatsarārdhena dehāntaṃ yoginīkulam
19.26ab: āvirbhavaty asaṃdehāt svavijñānaprakāśakam
19.26cd: tenāvirbhūtamātreṇa yogī yogikule kulī
19.27ab: bhaved api patir devi yogināṃ parameśvari
19.27cd: athavā cintayed devi yakārādikramāṣṭakam
19.28ab: svarūpeṇa prabhākārakarālākulavigraham
19.28cd: tasya madhye kuleśānaṃ svabodhakam anusmaran
19.29ab: sarvam eva ca tatpaścāc cakraṃ dīpaśikhākṛtim
19.29cd: saṃbhūtaṃ cintayed yogī yoginīpadakāṅkṣayā
19.30ab: etasmin vyaktim āpanne piṇḍasthaṃ buddha ucyate
19.30cd: tato 'syākasmikī devi mahāmudropajāyate
19.31ab: śṛṅgāravīrakāruṇyaśokakopādayas tathā
19.31cd: prabuddham etad uddiṣṭaṃ piṇḍastham amarārcite
19.32ab: divasair abhiyuktasya tato 'sya bahubhir dinaiḥ
19.32cd: dharāditattvabhāvānāṃ saṃvittir upajāyate
19.33ab: suprabuddhaṃ tad icchanti piṇḍasthaṃ jñānam uttamam
19.33cd: cakraṃ ca triguṇāṣṭāram athavā tatra cintayet
19.34ab: kādihāntākṣarākrāntaṃ pūrvarūpaṃ sabindukam
19.34cd: tatrāpi pūrvavat sarvaṃ kurvann etad phalaṃ labhet
19.35ab: ādivarṇānvitaṃ vātha ṣoḍaśāram anusmaran
19.35cd: madhyakrameṇa vā yogī pañcamaṃ cumbakādibhiḥ
19.36ab: dvāsaptatisahasrāṇi nāḍīnāṃ nābhicakrake
19.36cd: yataḥ piṇḍatvam āyānti tenāsau piṇḍa ucyate
19.37ab: tatra sthitaṃ tu yaj jñeyaṃ piṇḍasthaṃ tad udāhṛtam
19.37cd: a [lacuna] mala [lacuna] tkeśa [lacuna] kam
19.38ab: vijvaratvam avāpnoti vatsareṇa yadṛcchayā
19.38cd: cakrapañcakam etad dhi pūrvavad dhṛdaye sthitam
19.39ab: padastham iti śaṃsanti caturvhedaṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ
19.39cd: yatrārthāvagatir devi tat sthānaṃpadam ucyante
19.40ab: catuṣkam atra vijñeyaṃ bhedaṃ pañcadaśātmakam
19.40cd: sarvatobhadrasaṃsiddhau sarvatobhadratāṃ vrajet
19.41ab: jarāmaraṇanairguṇyanirmukto yogacintakaḥ
19.41cd: vyāptāv api prasiddhāyāṃ māyādhastattvagocaraḥ
19.42ab: vetti tatpatitulyatvaṃ tadīśatvaṃ ca gacchati
19.42cd: padasthe kiṃ tu candrābhaṃ pradīpābhaṃ na cintayet
19.43ab: etad evāmṛtaughena deham āpūrayat svakam
19.43cd: cintitaṃ mṛtyunāśāya bhavatīti kim adbhutam
19.44ab: upalakṣaṇam etat te candrabimbādyudīritam
19.44cd: yena yenaiva rūpeṇa cintyate parameśvarī
19.45ab: piṇḍasthādiprabhedeṣu tenaiveṣṭaphalapradā
19.45cd: rūpam aiśvaram icchanti śivasyāśivahāriṇaḥ
19.46ab: yadbhrūmadhyasthitaṃ yasmāt tena tatravyavasthitam
19.46cd: pañcakaṃ sūryasaṃkāśaṃ rūpastham abhidhīyate
19.47ab: tatrāpi pūrvavat siddhir īśvarāntapadodbhavā
19.47cd: rūpātītaṃ tu deveśi prāg evoktam anekadhā
19.48ab: ity eṣā kulacakrasya samāsādvyāptir uttamā
19.48cd: kathitā sarvasiddhyarthaṃ siddhayogīśvarīmate
19.49ab: sarvadātha vibhedena pṛthagvarṇavibhedataḥ
19.49cd: vidyādisarvasaṃsiddhyai yogināṃ yogam icchanti
19.50ab: bhūyo 'pi saṃpradāyena varṇabhedaś ca kīrtyate
19.50cd: strīrūpāṃ hṛdi saṃcintya sitavastrādibhūṣitām
19.51ab: nābhicakropaviṣṭām tu candrakoṭisamaprabhām
19.51cd: bījaṃ yat sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ tat tadā syād anāratam
19.52ab: svakīyenaiva vaktreṇa nirgacchat pravicintayet
19.52cd: tārahāralatākāraṃ visphuratkiraṇākulam
19.53ab: varṇais tārakasaṃkāśair ārabdham amitādyuti
19.53cd: māsārdhāc chāstrasaṃghātam udgiraty anivāritam
19.54ab: svapne māsāt samādhisthaḥ ṣaḍbhir māsair yathecchayā
19.54cd: ucchinnāny api śāstrāṇi granthataś cārthato 'pi vā
19.55ab: jānāti vatsarād yogī yadi tanmayatāṃ gataḥ
19.55cd: anuṣaṅgaphalaṃ caitat samāsād upavarṇitam % 19.55
19.56ab: vidyeśvarasamānatvasiddhir anyāś ca siddhayaḥ
19.56cd: prativarnavibhedena yathedānīṃ tathocyate
19.57ab: dhyātavyā yogibhir nityaṃ tattatphalabubhukṣubhiḥ
19.57cd: vinyāsakramayogena trividhenāpi vartmanā
19.58ab: yo yatrāṅge sthito varṇaḥ kulaśaktisamudbhavaḥ
19.58cd: taṃ tatraiva samādhāya svarūpeṇaiva yogavit
body.translated_text:
(19.1) Now, having heard this supreme procedure of yoga, <s>Śāṅkarī</s> (the Goddess),
with a serene face, bowing to the Teacher of the World, spoke again:
(19.2) 'The <s>Mālinī</s> of divided origin has been heard [by me] as that which is to be accomplished, O Lord;
the three <s>vidyā</s>s with their limbs have been duly ascertained.
(19.3) Now I wish to hear: how is the undivided [Mālinī] accomplished?
For the benefit of the chief practitioners (<s>sādhakendra</s>), please be gracious and speak.'
(19.4) Thus addressed by the Great Goddess, the Lord of the Worlds, with respect,
with blossoming lotus-face, replied with nectar-like words:
(19.5) 'The wise one, desiring to propitiate <s>Śambhu</s>, through the rite prescribed by the <s>Kula</s> [tradition],
should first worship the <s>kula-cakra</s> (circle of the clan), the wise one following the path prescribed by initiation.
(19.6) Then one should recite [the mantra of] the Supreme Power (<s>Parā Śakti</s>), one hundred thousand [times] uninterruptedly,
enclosed within the seed-syllable of <s>Parā</s>, neither too fast nor too slow.
(19.7) Likewise, the eight fragments (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) of hers, one hundred thousand each, uninterruptedly;
one should recite [the mantra] of <s>Kuleśvara</s> as well, six hundred thousand [times], with undivided mind.
(19.8) Having offered with a tenth [of the recitations] the substances described before, the wise one —
for one who is habitually engaged in constant remembrance, the power of speech (<s>vāk-siddhi</s>) arises.
(19.9) For one engaged in recitation within his own clan (<s>kula</s>), even if unable in [other] practice,
O Goddess, the wealth of worldly enjoyments arises in the lowest [degree].
(19.10) But one who is able should accomplish the middle or even the highest attainment;
having completed the worship procedure, one should wander the earth like a soaring bird.
(19.11) In a city, for five nights; in a town, for three nights;
and in a village, for one night — having stayed, one should perform this procedure.
(19.12) Whatever is the first syllable of the name [of a place], in whichever phonetic group that [syllable] falls —
that is declared to be the clan (<s>kula</s>) of that entity (city, etc.), by those who know the rites, without doubt.
(19.13) Whichever deity presides in that phonetic group in terms of naming —
that very [deity] should be meditated on and worshipped by practitioners as the lord of that [place].
(19.14) Having obtained something [to eat] from that city or other [settlement], with respect,
having positioned oneself in the phonetic group of one's own direction, one should employ the <s>cakra</s> at one's own rising [time].
(19.15) [lacuna] each one having risen [lacuna]
the deity of <s>Maheśvara</s> [lacuna]
(19.16) In sequence, just as at night [lacuna] so during the day;
in one's own direction, at one's own rising, the wise one should remember that same phonetic group.
(19.17) One should remain until the rising of another [direction]; then one should resort to one's own direction;
contemplating one's own clan, one should travel to the clan of that region, or —
(19.18) until [reaching] another direction, the mantrin should then contemplate that;
thus, until [returning to] one's own place, following the path prescribed by the <s>kula-cakra</s>,
(19.19) having wandered, one returns again, following the previous time-sequence;
by that time, O Goddess, the leading deity of that region's clan arrives
(19.20) and gives some food or other thing, or causes someone to give [it].
Endowed with this procedure, practicing secretly (<s>guptācāra</s>), firm in vow,
(19.21) having attained the meeting of <s>Yoginī</s>s (<s>Yoginī-melaka</s>), one achieves [success] within six months alone.
This procedure is difficult, O Goddess, for those lacking courage, the lowest of men.
(19.22) It is the chief [practice], granting all attainments, in all <s>Kula</s> scriptures.
Or, in even a single village, town, or city,
(19.23) having resorted to the directional portion of that [place], reciting just that clan [mantra],
within three years, without effort, one achieves the supreme fruit.
(19.24) Having renounced worldly pursuits, accepting only a morsel of food —
or in the navel center (<s>nābhi-cakra</s>), [meditating on] the meditation-circle of the clan-nature,
(19.25) one should perform the mental rotation through the entire time-sequence;
then, within half a year, the clan of <s>Yoginī</s>s within the body
(19.26) manifests without doubt, illuminating one's own knowledge;
merely by that manifestation, the yogin, [becoming] a clan-member (<s>kulī</s>) in the clan of yogins,
(19.27) becomes even a lord of yogins, O Goddess, O Supreme Goddess.
Or, O Goddess, one should meditate on the sequence of eight [letters] beginning with YA,
(19.28) in their own forms, with bodies fierce and blazing with radiance;
in the middle of that, remembering the lord of the clan (<s>Kuleśāna</s>) as the awakener of one's own awareness,
(19.29) and then the entire circle, of flame-tip shape,
as having arisen — the yogin should meditate, desiring the station of <s>Yoginī</s>s.
(19.30) When this becomes manifest, [the knowledge] situated in the body (<s>piṇḍastha</s>) is called 'awakened' (<s>buddha</s>);
then, O Goddess, there spontaneously arises in him the great <s>mudrā</s> (<s>mahāmudrā</s>):
(19.31) the erotic (<s>śṛṅgāra</s>), heroic (<s>vīra</s>), compassionate (<s>kāruṇya</s>), grief (<s>śoka</s>), anger (<s>kopa</s>), and others likewise —
when this arises, it is declared 'fully awakened' (<s>prabuddha</s>), [the knowledge] situated in the body, O one honored by the gods.
(19.32) For one who is diligent, after some days,
awareness of the nature of the principles from earth onward arises.
(19.33) This they call 'supremely awakened' (<s>suprabuddha</s>) — the supreme knowledge situated in the body.
Or, one should meditate there on a circle of three-times-eight [= twenty-four] spokes.
(19.34) Filled with the letters from KA to HA in the earlier form, with the <s>bindu</s> (dot);
in that too, performing everything as before, one obtains this fruit.
(19.35) Or, remembering [the circle] accompanied by the initial vowel, with sixteen spokes,
or the yogin [may proceed] by the middle method, the fifth by <s>cumbaka</s> and other [methods].
(19.36) Seventy-two thousand <s>nāḍī</s>s (channels) in the navel center —
since they come to a point (<s>piṇḍa</s>) [there], therefore it is called 'piṇḍa' (body-aggregate).
(19.37) Whatever is to be known as situated there — that is declared as 'piṇḍa-stha' (body-situated).
[lacuna]
(19.38) One attains freedom from fever within a year, spontaneously;
this fivefold circle, as before, situated in the heart,
(19.39) the discerning ones declare as 'pada-stha' (stage-situated), of four varieties.
Where the comprehension of meaning [arises], O Goddess, that place is called 'pada' (stage).
(19.40) Here, a fourfold [classification] should be known, of fifteen-fold division;
upon the accomplishment of the all-auspicious (<s>sarvatobhadra</s>) [stage], one attains all-auspiciousness.
(19.41) Freed from old age, death, and deficiency, the contemplator of yoga,
even in the well-known pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>), [still operating] within the domain of principles below <s>Māyā</s>,
(19.42) knows equality with its lord and attains lordship over it.
But in the stage-situated [practice], one should meditate on a moon-like [light], not a lamp-like [light].
(19.43) This very [light], filling one's own body with a flood of nectar (<s>amṛta</s>),
when meditated upon, serves to destroy death — what wonder is there in this?
(19.44) This moon-disc and other [images] have been described to you as indications;
in whatever form the Supreme Goddess (<s>Parameśvarī</s>) is meditated upon,
(19.45) in the varieties of body-situated and other [stages], by that very [form] she grants the desired fruit.
Those who remove what is inauspicious desire the sovereign form of <s>Śiva</s>.
(19.46) That which is situated between the eyebrows, since [it abides] there —
the fivefold [circle], resembling the sun, is called 'rūpa-stha' (form-situated).
(19.47) There too, accomplishment [proceeds] as before, arising from stages up to the level of <s>Īśvara</s>;
but that which transcends form (<s>rūpātīta</s>), O Goddess, has been described earlier in many ways.
(19.48) This is, in summary, the supreme pervasion (<s>vyāpti</s>) of the <s>kula-cakra</s>,
declared for the accomplishment of all attainments, according to the view of accomplished yogin-lords.
(19.49) Always, with differentiation, through the distinction of individual letters,
for the accomplishment of all <s>vidyā</s>s and everything else, yogins desire this yoga.
(19.50) Moreover, by tradition, the distinction of letters is also declared:
meditating in the heart on a female form, adorned with white garments and other ornaments,
(19.51) seated on the navel center, with radiance equal to ten million moons,
the seed of all scriptures — that should then be [meditated on] unceasingly,
(19.52) as if emerging from one's own mouth, one should meditate;
like a string of star-garlands, shimmering with effulgent rays,
(19.53) composed of letters resembling stars, of immeasurable radiance —
within half a month, one pours forth collections of scriptures, unstoppable.
(19.54) In dreams within a month; in <s>samādhi</s> within six months; at will;
even scriptures that have been lost, in their text and in their meaning,
(19.55) the yogin knows within a year, if he has become one with that.
And this is an incidental fruit, described in summary;
(19.56) the attainment of equality with <s>Vidyeśvara</s> and other attainments —
according to the distinction of each letter, as [will be] now declared:
(19.57) they should always be meditated upon by yogins desiring each respective fruit,
through the threefold path also, by the method of placement (<s>vinyāsa</s>).
(19.58) Whichever letter, born from the power of the clan (<s>kula-śakti</s>), is situated in whichever limb [of the body],
that very [letter], placed there in its own form, by the knower of yoga —'

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare kulacakrādhikara ekonaviṃśaḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>, the nineteenth chapter on the <s>kulacakra</s> (circle of clans) is concluded.

body.text: sarvamantranirṇayo viṃśo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: The twentieth chapter: the determination of all <s>mantras</s> (<s>sarvamantranirṇaya</s>).

body.text:
20.1ab: atha piṇḍādibhedena śāktaṃ vijñānam ucyate
20.1cd: yogināṃ yogasiddhyarthaṃ saṃkṣepān na tu vistarāt
20.2ab: piṇḍaṃ śarīram ity uktaṃ tadvac chaktiśivātmanoḥ
20.2cd: brahmānando balaṃ tejo vīryam ojaś ca kīrtyate
20.3ab: ajñānena niruddhaṃ tad anādyeva sadātmanaḥ
20.3cd: tadāvirbhūtaye sarvam aniruddhaṃ pravartate
20.4ab: tenāvirbhāvyamānaṃ tat pūrvāvasthāṃ parityajat
20.4cd: yāḥ saṃvittīr avāpnoti tā adhastāt prakīrtitāḥ % 4
20.5ab: tad eva padam icchanti sarvārthāvagatir yataḥ
20.5cd: tasmāt saṃjāyate nityaṃ nityam eva śivātmanoḥ
20.6ab: tad eva rūpam ity uktam ātmanaś ca vinaśvaram
20.6cd: rūpātītaṃ tad evāhur yatokṣāviṣayaṃ param
20.7ab: bhāvanāṃ tasya kurvīta namaskṛtya guruṃ budhaḥ
20.7cd: tāvad ālocayed vastu yāvat padam anāmayam
20.8ab: naivaṃ na caivaṃ nāpy evaṃ nāpi caivam api sphuṭam
20.8cd: cetasā yogayuktena yāvat tad idam apy alam
20.9ab: kṛtvā tanmayam ātmānaṃ sarvākṣārthavivarjitam
20.9cd: muhūrtaṃ tiṣṭhate yāvat tāvat kampaḥ prajāyate
20.10ab: bhramaṇodbhavanidrāś ca kiṃ cid ānanda ity api
20.10cd: tatra yatnena saṃdadhyāc cetaḥ paraphalecchayā
20.11ab: tad etad ātmano rūpaṃ śivena prakaṭīkṛtam
20.11cd: yatra tu yac ca vijñeyaṃ śivātmakam api sthitam
20.12ab: tadrūpodbalakatvena sthitim ity avadhārayet
20.12cd: tatsamabhyasato nityaṃ sthūlapiṇḍādy upāśrayāt
20.13ab: caturbhedatvam āyāti bhaktyābhinnam api svataḥ
20.13cd: sthūlapiṇḍe dvidhā proktaṃ bāhyābhyantarabhedataḥ
20.14ab: bhautikaṃ bāhyam icchanti dvitīyaṃ cātivāhikam
20.14cd: tatrādyopāśrayād yogī sasaṃvittir api sphuṭān
20.15ab: bāhyārthān saṃpragṛhṇāti kiṃ cid ādhyātmikān api
20.15cd: dvitīyopāśrayāt tattvabhāvārthān saṃprapadyate
20.16ab: īśate ca svadehāntaḥ pīṭhakṣetrādikaṃ sphuṭam
20.16cd: svarūpālocanād asya yat kiṃ cid upajāyate
20.17ab: tatra cetaḥ sthirīkurvaṃs tad eva sakalaṃ labhet
20.17cd: tena tatra na kurvīta caitad uttamavāñchayā
20.18ab: piṇḍadvayavinirmuktā kiṃ cit tadvāsanānvitā
20.18cd: vijñānakevalāntasthā padam ity abhidhīyate
20.19ab: yata etām anuprāpto vijñānakramayogataḥ
20.19cd: rūpodayātivijñānapadatvaṃ pratipadyate
20.20ab: etac caturvidhaṃ jñeyaṃ caturdhārthapratiśrayāt
20.20cd: sa ca tattvādisaṃvittipūrvas tatpatitāvadhiḥ
20.21ab: padabhāvavinirmuktā kiṃ cit tadanuvarjitā
20.21cd: avasthā svasvarūpasya prakāśakaraṇī yataḥ
20.22ab: tena sārūpyam ity uktā rūpasthaṃ yat tadānvitam
20.22cd: uditādiprabhedena tad apy uktaṃ caturvidhaṃ
20.23ab: jñānodayā ca deveśi mamatvāt tatphalapradam
20.23cd: amunā kramayogena antarā yeṣu saṃdadhat
20.24ab: cetaḥ śuddham avāpnoti rūpātītaṃ paraṃ padam
20.24cd: caturvidhaṃ tad apy uktaṃ saṃvittiphalabhedataḥ
20.25ab: trividhaṃ tat samabhyasya sarvasiddhiphalecchayā
20.25cd: caturthāt tu tanuṃ vyaktvā tatkṣaṇād apavṛjyate
20.26ab: iti piṇḍādi bhedena śivajñānam udāhṛtam
20.26cd: yogābhyāsavidhānena mantravidyāgaṇaṃ śṛṇu
20.27ab: pūrvoktavidhisaṃnaddhaḥ pradeśe pūrvacodite
20.27cd: nābhyādipañcadeśānāṃ parārṇaṃ kvāpi cintayet
20.28ab: svarūpeṇa prabhābhāraprakāśitatanūdaram
20.28cd: dīptibhis tasya tīvrābhir ā brahmabhuvanaṃ tataḥ
20.29ab: evaṃ saṃsmaratas tasya divasaiḥ saptabhiḥ priye
20.29cd: rudraśaktisamāveśaḥ sumahān saṃprajāyate
20.30ab: āviṣṭo bahuvākyāni saṃskṛtādīni jalpati
20.30cd: mahāhāsyaṃ tathā geyaṃ śivaruditam eva ca
20.31ab: karoty āviṣṭacittas tu na tu jānāti kiṃ cana
20.31cd: māsenaivaṃ yadā mukto yatra yatrāvalokayet
20.32ab: tatra tatra diśaḥ sarvā īkṣate kiraṇākulāḥ
20.32cd: yāṃ yām eva diśaṃ ṣaḍbhir māsair yuktas tu vīkṣate
20.33ab: nānākārāṇi rūpāṇi tasyāṃ tasyāṃ prapaśyati
20.33cd: na teṣu saṃdadhec cetaḥ na cābhyāsaṃ parityajet
20.34ab: kurvann etadvidhaṃ yogī bhīrur unmattako bhavet
20.34cd: vīraḥ śaktim punar yāti pramādāt tadgato 'pi san
20.35ab: vatsarād yogasaṃsiddhiṃ prāpnoti manasepsitām
20.35cd: parāparām athaitasyā aparāṃ vā yathecchayā
20.36ab: sadbhāvaṃ mātṛsaṃghasya hṛdayaṃ bhairavasya vā
20.36cd: navātmānam api dhyāyed ratiśekharam eva vā
20.37ab: aghoryādyaṣṭakaṃ vāpi māheśyādikam eva vā
20.37cd: amṛtādiprabhedena rudrān vā śaktayo 'pi vā
20.38ab: sarve tulyabalāḥ proktā rudraśaktisamudbhavāḥ
20.38cd: athavāmṛtapūrṇānāṃ prabhedaḥ procyate paraḥ
20.39ab: prāṇasthaṃ parayākrāntaṃ pratyekam api dīpitam
20.39cd: vidyāṃ prakalpayen mantraṃ prāṇākrāntaṃ parāsanam
20.40ab: dvādaśārasya cakrasya ṣoḍaśārasya vā smaret
20.40cd: aṣṭārasyāthavā devi tasya tredhā śatasya vā
20.41ab: ṣaḍarasyāthavā mantrī yathā sarvaṃ tathā śṛṇu
20.41cd: saṃkṣepād idam ākhyātaṃ sārdhaṃ cakraśatadvayam
20.42ab: etat triguṇātāṃ yāti strīpuṃyāmalabhedataḥ
20.42cd: śāntyādikarmabhedena pratyekaṃ dvādaśātmatām
20.43ab: dakṣaś caṇḍo haraḥ śauṇḍī pramatho bhīmamanmathau
20.43cd: śakuniḥ sumatir nando gopālo 'tha pitāmahaḥ
20.44ab: nandā bhadrā jayā kālī karālī vikṛtānanā
20.44cd: kroṣṭakī bhīmamudrā ca vāyuvegā hayānanā
20.45ab: gambhīrā ghoṣaṇī caiva dvādaśaitāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
20.45cd: āgneyyādicatuṣkoṇā brahmāṇyādyā api priye
20.46ab: siddhir ṛddhis tathā lakṣmīr dīptir mālā śikhā śivā
20.46cd: sumukhī vāmanī nandā harikeśī hayānanā
20.47ab: viśveśī ca sumākhyā ca etā vā dvādaśa kramāt
20.47cd: etāsāṃ vācakā jñeyāḥ svarāḥ ṣaṇṭhavivarjitāḥ
20.48ab: ṣoḍaśāre 'mṛtādyāś ca strīpuṃpāṭhaprabhedataḥ
20.48cd: śrīkaṇṭho 'nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiḥ śarvarīśvaraḥ
20.49ab: argheśo bhārabhūtiś ca sthitiḥ sthāṇur haras tathā
20.49cd: jhiṇṭhīśo bhautikaś caiva sadyojātas tathāparaḥ
20.50ab: anugraheśvaraḥ krūro mahāseno 'tha ṣoḍaśa
20.50cd: siddhir ṛddhir dyutir lakṣmī meghā kāntiḥ svadhā dhṛtiḥ
20.51ab: dīptiḥ puṣṭir matiḥ kīrtiḥ saṃsthitiḥ sugatiḥ smṛtiḥ
20.51cd: suprabhā ṣoḍaśī ceti śrīkaṇṭhādikaśaktayaḥ
20.52ab: ṣoḍaśāre svarā jñeyā vācakatvena sarvataḥ
20.52cd: aghorādyās tathāṣṭāre aghoryādyāś ca devatāḥ
20.53ab: māheśyādyās tathā devi caturviṃśaty ataḥ śṛṇu
20.53cd: nandādikāḥ kramāt sarvā brahmāṇyādyās tathaiva ca
20.54ab: saṃvarto lakulīkaś ca bhṛguḥ śveto bakas tathā
20.54cd: khaḍgī pinākī bhujago navamo balir eva ca
20.55ab: mahākālo dviraṇḍaś ca cchagalāṇḍaḥ śikhī tathā
20.55cd: lohito meṣamīnau ca tridaṇḍyāṣāḍhināmakau
20.56ab: umākānto 'rdhanārīśo dāruko lāṅgalī tathā
20.56cd: tathā someśaśarmāṇau caturvimśaty amī matāḥ
20.57ab: kādibhāntāḥ parijñeyā aṣṭāre yādyam aṣṭakam
20.57cd: makāro bindurūpasthaḥ sarveṣām upari sthitaḥ
20.58ab: juṃkāro 'tha tathā svāhā ṣaḍare ṣaṭ krameṇa tu
20.58cd: baliś ca balinandaś ca daśagrīvo haro hayaḥ
20.59ab: mādhavaś ca mahādevi ṣaṣṭhaḥ saṃparikīrtitaḥ
20.59cd: viśvā viśveśvarī caiva hārādrī vīranāyikā [hāraudrī?]
20.60ab: ambā gurveti yoginyo bījais tair eva ṣaṭ smṛtāḥ
20.60cd: anyonyavalitāḥ sarve svāmyāvaraṇabhedataḥ
20.61ab: akārādikṣakārāntāḥ sarvasiddhiphalapradāḥ
20.61cd: dhyānārādhanayuktānāṃ yogināṃ mantriṇām api
20.62ab: athavā sarvacakrāṇāṃ madhye vidyāṃ yathepsitām
20.62cd: mantraṃ vā pūrvam uddiṣṭaṃ japan dhyāyan prasiddhyati
20.63ab: iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ sarvakāmaphalapradam
body.translated_text:
Now the <s>śākta vijñāna</s> (knowledge pertaining to <s>Śakti</s>) is taught according to the division of <s>piṇḍa</s> (body) and so forth,
for the sake of <s>yogins</s>' attainment of <s>yoga</s>, in brief and not in detail.
<s>Piṇḍa</s> is said to be the body; likewise, of <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s>,
<s>brahmānanda</s> (the bliss of Brahman), <s>bala</s> (strength), <s>tejas</s> (brilliance), <s>vīrya</s> (potency), and <s>ojas</s> (vital energy) are declared.
That [bliss] has been obstructed by ignorance since beginningless time for all embodied beings;
for its manifestation, everything unobstructed proceeds.
As that is being made to manifest by it, abandoning its former state,
whatever realizations it attains — those have been described below.
That alone they desire as <s>pada</s> (the state), since from it arises the comprehension of all purposes;
therefore it arises eternally, ever of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.
That alone is called <s>rūpa</s> (form), and it is perishable with respect to the self;
that which is beyond <s>rūpa</s> they call the supreme, since it is beyond the domain of the senses.
The wise one, having bowed to the <s>guru</s>, should cultivate contemplation of that;
one should contemplate the reality until the state free from affliction [is reached].
"Not thus, nor thus, nor even thus, nor even this clearly" —
with a mind yoked in <s>yoga</s>, until "this too is enough."
Having made oneself absorbed in that, devoid of all sense-objects,
one remains for a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment), and then trembling arises.
Spinning, sudden appearances, drowsiness, and also a slight sense of <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) —
there one should with effort fix the mind, desiring the supreme fruit.
This is the <s>rūpa</s> (form) of the self, made manifest by <s>Śiva</s>;
wherever and whatever is to be known, it abides as having the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.
One should ascertain that it is established by virtue of being the strengthener of that <s>rūpa</s>;
for one who constantly practices that, due to the support of the gross <s>piṇḍa</s> and so forth,
it attains a fourfold division, though intrinsically undivided by devotion.
In the gross <s>piṇḍa</s>, it is said to be twofold, by the distinction of outer and inner:
the outer they consider to be <s>bhautika</s> (elemental), and the second is <s>ātivāhika</s> (the subtle transmigrating body).
From the support of the first, the <s>yogin</s>, though possessing awareness, clearly
apprehends external objects, and also somewhat internal ones.
From the support of the second, one attains the <s>tattva</s>-realities, states, and meanings,
and perceives clearly within one's own body <s>pīṭhas</s> (seats), <s>kṣetras</s> (sacred fields), and the like.
From the contemplation of its own nature, whatever arises,
by steadying the mind there, one would obtain all of that;
therefore one should not engage in this, out of desire for the highest.
Freed from the two <s>piṇḍas</s>, yet somewhat tinged with their impressions,
standing within pure consciousness alone — this is called <s>pada</s> (the state).
Since one who has attained this through the progressive method of <s>vijñāna</s> (knowledge)
attains the state of <s>pada</s> that is beyond the arising of <s>rūpa</s> and transcends <s>vijñāna</s>.
This should be known as fourfold, due to the fourfold support of objects;
and that is preceded by the realization of <s>tattvas</s> and so forth, with its limit being absorption into that.
Freed from the state of <s>pada</s>, yet somewhat connected to it,
since it is the state that illuminates one's own true nature,
therefore it is called <s>sārūpya</s> (identity of form); what is situated in <s>rūpa</s> is connected with that.
By the distinction of <s>udita</s> (arisen) and so forth, that too is said to be fourfold.
The arising of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), O <s>Deveśī</s> (Goddess of Gods), due to identification with it, bestows that fruit.
By this progressive method of <s>yoga</s>, placing the mind in between,
one attains the pure mind — beyond <s>rūpa</s>, the supreme <s>pada</s>.
That too is said to be fourfold, by the distinction of the fruits of realization.
Having practiced that threefold [path], with desire for the fruit of all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments),
from the fourth, having manifested the body, one is instantly liberated.
Thus the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> has been set forth according to the division of <s>piṇḍa</s> and so forth.
Now hear the assemblage of <s>mantra-vidyā</s> (mantra-knowledge) according to the method of <s>yoga</s> practice.
Equipped with the previously stated procedure, in the place previously indicated,
one should contemplate the supreme syllable of the five places beginning with the <s>nābhi</s> (navel), in whichever [place],
in its own form, with belly and body illuminated by the weight of its radiance;
then, by its intense rays of light, up to the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Thus, for one who contemplates in this way, within seven days, O beloved,
a great possession by <s>Rudra-śakti</s> (the power of <s>Rudra</s>) arises.
Possessed, one utters many words in <s>Saṃskṛta</s> and other languages,
great laughter, singing, and also the weeping of <s>Śiva</s> —
one whose mind is possessed performs [these], yet knows nothing at all.
When thus liberated within a month, wherever one gazes,
there in every direction one sees all directions filled with rays of light.
Whatever direction one looks upon, after six months of practice,
many forms of various shapes one perceives in each direction.
One should not fix the mind on them, nor should one abandon the practice.
The <s>yogin</s> who performs this kind [of practice], if timid, would become as if mad;
the hero, however, attains <s>śakti</s> (power); even one who has reached that [state], through carelessness [may fall].
Within a year, one obtains the <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic accomplishment) desired by the mind,
whether supreme-and-non-supreme, or non-supreme, according to one's wish.
One may meditate upon the true nature of the assembly of <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers), or the heart of <s>Bhairava</s>,
or the <s>Navātman</s> (nine-fold self), or indeed <s>Ratiśekhara</s>,
or the group of eight beginning with <s>Aghorā</s>, or that beginning with <s>Māheśī</s>,
or the <s>Rudras</s> by the division of <s>Amṛta</s> and so forth, or the <s>Śaktis</s> —
all are declared to be of equal power, arising from <s>Rudra-śakti</s>.
Alternatively, the supreme division of those filled with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) is now taught.
That which is situated in <s>prāṇa</s> (breath), pervaded by <s>Parā</s> (the Supreme), each one illuminated —
one should fashion it as a <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-mantra); the <s>mantra</s>, pervaded by <s>prāṇa</s>, is the seat of <s>Parā</s>.
One should contemplate the <s>cakra</s> of twelve spokes, or that of sixteen spokes,
or the eight-spoked one, O <s>Devī</s> (Goddess), or its three-hundred [variant],
or the six-spoked one — O <s>mantrin</s> (mantra-practitioner), hear how everything is [arranged].
This is taught in brief: two hundred and fifty <s>cakras</s> in total.
This becomes threefold by the division of female-male <s>yāmala</s> (union);
and twelvefold for each, by the distinction of rites of <s>śānti</s> (pacification) and so forth.
<s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Hara</s>, <s>Śauṇḍī</s>, <s>Pramatha</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, <s>Manmatha</s>,
<s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Gopāla</s>, and <s>Pitāmaha</s> —
<s>Nandā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Karālī</s>, <s>Vikṛtānanā</s>,
<s>Kroṣṭakī</s>, <s>Bhīmamudrā</s>, <s>Vāyuvegā</s>, <s>Hayānanā</s>,
<s>Gambhīrā</s>, and <s>Ghoṣaṇī</s> — these twelve [pairs] are declared.
With four corners beginning from the southeast, [presided over by] <s>Brahmāṇī</s> and the others, O beloved.
<s>Siddhi</s> (Accomplishment), <s>Ṛddhi</s> (Prosperity), <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune), <s>Dīpti</s> (Radiance), <s>Mālā</s> (Garland), <s>Śikhā</s> (Flame), <s>Śivā</s> (Auspicious One),
<s>Sumukhī</s> (Fair-faced), <s>Vāmanī</s> (Dwarf-goddess), <s>Nandā</s> (Joyous), <s>Harikeśī</s> (Golden-haired), <s>Hayānanā</s> (Horse-faced),
<s>Viśveśī</s> (Lady of the Universe) and <s>Sumā</s> — these also are twelve, in order.
The signifiers of these should be known as the vowels, excluding the <s>ṣaṇṭha</s> (sixth [vowel]).
In the sixteen-spoked [<s>cakra</s>], <s>Amṛta</s> and the others, by the division of female and male recitations:
<s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Sūkṣma</s>, <s>Trimūrti</s>, <s>Śarvarīśvara</s>,
<s>Argheśa</s>, <s>Bhārabhūti</s>, <s>Sthiti</s>, <s>Sthāṇu</s>, <s>Hara</s>,
<s>Jhiṇṭhīśa</s>, <s>Bhautika</s>, <s>Sadyojāta</s>, and another,
<s>Anugraheśvara</s>, <s>Krūra</s>, and <s>Mahāsena</s> — thus sixteen.
<s>Siddhi</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Dyuti</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Meghā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>,
<s>Dīpti</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Mati</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, <s>Saṃsthiti</s>, <s>Sugati</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>,
<s>Suprabhā</s> — the sixteenth — these are the <s>Śaktis</s> of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> and the others.
In the sixteen-spoked [<s>cakra</s>], the vowels should be known as the signifiers in every case.
In the eight-spoked [<s>cakra</s>], <s>Aghora</s> and the others, and <s>Aghorī</s> and the other goddesses;
<s>Māheśī</s> and the others likewise, O <s>Devī</s> — now hear the twenty-four:
All the <s>Nandā</s>-group in order, and the <s>Brahmāṇī</s>-group likewise.
<s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Lakulīka</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Baka</s>,
<s>Khaḍgī</s>, <s>Pinākī</s>, <s>Bhujaga</s>, the ninth is <s>Bali</s>,
<s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Dviraṇḍa</s>, <s>Cchagalāṇḍa</s>, <s>Śikhī</s>,
<s>Lohita</s>, <s>Meṣa</s>, <s>Mīna</s>, and those named <s>Tridaṇḍī</s> and <s>Āṣāḍhin</s>,
<s>Umākānta</s>, <s>Ardhanārīśa</s>, <s>Dāruka</s>, <s>Lāṅgalī</s>,
and <s>Someśa</s> and <s>Śarman</s> — these twenty-four are recognized.
They should be known [as designated] by [consonants] from <s>ka</s> to <s>bha</s>; in the eight-spoked [<s>cakra</s>], the group of eight beginning with <s>ya</s>;
<s>makāra</s>, stationed in the form of <s>bindu</s> (point), is situated above all of them.
The syllable <s>juṃ</s> and then <s>svāhā</s> — in the six-spoked [<s>cakra</s>], six in order:
<s>Bali</s>, <s>Balinanda</s>, <s>Daśagrīva</s> (Ten-necked [<s>Rāvaṇa</s>]), <s>Hara</s>, <s>Haya</s>,
and <s>Mādhava</s>, O <s>Mahādevī</s> (Great Goddess) — the sixth is proclaimed.
<s>Viśvā</s>, <s>Viśveśvarī</s>, <s>Hārādrī</s>, <s>Vīranāyikā</s>,
<s>Ambā</s>, and <s>Gurvī</s> — these <s>yoginīs</s> are likewise six, with those very seed-syllables.
All [<s>cakras</s>], intertwined with one another, by the distinction of lord and retinue,
beginning with <s>akāra</s> and ending with <s>kṣakāra</s>, bestow the fruit of all <s>siddhis</s> (accomplishments),
for <s>yogins</s> and <s>mantrins</s> (mantra-practitioners) who are engaged in <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) and worship.
Alternatively, in the center of all the <s>cakras</s>, whichever <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge-mantra) is desired,
or the <s>mantra</s> previously taught — by reciting and meditating [on it], one achieves success.
Thus it has been taught in brief, bestowing the fruit of all desires.

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare sarvamantranirṇayo nāma viṃśatitamo 'dhikāraḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, called 'The Determination of All <s>Mantras</s>' (<s>Sarvamantranirṇaya</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s> [Tantra].

body.text: candrākṛṣṭyadhikāra ekaviṃśatitamaḥ
body.translated_text: The Twenty-first Chapter: On the Attraction of the Moon (<s>Candrākṛṣṭyadhikāra</s>)

body.text:
21.1ab: athātaḥ paramaṃ guhyaṃ śivajñānāmṛtottamam
21.1cd: vyādhimṛtyuvināśāya yoginām upavarṇyate
21.2ab: ṣoḍaśāre khage cakre candrakalpitakarṇike
21.2cd: svarūpeṇa parāṃ tatra sravantīm amṛtaṃ smaret
21.3ab: pūrvanyāsena saṃnaddhaḥ kṣaṇam ekaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
21.3cd: tatas tu rasanāṃ nītvā lambake viniyojayat
21.4ab: sravantam amṛtaṃ divyaṃ candrabimbasitaṃ smaret
21.4cd: mukham āpūryate tasya kiṃ cil lavaṇavāriṇā
21.5ab: lohagandhena tac cātra na pibet kiṃ tu nikṣipet
21.5cd: evaṃ samabhyaset tāvad yāvat tat svādu jāyate
21.6ab: jarāvyādhivinirmukto jāyate tatpibaṃs tataḥ
21.6cd: ṣaḍbhir māsair anāyāsād vatsarān mṛtyujid bhavet
21.7ab: tatra svāduni saṃjāte tadāprabhṛti tatragam
21.7cd: yad eva cintayed dravyaṃ tenāsyāpūryate mukham
21.8ab: rudhiraṃ madiraṃ vātha vasāṃ vā kṣīram eva vā
21.8cd: ghṛtatailādikaṃ vātha dravaddravyam ananyadhīḥ
21.9ab: athānyaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi saṃkrāntividhim uttamam
21.9cd: mṛte jīvaccharīre tu praviśed yogavidyayā
21.10ab: nivātastho jitaprāṇo jitāsanavidhikramaḥ
21.10cd: kurvīta vāyunāveśam arkatūle śanaiḥ śanaiḥ
21.11ab: svādākṛṣṭividhiṃ yāvad guḍe nimbe ca kārayet
21.11cd: śrīkhaṇḍaguḍakarpūrais tataḥ kṛtvākṛtim śubhām
21.12ab: praguṇām aguṇa[lacuna]nyaṅgeṣu saṃdadhat
21.12cd: nyāsaṃ kṛtvāpi tatrāpi vedhaṃ kuryāc chanaiḥ śanaiḥ
21.13ab: nirodhaṃ tatra kurvīta ghaṭṭanaṃ tadanantaram
21.13cd: ghaṭṭanaṃ nāma vijñeyam aṅgapratyaṅgacālanam
21.14ab: evam abhyasatas tasya yogayuktasya yoginaḥ
21.14cd: calate pratimā sā tu dhāvate cāpi saṃmukhī
21.15ab: punas tāṃ prerayet tāvad yāvat svasthānam āgatam
21.15cd: patitāṃ cālayed bhūya uttānāṃ pārśvataḥ sthitaḥ
21.16ab: evaṃ sarvātmanas tāvad yāvat svavaśatāṃ gatām
21.16cd: tataḥ prabhṛty asau yogī praviśed yatra rocate
21.17ab: mṛte jīvaccharīre vā saṃkrāntyākrāntibhedataḥ
21.17cd: prakṣipya jalavac chaktijālam sarvāṅgasaṃdhiṣu
21.18ab: pratyaṅgam aṅgatas tasya śaktiṃ tenākramed budhaḥ
21.18cd: svakīyaṃ rakṣayed deham ākrāntāv anyathā tyajet
21.19ab: bahūny api śarīrāṇi dṛḍhalakṣyo yadāḷbhavet
21.19cd: tadāḷgṛhṇāty asaṃdehaṃ yugapat saṃtyajann api
21.20ab: athāparaṃ pravakṣyāmi sadyaḥpratyayakārakam
21.20cd: samādhānāmṛtaṃ divyaṃ yogināṃ mṛtyunāśanam
21.21ab: candrākṛṣṭikaraṃ nāma māsād vāḷyogabhogadam
21.21cd: śuklapakṣe dvitīyāyāṃ meṣasthe tigmarociṣi
21.22ab: snātaḥ śucir nirāhāraḥ kṛtapūjāvidhir budhaḥ
21.22cd: nyasec candre kalājālaṃ parayā samadhiṣṭhitam
21.23ab: sarvabādhāparityakte pradeśe saṃsthito budhaḥ
21.23cd: ekacittaḥ praśāntātmā śivasadbhāvabhāvitaḥ
21.24ab: tāvad ālokayec candraṃ yāvad astam upāgatam
21.24cd: tato bhuñjīta dugdhena candradhyānasamanvitaḥ
21.25ab: evaṃ dine dine kuryād yāvat pañcadaśī bhavet
21.25cd: śeṣāṃ rātriṃ svaped dhyāyaṃśḷcandrabimbagatāṃ parām
21.26ab: paurṇamāsīṃ tathā yogī ardharātra upasthitaḥ
21.26cd: jane niḥśabdatāṃ yāte prasupte sarvajantubhiḥ
21.27ab: candrakoṭikaraprakhyāṃ tārahāravibhūṣaṇām
21.27cd: sitāmbaraparīdhānāṃ sitacandanacarcitām
21.28ab: mauktikābharaṇopetaṃ surūpāṃ navayauvanām
21.28cd: āpyāyanakarīṃ devīṃ samantād amṛtasravām
21.29ab: rājīvāsanasaṃsthāṃ ca yoganidrām avasthitām
21.29cd: candrabimbe parāṃ devīṃ īkṣate nātra saṃśayaḥ
21.30ab: tatas tāṃ cetasā vyāpya tāvad ākarṣayet sudhīḥ
21.30cd: yāvan mukhāgram āyātā tatra kuryāt sthiraṃ manaḥ
21.31ab: tataḥ prasārya vadanaṃ dhyānāsaktena cetasā
21.31cd: nigiret tāṃ samākṛṣya bhūyo hṛdi vicintayet
21.32ab: tayā praviṣṭayā dehaṃ yogī duḥkhavivarjitaḥ
21.32cd: śaktitulyabalo bhūtvā jīved ācandratārakam
21.33ab: eko 'py anekadhātmānaṃ saṃvibhajya nijecchayā
21.33cd: trailokyaṃ yaugapadyena bhunakti vaśatāṃ gatam
21.34ab: āsādya vipulān bhogān pralaye samupasthite
21.34cd: param abhyeti nirvāṇaṃ duṣprāpam akṛtātmanām
21.35ab: athavā tan na śaknoti gagane paricintitum
21.35cd: pratibimbe tathā dhyāyed udakādiṣu pūrvavat
21.36ab: tat pītvāḷmanasā śeṣāṃ svaped rātrim anusmaran
21.36cd: pūrvoktaṃ samavāpnoti ṣaḍbhir māsair akhaṇḍitam
body.translated_text:
(21.1) Now, the supreme secret — the highest nectar of the knowledge of <s>Śiva</s> — is described for <s>yogins</s>, for the destruction of disease and death.
(21.2) In the celestial wheel (<s>cakra</s>) with sixteen spokes and a pericarp fashioned as the moon, one should contemplate the supreme [<s>Śakti</s>] in her own form, streaming <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) there.
(21.3) The discerning one, girded with the previous <s>nyāsa</s> (placement), [should remain] for one moment. Then, having extended the tongue, he should fix it at the <s>lambaka</s> (uvula).
(21.4) One should contemplate the divine <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) streaming forth, white as the disc of the moon. His mouth fills with a slightly salty liquid.
(21.5) Having a metallic smell, one should not drink that but rather spit it out. One should practice thus until it becomes sweet.
(21.6) By drinking that, one becomes freed from old age and disease. Within six months, effortlessly, [and] within a year, one becomes a conqueror of death.
(21.7) When sweetness has arisen there, from that time onward, whatever substance one contemplates [as flowing] there fills the mouth:
(21.8) Blood, wine, fat, milk, ghee, oil, or any other liquid substance — [contemplated] with undivided attention.
(21.9) Now I shall describe another [practice] — the supreme method of <s>saṃkrānti</s> (transference). One should enter a dead or living body through the knowledge of <s>yoga</s>.
(21.10) Stationed in a windless place, having conquered the breath and mastered the sequence of <s>āsana</s> (posture) procedures, one should gradually effect the entry of breath into a cotton-ball of the <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) plant.
(21.11) One should perform the practice of self-attraction with jaggery and neem. Then, having fashioned an auspicious figure with sandalwood, jaggery, and camphor,
(21.12) Well-shaped, without [lacuna] ...placing upon the other limbs, having performed <s>nyāsa</s> there too, one should gradually effect the piercing (<s>vedha</s>).
(21.13) One should perform the restraint (<s>nirodha</s>) there, and then the agitation (<s>ghaṭṭana</s>). The agitation should be known as the moving of limbs and sub-limbs.
(21.14) Thus, for the <s>yogin</s> joined with <s>yoga</s> who practices in this way, that image moves and even runs forward.
(21.15) He should impel it again until it has returned to its own place. Having fallen, he should again move it while standing at its side, [making it rise from] a supine [position].
(21.16) Thus [he should practice] with the entirety [of the figure], until it has come under his control. From that point onward, that <s>yogin</s> may enter wherever he pleases.
(21.17) Into a dead or living body — through the distinction of transference (<s>saṃkrānti</s>) and invasion (<s>ākrānti</s>), casting the net of <s>Śakti</s> like water into all the joints of the limbs.
(21.18) The wise one should [pervade] each sub-limb through that [body's] limbs with [his own] <s>Śakti</s>. In the case of invasion, he should protect his own body; otherwise he should abandon it.
(21.19) When [the <s>yogin</s>] of firm aim has become [accomplished], he seizes even many bodies without doubt, even while simultaneously abandoning [the previous one].
(21.20) Now I shall describe another [practice] — the divine nectar of absorption (<s>samādhāna</s>), which produces immediate evidence, destroys death for <s>yogins</s>,
(21.21) Called 'Moon-attraction' (<s>Candrākṛṣṭi</s>), which within a month bestows the enjoyments of <s>yoga</s>. On the second day of the bright fortnight, when the sun is in <s>Meṣa</s> (Aries),
(21.22) The wise one, having bathed, pure, fasting, having performed the worship ritual, should place the net of <s>kalās</s> (lunar digits) on the moon, established with the <s>Parā</s> [<s>vidyā</s>].
(21.23) The wise one, stationed in a place free from all disturbances, single-minded, with a tranquil self, absorbed in the true nature of <s>Śiva</s>,
(21.24) Should gaze at the moon until it sets. Then he should eat with milk, accompanied by meditation on the moon.
(21.25) Thus he should do day after day until the fifteenth [i.e., the full moon]. The remaining night, he should sleep meditating on the supreme [<s>Śakti</s>] stationed in the moon-disc.
(21.26) On the full-moon night, the <s>yogin</s>, standing at midnight, when the people have fallen silent and all creatures are asleep,
(21.27) [Beholds her] — resembling [the radiance of] ten million moon-beams, adorned with a necklace of stars, clad in white garments, anointed with white sandalwood paste,
(21.28) Adorned with pearl ornaments, beautiful, in the bloom of youth, the <s>Devī</s> who causes nourishment, streaming nectar from all sides,
(21.29) Seated on a lotus, established in yogic sleep (<s>yoganidrā</s>) — he sees the supreme <s>Devī</s> in the moon-disc; there is no doubt about this.
(21.30) Then, having pervaded her with the mind, the wise one should attract [her] until she comes to the tip of the mouth. There he should make the mind steady.
(21.31) Then, opening the mouth wide, with the mind absorbed in meditation, he should swallow her having drawn [her in], and again contemplate [her] in the heart.
(21.32) When she has entered the body, the <s>yogin</s>, freed from suffering, having become equal in power to <s>Śakti</s>, lives as long as the moon and stars [endure].
(21.33) Even alone, having divided himself into many by his own will, he simultaneously enjoys the three worlds which have come under his control.
(21.34) Having attained vast enjoyments, when dissolution arrives, he reaches the supreme <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is difficult to attain for those who have not cultivated the self.
(21.35) Or, if he cannot contemplate [the moon] in the sky, he should meditate upon [its] reflection in water and the like, as before.
(21.36) Having drunk that mentally, he should sleep the remaining night, remembering [the practice]. Within six months, uninterrupted, he attains what was previously described.

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre candrākṛṣṭyadhikāra ekaviṃśatitamaḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-first chapter, on the attraction of the Moon (<s>Candrākṛṣṭi</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: sūryākṛṣṭyadhikāro dvāviṃśatitamaḥ
body.translated_text: The Twenty-Second Chapter: On the Attraction of the Sun (<s>Sūryākṛṣṭyādhikāra</s>)

body.text:
22.1ab: athānyaṃ paramaṃ guhyaṃ kathayāmi tava priye
22.1cd: yan na kasya cid ākhyātaṃ yogāmṛtam anuttamam
22.2ab: sūryākṛṣṭikaraṃ nāma yogināṃ yogasiddhidam
22.2cd: samyaṅ māsacatuṣkeṇa dināṣṭābhyadhikena tu
22.3ab: praharsyāṣṭamo bhāgo nāḍikety abhidhīyate
22.3cd: tatpādakramavṛddhyā tu prativāsaram abhyaset
22.4ab: udayāstamayaṃ yāvad yatra sūryaḥ pradṛśyate
22.4cd: pradeśe tatra vijane sarvabādhāvivarjite
22.5ab: ahorātroṣito yogī makarasthe divākare
22.5cd: śucir bhūtvā kṛtanyāsaḥ kṛtaśītapratikriyaḥ
22.6ab: bhānubimbe nyasec cakram aṣṭaṣaḍdvādaśārakam
22.6cd: śivaśaktighanopetaṃ bhairavāṣṭakasaṃyutam
22.7ab: varṣādiṛtusaṃyuktaṃ māsairṛkṣādibhir yutam
22.7cd: aṣṭāraṃ cintayed bimbe śeṣaṃ raśmiṣu cintayet
22.8ab: tatra cittaṃ samādhāya proktakālaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
22.8cd: animīlitanetras tu bhānubimbaṃ nirīkṣayet
22.9ab: tataḥ kāle vyatikrānte sunimīlitalocanaḥ
22.9cd: praviśed andhakārāntarbhuvanaṃ nirupadravam
22.10ab: tatronmīlitanetras tu bimbākāraṃ prapaśyati
22.10cd: saṃdhāya tatra caitanyaṃ tiṣṭhed yāvan na paśyati
22.11ab: naṣṭe 'pi cetasā śeṣaṃ tiṣṭhet kālam anusmaran
22.11cd: evaṃ māsena deveśi sthiraṃ tad upajāyate
22.12ab: māsadvayena sarvatra prekṣate nātra saṃśayaḥ
22.12cd: tribhiḥ samīkṣate sarvaṃ ravibimbasamākulam
22.13ab: proktakālāvasānena vṛṣasthe tigmarociṣi
22.13cd: prekṣate sūryabimbāntaḥ sacakraṃ parameśvaram
22.14ab: upalabdhaṃ samākṛṣya mukhāgre sthiratāṃ nayet
22.14cd: āpīya pūrvavat paścād vṛttiṃ niścalatāṃ nayet
22.15ab: tatra tena sahātmānam ekīkṛtya muhūrtakam
22.15cd: yāvat tiṣṭhati deveśi tāvat saṃtyajati kṣitim
22.16ab: paśyato janavṛndasya yāti sūryena caikataḥ
22.16cd: anena vidhinā devi siddhayogīśvareśvaraḥ
22.17ab: śivādyavaniparyantaṃ na kva cit pratihanyate
22.17cd: bhuktvā tu vipulān bhogān niṣkale līyate pare
22.18ab: tad etat khecarīcakraṃ yatra khecaratāṃ vrajet
22.18cd: siddhayogeśvarītantre sarahasyam udāhṛtam
22.19ab: athavā cakrarūpeṇa sabāhyābhyantaraṃ svakam
22.19cd: dehaṃ cintayataḥ pūrvaṃ phalaṃ syān niścitātmanaḥ
22.20ab: uccaran phādināntāṃ vā dhvanijyotirmaruddyutām
22.20cd: viśrāmya mastake cittaṃ kṣaṇam ekaṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ
22.21ab: triśūlena prayogena sadyas tyajati medinīm
22.21cd: evaṃ samabhyasan māsāc cakravad bhramati kṣitau
22.22ab: muhūrtaṃ spṛśate bhūmiṃ muhūrtāc ca nabhastalam
22.22cd: śivārāvādi kurute valanāsphoṭanāni ca
22.23ab: mudrābandhādikaṃ vātha bhāṣā vāḷvakty anekadhā
22.23cd: ṣaṇmāsān medinīṃ tyaktvā samādhistho dṛḍhendriyaḥ
22.24ab: tiṣṭhate hastamātreṇa gagane yogacintakaḥ
22.24cd: paśyate yoginīvṛndam anekākāralakṣaṇam
22.25ab: saṃvatsareṇa yuktātmā tatsamānaḥ prajāyate
22.25cd: paśyatām eva lokānāṃ tejobhir bhāsayan diśaḥ
22.26ab: yāty utkṛṣya mahīpṛṣṭhāt khecarīṇāṃ patir bhavet
22.26cd: mudrā khageśvarī nāma kathitā yoginīmate
22.27ab: jāgaritvātha vā yogī tryahorātram atandritaḥ
22.27cd: caturthe 'hni niśārambhe pūjayitvā maheśvaram
22.28ab: tato 'ndhakāre bahule kṛtarakṣāvidhir budhaḥ
22.28cd: bhruvor madhye samādhāya kṣaṇaṃ cetaḥ prapaśyati
22.29ab: tejo rūpapratīkāśaṃ paryaṅkāsanam āsthitaḥ
22.29cd: prayogaṃ tv eva satataṃ yogayuktaḥ samabhyaset
22.30ab: paśyate māsamatreṇa gṛhāntarvastu yat sthitam
22.30cd: dvābhyāṃ bahiḥ sthitaṃ sarvaṃ tribhiḥ pattanasaṃsthitam
22.31ab: caturbhir viṣayāntaḥsthaṃ pañcabhir maṇḍalāvadhi
22.31cd: ṣaḍbhir māsair mahāyogī cchidraṃ paśyati medinīm
22.32ab: sarvajñatvam avāpnoti vatsarān nātra saṃśayaḥ
22.32cd: yoginīsiddhasaṅghasya sadbhāvavyāptisaṃsthitam
22.33ab: paśyate yogayuktātmā tatsamānaś ca jāyate
22.33cd: anenaiva vidhānena svastikāsanasaṃsthitaḥ
22.34ab: binduṃ nānāvidhaṃ tyaktvā śuddharūpam anusmaret
22.34cd: tenāpi sarvaṃ purvoktaṃ vyāpnoti phalam uttamam
body.translated_text:
(22.1) Now I shall tell you another supreme secret, O beloved, which has not been revealed to anyone — the unsurpassed nectar of <s>yoga</s>,
(22.2) called <s>Sūryākṛṣṭi</s> (Solar Attraction), which grants <s>yoga-siddhi</s> (yogic perfection) to <s>yogin</s>s. In exactly four months and eight additional days,
(22.3) an eighth part of a <s>praharsa</s> is called a <s>nāḍikā</s>. One should practice daily with a gradual increase by a quarter [of that duration].
(22.4) In a place where the sun is visible from rising to setting, in a solitary spot free from all disturbances —
(22.5) the <s>yogin</s>, having fasted for a full day and night, when the sun is in <s>Makara</s> (Capricorn), having become ritually pure, having performed <s>nyāsa</s> (placement), having made preparations against the cold,
(22.6) should place upon the sun's disk a <s>cakra</s> (wheel) with eight, six, and twelve spokes, endowed with dense [configurations of] <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s>, accompanied by the eight <s>Bhairava</s>s,
(22.7) conjoined with the seasons beginning with the rains, furnished with months, lunar mansions, and the like. One should contemplate the eight-spoked [wheel] on the disk; the rest upon the rays.
(22.8) Having fixed the mind there for the prescribed duration, the discerning one, with unblinking eyes, should gaze upon the sun's disk.
(22.9) Then, when the [prescribed] time has elapsed, with eyes well-closed, one should enter the inner world of darkness, free from disturbance.
(22.10) There, with eyes opened, one sees the form of the disk. Having fixed consciousness there, one should remain until one no longer sees it.
(22.11) Even when it has vanished, one should remain for the remaining time, contemplating it mentally. Thus, O Queen of the Gods, within a month that [image] becomes stable.
(22.12) In two months, one sees [it] everywhere — there is no doubt about this. In three, one perceives everything pervaded by the sun's disk.
(22.13) At the conclusion of the prescribed period, when the fierce-rayed [sun] is in <s>Vṛṣa</s> (Taurus), one sees <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) together with the <s>cakra</s> within the sun's disk.
(22.14) Having perceived and drawn [him] forth, one should establish [him] in stability before one's face. Having absorbed [him] as before, one should then bring the mental activity to stillness.
(22.15) There, having unified oneself with him for a <s>muhūrta</s> (moment) — O Queen of the Gods, as long as one remains [thus], for that long one abandons the earth.
(22.16) In the sight of the assembled people, one goes together with the sun. By this method, O Goddess, [one becomes] a perfected lord of lords of <s>yogin</s>s,
(22.17) from <s>Śiva</s> down to the earth, unobstructed anywhere. Having enjoyed abundant pleasures, one dissolves in the supreme partless [reality].
(22.18) That is the <s>Khecarī Cakra</s> (Wheel of Sky-travel), by which one attains the state of sky-movement; it was declared with its secrets in the <s>Siddhayogeśvarī Tantra</s>.
(22.19) Alternatively, for one with a determined mind who first contemplates one's own body, both externally and internally, in the form of a <s>cakra</s>, the [previously stated] fruit would arise.
(22.20) Or, uttering [sounds] ending with 'pha' and the like — the radiance of sound, light, and wind — the discerning one, resting the mind at the crown of the head for a single instant,
(22.21) by the application of the trident, instantly leaves the earth. Thus, through such practice, in a month one revolves like a wheel upon the earth.
(22.22) For a moment one touches the ground, for a moment the sky. One makes the sound of <s>Śiva</s>'s roar and performs circling and clapping,
(22.23) or binding of <s>mudrā</s>s and the like, or speaks language in many forms. In six months, having abandoned the earth, established in <s>samādhi</s>, with firm senses,
(22.24) the <s>yoga</s>-practitioner stands at the height of a hand's measure in the sky. He sees the host of <s>yoginī</s>s, characterized by manifold forms.
(22.25) In a year, the united soul becomes equal to them. In the very sight of the people, illuminating the directions with radiances,
(22.26) having risen from the earth's surface, one becomes the lord of the <s>Khecarī</s>s (sky-travelers). The <s>mudrā</s> called <s>Khageśvarī</s> (Queen of the Sky) has been described in the <s>Yoginī</s> doctrine.
(22.27) Or the <s>yogin</s>, having stayed awake without laziness for three days and nights, on the fourth night, at the beginning of the night, having worshipped <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord),
(22.28) then in dense darkness, the wise one, having performed the protection ritual, fixing the mind between the eyebrows for a moment, perceives
(22.29) a radiance resembling [various] forms, seated in <s>paryaṅkāsana</s> (the couch-posture). One should continuously practice this application, united with <s>yoga</s>.
(22.30) Within a month one sees what is situated inside the house; in two [months], everything situated outside; in three, what is within the town;
(22.31) in four, what is within the realm; in five, up to the [entire] region; in six months, the great <s>yogin</s> sees through the earth.
(22.32) One attains omniscience within a year — there is no doubt. Established in the true nature of the pervasion of the assembly of <s>yoginī</s>s and <s>siddha</s>s,
(22.33) the <s>yoga</s>-united soul perceives [it] and becomes equal to them. By this very method, established in <s>svastikāsana</s> (the auspicious posture),
(22.34) having abandoned the manifold <s>bindu</s> (point of light), one should contemplate the pure form. By that too, one attains all the previously stated supreme fruit.

body.text:
iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre sūryākṛṣṭyadhikāra dvāviṃśatitamaḥ
samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-second chapter, on the attraction of the sun (<s>Sūryākṛṣṭyādhikāra</s>), in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: trayoviṃśatitamo 'dhikāraḥ
body.translated_text: The twenty-third chapter.

body.text:
23.1ab: athātaḥ paramaṃ guhyaṃ kathayāmi tavādhunā
23.1cd: sadyopalabdhijanakaṃ yogināṃ yogasiddhaye
23.2ab: pūrvanyāsena saṃnaddhaś cittaṃ śrotre niveśayet
23.2cd: nivāte svalpavāte vā bāhyaśabdavivarjite
23.3ab: tatas tatra śṛṇoty eṣa yogī dhvanim anāvṛtam
23.3cd: suviśuddhasya kāṃsyasya hatasyeha muhur muhuḥ
23.4ab: yam ākrṇya mahādevi puṇyapāpaiḥ pramucyate
23.4cd: tatra saṃdhāya caitanyaṃ ṣaṇmāsād yogavittamaḥ
23.5ab: rutaṃ pakṣigaṇasyāpi prasphuṭaṃ vetty ayatnataḥ
23.5cd: dūrāc chravaṇavijñānaṃ vatsareṇāsya jāyate
23.6ab: sarvakāmaphalāvāptir vatsaratritayena ca
23.6cd: siddhyatīti kim āścāryam anāyāsena siddhyati
23.7ab: athavā grahaṇe māsi kṛtvā sūryaṃ tu pṛṣṭhataḥ
23.7cd: pūrvanyāsena saṃnaddhaḥ kiṃ cid bhittimadāśritaḥ
23.8ab: lakṣayed ātmanaś chāyāṃ mastakordhvam anāhatam
23.8cd: dhūmavartiviniṣkrāntāṃ tadgatenāntarātmanā
23.9ab: yāti tanmayatāṃ tatra yogayukto yathā yathā
23.9cd: tathā tathāsya mahatī sāḷvittir upajāyate
23.10ab: tatas tatra mahātejah sphuratkiraṇasaṃnibham
23.10cd: paśyate yatra dṛṣṭe 'pi sarvapāpakṣayo bhavet
23.11ab: tad asyābhyāsato māsāt sarvatra pravisarpati
23.11cd: jvālāmālākulākārā diśaḥ sarvāḥ prapaśyati
23.12ab: ṣaṇmāsam abhyasan yogī sarvajñatvam avāpnuyāt
23.12cd: abdaṃ divyatanur bhūtvā śivavan modate ciram
23.13ab: atha jātyaḥ pravakṣyante sapūrvāsanaśāśvatāḥ
23.13cd: hrīṃ kṣlāṃ kṣvīṃ vaṃ tathāḷkṣaṃ ca pañcakasya yathākramam
23.14ab: haṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ tathā vaṃ ca pañcakasyāparasya ca
23.14cd: ṛṃ .Rṃ ḷṃ .Lṃ tathā oṃ auṃ haḥ aṃ ākarṇikāvadhau
23.15ab: kesareṣu bhakārāntā haṃ hāṃ hiṃ hīṃ ca huṃ tathā
23.15cd: hūṃ heṃ haiṃ ca daleṣv evaṃ svasaṃjñābhiś ca śaktayaḥ
23.16ab: maṇḍalatritaye śeṣaṃ sūkṣmaṃ pretasya kalpayet
23.16cd: jrakāraṃ śūlaśṛṅgāṇām ity etat parikīrtitam
23.17ab: anuktāsanayogeṣu sarvatraiva prakalpayet
23.17cd: namaḥ svāhā tathā vauṣaṭ huṃ vaṣaṭ phaṭ ca
jātayaḥ\testim{\svacchandatantra 1.72}
23.18ab: prāyaścitteṣu sarveṣu japen mālām akhaṇḍitām
23.18cd: bhinnāṃ vāpy athavābhinnām atikramabalābalam
23.19ab: sakṛjjapāt samārabhya yāval lakṣatrayaṃ priye
23.19cd: prāṇavṛttinirodhena tataḥ parataraṃ kva cit
23.20ab: sadā bhramaṇaśīlānāṃ pīṭhakṣetrādikaṃ bahiḥ
23.20cd: prayogaṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi sukhasiddhiphalapradam
23.21ab: nāsākrāntaṃ mahāprāṇaṃ daṇḍarūpaṃ sabindukam
23.21cd: tadvad guhyaṃ ca kurvīta vidyeyaṃ dvyakṣarā matā
23.22ab: asyāḥ pūrvoktavidhinā kṛtasevaḥ prasannadhīḥ
23.22cd: pīṭhādikaṃ bhramet siddhyai nānyathā vīravandite
23.23ab: tat pradeśaṃ samāsādya mantrair ātmānam ādarāt
23.23cd: vidyayā veṣtayet sthānaṃ raktasūtrasamānayā
23.24ab: bahudhānanyacittas tu sabāhyābhyantaraṃ budhaḥ
23.24cd: tatas tatra kva cit kṣetre yoginyo bhīmavikramāḥ
23.25ab: samāgatya prayacchanti saṃpradāyaṃ svakaṃ svakam
23.25cd: yenāsau labdhamātreṇa saṃpradāyena suvrate
23.26ab: tatsamānabalo bhūtvā bhuṅkte bhogān yathepsitān
23.26cd: athavā kṛtasevas tu lakṣam ekaṃ japet sudhīḥ
23.27ab: tarpayitvā daśāṃśena kṣudrakarmasu yojayet
23.27cd: tatroccāritamātreyaṃ viṣakṣayakarī bhavet
23.28ab: cakravabhramamāṇaiṣā yonau raktāṃ vicintayet
23.28cd: gamāgamakramād vāpi vinda[lacuna]vāritā
23.29ab: tatrasthaś cāśu saṃghātavighātākuñcanena tu
23.29cd: kṣaṇād ananyacittas tu kṣobhayed urvaśīm api
23.30ab: kṛtasevavidhir vātha lakṣatrayajapena tu
23.30cd: mahatīṃ śriyam ādhatte padmaśrīphalatarpitā
23.31ab: ṣaḍutthāsanasaṃsthānā sādhitāpy uktavartmanā
23.31cd: sarvasiddhikarī devī mantriṇām upajāyate
23.32ab: śūlapadmavidhiṃ muktvā navātmādyaṃ ca saptakam
23.32cd: ṣaḍuttham āsanaṃ dadyāt sarvacakravidhau budhaḥ
23.33ab: kudrā ca mahatī yojyā hṛdbījenopacārakam
23.33cd: athānyat saṃpravakṣyāmi svapnajñānam anuttamam
23.34ab: hṛccakre tanmayo bhūtvā rātrau rātrāv ananyadhīḥ
23.34cd: māsād ūrdhvaṃ mahādevi svapne yat kiṃcid īkṣate
23.35ab: tat tathyaṃ jāyate tasya dhyānayuktasya yoginaḥ
23.35cd: tatraiva yadi kālasya niyamena rato bhavet
23.36ab: tadā prathamayāme tu vatsareṇa śubhāśubham
23.36cd: ṣaṭtrimāsena kramaśo dvitīyādiṣv anukramāt
23.37ab: aruṇodayavelāyāṃ daśāhena phalaṃ labhet
23.37cd: saṃkalpapūrvake 'py evaṃ pareṣām ātmano 'pi vā
23.38ab: kva cit kārye samutpanne suptajñānam upākramet
23.38cd: ity etat kathitaṃ devi siddhayogīśvarīmatam
23.39ab: nātaḥ parataraṃ jñānaṃ śivādyavanigocare
23.39cd: ya evaṃ tattvato veda sa śivo nātra saṃśayaḥ
23.40ab: tasya pādarajaḥ mūrdhni dhṛtaṃ pāpapraśāntaye
23.40cd: etac chrutvā mahādevī paraṃ saṃtoṣam āgatā
23.41ab: evaṃ kṣamāpayām āsa praṇipatya punaḥ punaḥ
23.41cd: iti vaḥ sarvam ākhyātaṃ mālinīvijayottaram
23.42ab: mamaitat kathitaṃ devyā yogāmṛtam anuttamam
23.42cd: bhavadbhir api nākhyeyam aśiṣyāṇām idaṃ mahat
23.43ab: na cāpi paraśiṣyāṇām aparīkṣya prayatnataḥ
23.43cd: sarvathaitat samākhyātaṃ yogābhyāsaratātmanām
23.44ab: prayātānāṃ vinītānāṃ śivaikārpitacetasām
23.44cd: kārtikeyāt samāsādya jñānāmṛtam idaṃ mahat
23.45ab: manayo yogam abhyasya parāṃ siddhim upāgatāḥ
body.translated_text:
(23.1) Now I shall tell you the supreme secret, which generates immediate realization, for the <s>yoga</s>-attainment of <s>yogins</s>.
(23.2) Girded with the previous <s>nyāsa</s>, one should fix the mind on the ear, in a windless or slightly breezy place, free from external sounds.
(23.3) Then the <s>yogin</s> hears there an unobstructed sound — as of a very pure bronze vessel being struck again and again.
(23.4) Hearing which, O <s>Mahādevī</s>, one is released from merit and sin. Fixing consciousness there, within six months the foremost knower of <s>yoga</s>
(23.5) Effortlessly understands clearly even the cries of flocks of birds. The knowledge of distant hearing arises for him within a year.
(23.6) The attainment of all desired fruits is accomplished within three years — what is surprising? It is accomplished effortlessly.
(23.7) Alternatively, in the month of an eclipse, having placed the sun behind oneself, girded with the previous <s>nyāsa</s>, leaning slightly against a wall,
(23.8) One should observe one's own shadow — [the part] above the crown, unstruck, emerging like a column of smoke — with the inner self absorbed in that.
(23.9) To the extent the one joined with <s>yoga</s> attains identity with that, to that extent great accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>) arises for him.
(23.10) Then one perceives there a great radiance resembling flashing rays — upon seeing which, the destruction of all sins occurs.
(23.11) Through practice, within a month, that spreads everywhere. Teeming with garlands of flames, he perceives all directions.
(23.12) Practicing for six months, the <s>yogin</s> would attain omniscience. Within a year, having become of divine body, he rejoices for long like <s>Śiva</s>.
(23.13) Now the seed-syllables (<s>jāti</s>) will be declared, eternal, with their prior seats: '<s>hrīṃ</s>', '<s>kṣlāṃ</s>', '<s>kṣvīṃ</s>', '<s>vaṃ</s>', and '<s>kṣaṃ</s>' — for the [first] group of five in order;
(23.14) '<s>haṃ</s>', '<s>yaṃ</s>', '<s>raṃ</s>', '<s>laṃ</s>', and '<s>vaṃ</s>' — for the other group of five. '<s>ṛṃ</s>', '<s>ṝṃ</s>', '<s>ḷṃ</s>', '<s>ḹṃ</s>', and '<s>oṃ</s>', '<s>auṃ</s>', '<s>haḥ</s>', '<s>aṃ</s>' — up to the pericarp.
(23.15) On the filaments, [those] ending with '<s>bha</s>'; '<s>haṃ</s>', '<s>hāṃ</s>', '<s>hiṃ</s>', '<s>hīṃ</s>', '<s>huṃ</s>', '<s>hūṃ</s>', '<s>heṃ</s>', '<s>haiṃ</s>' — on the petals. Thus the <s>Śaktis</s> with their own designations.
(23.16) On the three <s>maṇḍalas</s>, one should assign the remainder, subtle, of the <s>preta</s> (corpse). The '<s>jra</s>'-syllable for the trident-horns — thus it has been declared.
(23.17) In rituals where the seat is not specified, one should assign [them] everywhere. '<s>namaḥ</s>', '<s>svāhā</s>', '<s>vauṣaṭ</s>', '<s>huṃ</s>', '<s>vaṣaṭ</s>', '<s>phaṭ</s>' — these are the seed-types.
(23.18) In all expiatory rites, one should recite an unbroken rosary — whether broken or unbroken [in sequence], whether the transgression is strong or weak.
(23.19) Beginning from a single recitation up to three <s>lakṣas</s> (hundred-thousands), O beloved, with the restraint of the breath-activities — beyond that, somewhere [higher].
(23.20) For those who are always given to wandering, I shall declare the external practice of <s>pīṭhas</s> (sacred seats), <s>kṣetras</s> (fields), and the like, which bestows the fruit of easily attained <s>siddhi</s>.
(23.21) The great breath (<s>mahāprāṇa</s>) occupying the nose, of rod-form, with <s>bindu</s>; likewise the secret [syllable] should be made — this <s>vidyā</s> is considered to have two syllables.
(23.22) Having performed worship by the previously described method, with a pleased mind, one should wander to <s>pīṭhas</s> and the like for <s>siddhi</s>; not otherwise, O one praised by heroes.
(23.23) Having reached that place, one should carefully wrap oneself with <s>mantras</s> and encircle the place with the <s>vidyā</s>, like a red cord.
(23.24) The wise one, with mind on nothing else, both externally and internally — then at some <s>kṣetra</s> (sacred field), <s>Yoginīs</s> of fearsome prowess,
(23.25) Having assembled, bestow their respective <s>saṃpradāya</s> (lineage-transmission). By which, upon merely receiving that <s>saṃpradāya</s>, O devoted one,
(23.26) Having become equal in power to them, he enjoys desired pleasures. Or, the wise one who has performed worship should recite one <s>lakṣa</s> (hundred-thousand),
(23.27) Having satiated [the deity] with a tenth [portion], he should employ [the <s>mantra</s>] in minor rituals. Therein, by merely uttering it, it becomes the destroyer of poison.
(23.28) [This <s>vidyā</s>], as it whirls like a wheel — one should contemplate [her] red in the <s>yoni</s>. Through the sequence of coming and going, or [lacuna]...
(23.29) Stationed there, through quick contraction and expansion of the mass, in an instant, with undivided mind, one can agitate even <s>Urvaśī</s>.
(23.30) Or, one who has performed the worship method, through recitation of three <s>lakṣas</s>, acquires great prosperity — satiated with the fruit of the <s>Padmaśrī</s> (lotus-glory).
(23.31) The <s>Devī</s>, established in the six-arising seat (<s>ṣaḍutthāsana</s>), accomplished by the described path, becomes the giver of all <s>siddhis</s> for the <s>mantra</s>-practitioners.
(23.32) Excluding the trident-lotus method and the first group of seven of the nine-formed [<s>mantra</s>], the wise one should give the six-arising seat in all <s>cakra</s>-rituals.
(23.33) The minor and great [<s>mudrās</s>] should be employed, with the heart-seed as the ritual offering. Now I shall describe another [practice] — the unsurpassed knowledge of dreams (<s>svapnajñāna</s>).
(23.34) Having become absorbed in the heart-<s>cakra</s>, night after night with undivided mind — after a month, O <s>Mahādevī</s>, whatever the <s>yogin</s> sees in dream,
(23.35) That becomes true for him, the <s>yogin</s> engaged in meditation. If there he becomes devoted to a fixed schedule of time,
(23.36) Then in the first watch [of the night], [what is dreamt] manifests within a year — for good or ill; within six [months], three months, in sequence for the second [watch] and onward.
(23.37) At the time of dawn's reddening, one obtains the fruit within ten days. Even with a deliberate intention, for others or for oneself —
(23.38) When some matter has arisen, one should undertake the knowledge of sleep. This, O <s>Devī</s>, has been declared according to the doctrine of <s>Siddhayogeśvarī</s>.
(23.39) There is no knowledge higher than this in the domain [extending] from <s>Śiva</s> to the earth. He who truly knows this is <s>Śiva</s> — there is no doubt about this.
(23.40) The dust of his feet, borne on the head, [is sufficient] for the pacification of sins. Hearing this, the great goddess (<s>Mahādevī</s>) attained supreme satisfaction.
(23.41) She thus asked forgiveness, bowing again and again. 'Thus has all been told to you — the <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>.
(23.42) This supreme nectar of <s>yoga</s>, told to me by the <s>Devī</s> — by you also it should not be told to non-disciples; this is great.
(23.43) Nor to the disciples of others, without careful examination. In every way, this has been declared for those whose selves are devoted to the practice of <s>yoga</s>,
(23.44) Who have set forth [on the path], who are disciplined, whose minds are offered to <s>Śiva</s> alone. Having received this great nectar of knowledge from <s>Kārtikeya</s>,
(23.45) The sages, having practiced <s>yoga</s>, attained the supreme <s>siddhi</s>.

body.text: iti śrīmālinīvijayottare tantre trayoviṃśatitamo 'dhikāraḥ samāptaḥ
body.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter in the glorious <s>Mālinīvijayottara Tantra</s>.

body.text: samāptaṃ cedaṃ mālinīvijayottaraṃ nāma mahātantram
body.translated_text: Thus ends the great tantra called <s>Mālinīvijayottara</s>.
